# Audit over-subscribed dialog is incorrect

## Problem statement

The herdr selection list's over-quota confirmation dialog (shown when the operator presses `a-a` to fire `/skill:audit` while the audit tier is at/over its host cap) reports a stale/inflated audit count. The worklist header counter was recently fixed to exclude dead (pane-gone) audit entries, but the dialog still uses the old admission-count rule, so the two surfaces disagree: the header says `audit 0/1` while the dialog claims `1 running, max 1`.

## Users

- **Herdr operators** firing audits by hand from the selection list. Example user story: "As an operator who just saw `[budget: implement 0/2 · audit 0/1]` in the header, when I press `a-a` to run an audit I expect the over-quota dialog — if shown at all — to quote the same audit count I just saw, not a phantom `1 running`."

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/host-budget-dialog.ts` — renders the over-quota dialog from `HostBudgetPromptRequest { kind, live, max }`; quotes `live` verbatim ("(`<live>` running, max `<max>`) — over by `<overshoot>`").
- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.interactive.ts` — `prepareInteractiveAgentDispatch` decides whether to prompt. It computes the tier count via `readTierCount`, which for the audit tier calls `freshCount` (marker-compatible: every fresh entry counts, no live-pane requirement).
- `packages/herdr/src/host-budget-status.ts` — `readHostBudgetStatus` (the header counter) uses `reduceAuditDisplayCounts`, a **pane-aware** display rule: a fresh confirmed entry whose `paneId` is absent from the trusted live pane list is excluded. This was introduced by WL-0MW8D4UQH002TWJV ("Audit budget header must not count a dead (pane-gone) audit entry", completed 2026-11-09).
- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.ts` — `freshCount`/`reduceMarkerCounts` (admission, marker-compatible) vs `reduceAuditDisplayCounts` (display, pane-aware) are intentionally different reductions.
- Combined consequence: the **display** count and the **admission** count can differ by exactly the dead-pane entries. The interactive dialog quotes the admission count, so it reads higher than the header.

## Desired change

Make the interactive over-quota dialog quote the same audit count the operator sees in the worklist header — i.e. the pane-aware **display** count — while leaving the dispatcher's admission semantics (fail-closed, marker-compatible) untouched.

Concretely: in `prepareInteractiveAgentDispatch`'s count path for the audit tier, use the pane-aware display reduction (the same one `readHostBudgetStatus` uses) to populate both the prompt decision and the `live` value quoted in `HostBudgetPromptRequest`, so:

- a fresh audit entry whose `paneId` is absent from the trusted live pane list is **not** counted in the dialog (and does not, on its own, trigger the prompt);
- an unconfirmed audit entry (no `paneId`, reserve→spawn window) is still counted;
- an audit entry whose pane is live is still counted;
- stale entries stay excluded;
- the implement tier's counting is unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The over-quota dialog's audit `live` count matches the worklist header's audit display count for the same ledger and live pane list (the two surfaces no longer disagree).
- A dead (confirmed) audit entry whose `paneId` is absent from the live pane list does not trigger the over-quota dialog and is not quoted in it; an unconfirmed fresh audit entry and a fresh audit entry with a live pane still trigger/count; stale entries are excluded.
- Dispatcher admission (`readAuditBudgetState`/`freshCount`/`admitHostDispatch`) is unchanged: fail-closed, marker-compatible counting, 2 h staleness release.
- The implement-tier dialog behaviour and counts are unchanged.
- Unit tests pin the dialog-vs-header agreement (dead / live / unconfirmed / stale audit entries) and the unchanged admission behaviour.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` documents that the interactive dialog's audit display count follows the header's pane-aware rule.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Operators see the same audit count in the over-quota dialog as in the worklist header, so firing `a-a` no longer pops a phantom "1 running" prompt when no audit is actually in flight.

## Constraints

- Must not change dispatcher admission semantics (fail-closed; `maxAudit` governs dispatcher ticks).
- Must keep the display read read-only (no ledger reap/rewrite from the dialog path).
- The live pane list must remain a trusted machine-wide read; an absent list must fall back to the freshness rule (as the header does) rather than inventing a zero.
- No new dependencies; reuse existing pure reductions.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.interactive.ts` — switch the audit-tier count fed to the prompt from `freshCount` to the pane-aware display reduction (needs the live pane list it already reads).
- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.interactive.test.ts` — pin dialog-vs-header agreement and the dead/live/unconfirmed/stale cases.
- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.ts` — reuse `reduceAuditDisplayCounts` (no new reduction unless a shared helper is warranted).
- `packages/herdr/src/host-budget-status.ts` — reference for the pane-aware display rule.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — document the dialog's display-count rule.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk (default):** Only the dialog's audit count is changed. The dispatcher's admission logic, the header counter, and the implement tier are untouched. If further alignment is desired (e.g. implement tier using display count in the dialog), file as a separate item.
- **Count divergence trade-off:** After the change, the dialog may not prompt at all when only dead-pane entries are present — the operator can fire an audit that admission (marker-compatible) would refuse. This is intentional: the operator sees the count they saw in the header and is making an informed choice.
- **Assumption:** The live pane list is already read in `prepareInteractiveAgentDispatch` and is available for the audit-tier display count. No new subprocess calls needed.

## Related work

- **WL-0MW8D4UQH002TWJV** — "Audit budget header must not count a dead (pane-gone) audit entry" (completed): introduced the pane-aware display rule for the header. This item makes the dialog follow the same rule.
- **WL-0MW5KC8J300942EA** — parent of the above (sweep/release backstop for closed panes).
- **WL-0MVXY0Z93002HKCZ** — the F4 interactive over-quota dialog (origin of the count source this item corrects).
- **WL-0MVXWQFGV000D2AB** — parent host dispatch budget work.
- **WL-0MTOFAUCH00217XL** – "Fix: derive header count from WorkItem rows only" (completed): header-count derivation (worklist list rows, not budget). Related header-count correctness precedent.
- **WL-0MW454I1X009Q17E** – "Group counts are incorrect" (open): another selection-list count surface. Related display-count correctness.
- **WL-0MTOFANL6004M3TY** – "Test: header count excludes heading rows" (completed): test precedent for header-count correctness.

### Related docs

- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — documents the host dispatch budget, the F4 dialog and the pane-aware audit display rule.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — herdr plugin overview.
- `CLI.md` — CLI reference.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interactive questions were required — the bug and its root cause were fully resolvable from the repository and worklog.

- Q: "Which surfaces disagree, and why?" — Answer (agent, from repo research): The worklist header (`readHostBudgetStatus` → `reduceAuditDisplayCounts`, pane-aware) excludes dead confirmed audit entries; the interactive over-quota dialog (`prepareInteractiveAgentDispatch` → `readTierCount` → `freshCount`, marker-compatible) counts them. Source: `packages/herdr/src/host-budget-status.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.interactive.ts`.
- Q: "Was the header fixed recently by another item?" — Answer (agent, from worklog): Yes — WL-0MW8D4UQH002TWJV ("Audit budget header must not count a dead (pane-gone) audit entry", completed 2026-11-09) introduced the pane-aware display rule for the header only, deliberately leaving admission unchanged. Source: `wl show WL-0MW8D4UQH002TWJV`.
- Q: "Should the dialog follow the display rule or the admission rule?" — Answer (agent, from intent): The dialog is a user-facing prompt that must agree with the header the operator just read; it should quote the pane-aware display count. Admission remains marker-compatible and fail-closed. Source: item description + WL-0MW8D4UQH002TWJV design note.
- Q: "Is the live pane list already available in the interactive path?" — Answer (agent, from repo research): Yes — `prepareInteractiveAgentDispatch` already reads the machine-wide live pane list (`readLivePanes`) for the implement tier, so no new subprocess read is needed. Source: `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.interactive.ts`.

# ruff EXE001 in maintenance_routines.py:1 — producer decision: false positive or fix needed

## Problem statement

Ruff flags EXE001 on `skill/maintenance-routines/scripts/maintenance_routines.py:1` because the file has a shebang (`#!/usr/bin/env python3`) but lacks the executable bit. The audit system flagged this as a candidate false positive — the claim is that the file is a library/utility module, not a CLI entry point, so the executable bit is intentionally absent.

## Users

- **Developer / CI** — expects consistent lint signals; false positives erode trust in the audit system.
- **Operator** — needs to know whether to accept this as a waiver or fix the inconsistency.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Producer decision recorded.** The operator decides one of: (a) accept as a false positive via an audit waiver, (b) fix by adding the executable bit, or (c) fix by removing the shebang.
2. **Action taken.** The chosen action is implemented — either `audit_waiver.py add` is run, or the file is edited and committed.
3. **No residual finding.** Running `ruff check --select EXE001` on the file produces no errors.

## Impact

The operator gets a clear signal on whether this lint finding represents a real code quality issue or a spurious alert, preserving trust in the audit system's signals.

## Constraints

- The file is used both as an importable module (`import maintenance_routines as mr`) and as a directly runnable script (`python3 scripts/maintenance_routines.py`) by the herdr downtime worker and integration tests.
- Any change must not break the herdr scheduled-prompt dispatch path.

## Existing state

- `skill/maintenance-routines/scripts/maintenance_routines.py` has `#!/usr/bin/env python3` on line 1, permissions `-rw-rw-r--` (no executable bit).
- Ruff confirms: `EXE001 Shebang is present but file is not executable`.
- The file is invoked as `python3 scripts/maintenance_routines.py` in tests (via `subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(SCRIPT)])`), not as a direct executable (`./maintenance_routines.py`).
- A `# <!-- REFACTOR-WL-0MW34DD93007Q2U3` comment block already exists in the file noting this exact issue.
- Parent work item `WL-0MVIDWJ090090J3Q` (Maintenance routines skill) is completed.

## Analysis

This is **not a false positive**. Ruff is correctly identifying an inconsistency: a shebang implies the file can be executed directly (e.g. `./maintenance_routines.py`), but without the executable bit, it cannot. The file *is* runnable — just only via `python3 script.py`. The argument that "it's a library, not a CLI" does not make the finding invalid; the shebang is functional (used by the herdr downtime worker and tests), so the executable bit should be present for consistency.

## Producer decision required

The operator must choose between two fix options:

- **Option A (recommended): Add the executable bit.** `chmod +x skill/maintenance-routines/scripts/maintenance_routines.py`. Simple, preserves the shebang, consistent with how the file is actually used.
- **Option B: Remove the shebang.** If the file should never be run directly, remove `#!/usr/bin/env python3` from line 1.
- **Option C: Accept as a false positive (waiver).** Use `audit_waiver.py add` to suppress the finding. Not recommended — the finding is legitimate.

## Key Files

- `skill/maintenance-routines/scripts/maintenance_routines.py` — the flagged file (add `+x` or remove shebang).
- `skill/maintenance-routines/tests/test_maintenance_routines.py` — confirms the file is imported as a module.
- `tests/skill/maintenance-routines/test_maintenance_routines_cli.py` — confirms the file is run via `python3`, not directly.

## Related work

- **WL-0MVIDWJ090090J3Q** — Maintenance routines skill: create/maintain daily scheduled sessions (completed). Parent of the file in question.
- **WL-0MW8RRGY700736KZ** — ruff EXE001 in test_maintenance_routines.py:1 (open). Same root cause: shebang without executable bit.
- **WL-0MW8RRHLS006RDDQ** — ruff EXE001 in test_maintenance_routines_cli.py:1 (open). Same root cause.
- **WL-0MW34DD93007Q2U3** — Refactor: Formatting (open). Created during the parent work item's implementation.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — chmod might affect deployment.** If the deployment process strips the executable bit, the change is lost. Mitigation: verify deployment preserves file permissions.
- **Assumption — the file is intended to be directly runnable.** The presence of the shebang suggests it is; the herdr downtime worker invokes it.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q: Is this a false positive?** — Answer: No. Ruff is correctly flagging an inconsistency (shebang without executable bit). The file is used as a runnable script, so the executable bit should be present. Producer must choose: add executable bit (recommended), remove shebang, or accept the waiver (not recommended).

# Herdr audit admission queries the proxy-managed budget

## Goal

Make the herdr downtime dispatcher's **audit-tier** capacity decision read the proxy's audit availability (the shared local resource) instead of asserting a per-host `budget.json` cap, so two ContextHub instances on different servers cannot independently believe they are under cap.

**discovered-from:** LP-0MW0KZUJP0019SLS (llm worklog — "Serialise audits at the shared local resource, not per host or per repo").

**Producer direction (2026-11-09):** `budget.json` is managed per ContextHub host and ContextHub may run on several servers; it is better for the proxy to manage the budget and for ContextHub to query it than for each host to enforce its own cap.

## Impact

Audit dispatch on any ContextHub host now takes its capacity decision from the proxy's shared audit budget, so a second audit is refused while one is already running anywhere — no more two concurrent audits on the one GPU — and an unreachable proxy stops audits with a named `audit-budget-unknown` reason instead of silently admitting a duplicate.

## Problem

`getActiveAudit` (`packages/herdr/src/index.ts`) reads the machine-scoped ledger (`host-dispatch-budget.ts`, `dispatch-budget.json`) and the per-host `budget.json` cap (`maxAudit`, default 1). The host-wide guard serialises audits **on one machine**, but the resource they contend for is the single local `llama-server` GPU shared by every host. Two ContextHub hosts enforcing one audit each produce two concurrent audits on one GPU — the 2026-11-03 incident. The `machine-coordination.ts` comment already records the limitation: "single-machine v1 only; multi-machine (flock/NFS) is out of scope".

The proxy already owns the audit budget and the live audit-lease registry (sibling llm item LP-0MW95FYMH006XYNK), and every ContextHub host already talks to the proxy for model traffic.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Audit admission is proxy-derived.** For the audit tier only, `getActiveAudit` / the dispatch gate queries the proxy's audit-availability endpoint (cap, live leases, available) and does not assert the local `budget.json` cap. The implement tier keeps its existing per-host budget (out of scope).
- **AC2 — One vocabulary, no disagreement.** The refusal reason token and log vocabulary match the proxy's (`audit-budget-saturated`), so a dispatcher admission and a proxy refusal cannot disagree; a divergence is logged with both sides' evidence.
- **AC3 — Fail-safe on an unreachable proxy.** If the proxy cannot be reached, audit dispatch fails **closed** with a named reason (e.g. `audit-budget-unknown`) and logs the proxy error; the legacy local-ledger path remains behind an explicit flag for one release.
- **AC4 — Single-machine limitation documented.** The `~/.herdr/downtime` single-machine constraint and the chosen cross-machine mechanism (proxy-owned budget + query) are documented, superseding the "out of scope" note in `machine-coordination.ts`.
- **AC5 — Testing/validation.** Tests cover: availability read maps to the dispatch decision; second audit refused with agreement between dispatcher and proxy; unreachable proxy fails closed; stale-lease reclamation reflected; the implement tier is unchanged. Changed-scope tests pass via `/skill:test`.
- **AC6 — Docs.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (gate table, machine-dir files, reason tokens, operator runbook), and `budget.json` is no longer documented as audit-authoritative.
- **AC7 — Full suite.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (enforced at the dev-push gate).

## Out of scope

- The proxy-side budget/lease implementation (sibling llm item LP-0MW95FYMH006XYNK).
- Implement-tier budget changes.
- Multi-machine herdr leader election beyond audit admission.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `getActiveAudit` audit-tier query path.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch.ts` / `downtime-worker.dispatch-filter.ts` — audit gate consumption of the proxy availability.
- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.ts` — legacy path behind a flag; availability vocabulary.
- `packages/herdr/src/machine-coordination.ts` — single-machine limitation note update.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` / `host-dispatch-budget.acceptance.test.ts` — new acceptance tests.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** every ContextHub host can reach the proxy (it already proxies model traffic).
- **Risk:** a proxy outage now blocks audit dispatch (fail-closed). Mitigation: a named reason, operator-visible log, and the one-release legacy flag.
- **Scope-creep guard:** extra opportunities become linked work items, not scope.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MWAM5N75004ROSW** – Host-wide release barrier: pause new implement/audit dispatch on every root while a release runs (open)
- **WL-0MW50EHZ6007QBPB** – Generalise host dispatch budget to any work item type (absent = unlimited, audit-only over-hold) (open)
- **WL-0MW9VQ08W000SN63** – Implement budget header under-counts: panes running >2h are dropped from the counter (open)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, ac5 (+185 more)
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, ac5 (+180 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: ac2, already, audit, audits, available (+143 more)

## Plan (2026-11-10)

Feature decomposition — test-first, vertical slices, dependency order. Each child is one end-to-end deliverable (code, tests, docs where relevant).

| # | Child | Type | Depends on | Parent ACs traced |
|---|-------|------|-----------|-------------------|
| 1 | Pin the proxy audit-availability wire contract (WL-0MWAMS1PW000O3OS) | task (tests + types) | — | AC1, AC5 |
| 2 | Add the fail-closed audit-availability client (WL-0MWAMSCOP003R837) | feature | 1 | AC1, AC5 |
| 3 | Audit gate reads proxy availability (WL-0MWAMSDNW000SL0E) | feature | 2 | AC1, AC2, AC3 |
| 4 | Admission choke point, divergence log and legacy flag (WL-0MWAMSK9H005BOHD) | feature | 3 | AC2, AC3, AC5 |
| 5 | Cross-host audit serialisation acceptance proof (WL-0MWAMSLBL001JNKO) | task (tests) | 4 | AC5, AC7 |
| 6 | Document proxy-owned audit budget and vocabulary (WL-0MWAMSMBH001BE5G) | docs | 4 | AC4, AC6 |

### Design decisions

- **Contract first, client second.** The proxy-side endpoint does not exist yet (sibling LP-0MW95FYMH006XYNK; probed 2026-11-10 — the live proxy serves `/llama/local/status` and `/llama/local/reserve` only). Children 1–2 therefore pin the wire contract with one path constant (`AUDIT_AVAILABILITY_PATH`, provisional `/llama/local/audit/status`) and alias-tolerant parsing, exactly as the reserve-handshake slice C1 did (`downtime-worker.local-reservation.ts`). Children 1–2 change no behaviour.
- **Fail-closed default.** `endpoint-absent` (404), `unreachable` (timeout/network/HTTP error) and `unparsable` all map to `reason: 'audit-budget-unknown'` — audit dispatch stops with a named reason rather than silently trusting a per-host cap.
- **One-release escape hatch.** `HERDR_AUDIT_LOCAL_BUDGET=1` restores the pre-change `budget.json` `maxAudit` + local-ledger decision for the audit tier; env var (not a persisted setting) so it is revertible without a file edit and matches the `HERDR_HOST_MAX_*` precedent.
- **Local ledger becomes observability-only for the audit tier.** Audit entries are still reserved/confirmed/released so the worklist header, the interactive over-quota dialog, the closed-pane sweep and the release paths keep working, but an audit entry can never cause a refusal. A proxy/local disagreement is logged with both sides' evidence (AC2).
- **The per-worklog dispatch-marker single-flight check is retained unchanged** — it answers a different question ("has this worklog already been audited this window?"), not the capacity question.
- **The implement tier is untouched.**
- **Rollout sequencing.** Children 3–4 flip the default behaviour, so they must not be released before the proxy side lands; until then operators run with `HERDR_AUDIT_LOCAL_BUDGET=1`. This is the concrete consequence of the cross-store blocking relationship recorded above (`wl dep` cannot span worklog stores).
- **AC7 is gate-enforced**, not a feature: the dev-push gate runs the full suite; child 5 owns confirming the gate is green for the branch before this item reaches `in_review`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "The proxy's audit-availability endpoint does not exist yet (probe 2026-11-10: `/openapi.json` lists only `/llama/local/status` and `/llama/local/reserve`; `/llama/local/audit*` answers 404). How should planning proceed?" — Answer (plan, adopted assumption; this is a downtime-dispatched run with no interactive producer): pin the client-side contract first (types + tolerant parser + one path constant) and implement the client against it, following the reserve-handshake C1 precedent. Options considered: (a) pin contract now **[chosen]**; (b) block this item until the sibling proxy item ships; (c) wait for the proxy owner to name the path. Evidence: `curl` probe of `http://192.168.0.199:8000/openapi.json`; `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.local-reservation.ts` header. **OPEN QUESTION (directed to the proxy owner on LP-0MW95FYMH006XYNK): please confirm the final path and field names for the audit-availability read; the client keeps the path a one-line change and reads documented aliases for the fields.**
- Q: "On HTTP 404 (a proxy that predates the endpoint), should audit dispatch fall back to the local ledger automatically or fail closed?" — Answer (plan): fail closed with `audit-budget-unknown`; the legacy path is reachable only through the explicit flag, per this item's AC3. Rationale: a silent auto-fallback recreates the 2026-11-03 double-audit on any host whose proxy lags, and AC3 both names the reason and restricts the legacy path to a flag.
- Q: "Which mechanism carries the one-release legacy flag?" — Answer (plan): the environment variable `HERDR_AUDIT_LOCAL_BUDGET=1`, matching the existing `HERDR_HOST_MAX_IMPLEMENT` / `HERDR_HOST_MAX_AUDIT` precedent — no settings-schema migration, revertible without editing a persisted file. **Recommended:** env flag.
- Q: "Does the local audit ledger keep being written once admission is proxy-derived?" — Answer (plan): yes, as observability only — the header, interactive dialog, closed-pane sweep and release paths depend on it; it can never cause a refusal and disagreements are logged. Recorded in child 4's acceptance criteria.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-10 — Plan decomposition created: 6 children (contract pin → client → audit gate → admission/flag → cross-host acceptance → docs), dependency edges wired, AC coverage review `proceed` (no auto-created gap children), effort/risk refreshed.

# Implement budget header under-counts: panes running >2h are dropped from the counter

## Problem Statement

The host dispatch-budget header (`[budget: implement X/Y]`) silently under-counts implement entries whose `heartbeatAt` is older than 2 hours, even when their associated pane is still alive and working. This causes the worklist counter to report fewer running implements than exist, and more critically, causes admission to over-admit new implements on top of an already-saturated host.

## Users

- **Herdr operators**: Engineers monitoring the host dispatch budget via the worklist header
- **The downtime dispatcher**: The admission logic that uses `liveCount` to enforce the `maxImplement` cap

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A confirmed implement entry whose `paneId` is in the live pane list is counted regardless of heartbeat age — asserted with a fixed clock and an entry heartbeated 5 h ago.
2. The liveness table in the module header (`packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.ts`) and the docs liveness wording (`docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`: the gate-table `implement` row plus the surrounding implement-tier prose) are updated to the new rule, and the `stale | yes | no` row is removed or re-qualified.
3. `readHostBudgetStatus` remains a **non-mutating** read: a test asserts the ledger file bytes are unchanged after a display read that counts a stale-but-live entry.
4. Admission (`liveCount`) and display (`readHostBudgetStatus`) agree on the count for stale-but-live entries — one shared rule, no second counting path.
5. Existing behaviour is preserved: stale + pane-not-live entries are still reaped/uncounted; fresh entries unchanged; the audit display rule (`reduceAuditDisplayCounts`) unchanged.
6. Regression test replays the observed scenario (3 fresh + 5 stale-but-live implement panes → counter reads 8, not 3).

## Impact

The worklist budget counter and the machine-wide implement cap now agree with reality for long-running implements, so the dispatcher stops silently admitting extra implements on top of a host that is already saturated.

## Constraints

- `readHostBudgetStatus` is specified as a non-mutating display read — cannot modify the ledger file.
- The audit display rule (`reduceAuditDisplayCounts`) must remain unchanged.
- Best-effort only — no new daemons or pollers.

## Existing State

- `reduceLedgerCounts` uses staleness (`!stale && hasLivePane`) to decide whether to count an entry.
- `heartbeatAt` is written only at `reserve` and `confirmHostDispatch` — no heartbeat refresh path exists.
- `HOST_BUDGET_STALE_WINDOW_MS` = 2 hours.
- Any implement running longer than 2 h becomes `stale` and is silently excluded from the counter.

## Desired Change

Treat a confirmed entry whose `paneId` is in the trusted live pane list as fresh regardless of heartbeat age. Two options under consideration:

1. **Pane-derived freshness (preferred):** On the `liveCount` path (admission), treat entries with live panes as fresh; optionally write the refreshed heartbeat back. On the display path, use a read-only pane-derived freshness override.
2. **Explicit heartbeat tick:** Refresh `heartbeatAt` for all confirmed entries with live panes once per dispatch tick.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk — Option 1 writes to ledger on display path:** If the display path (`readHostBudgetStatus`) writes refreshed heartbeats, it violates its non-mutating contract and could cause unintended side effects (e.g., stale ledger state during concurrent access). Mitigation: implement pane-derived freshness as a **pure rule inside the shared reduction** (`reduceLedgerCounts`) so admission (`liveCount`) and display (`readHostBudgetStatus`) reach the same verdict with no second counting path, and add **no heartbeat write-back** on either path — the display read stays byte-identical (AC3), and the only ledger write remains the existing stale + pane-absent reap.
- **Risk — Pane list is itself stale:** If the trusted live pane list has not been refreshed recently, entries may be counted as alive when they are not. This is inherent to the existing system (the liveness table already accepts this trade-off).
- **Risk — Scope creep into audit path:** The audit display rule (`reduceAuditDisplayCounts`) must remain unchanged. Ensure the fix does not leak into audit counting.
- **Assumption — `paneId` is reliable:** The fix assumes that a `paneId` present in the live pane list is conclusive evidence the work is still in flight. This is consistent with the existing liveness model.
- **Scope — only implement entries are affected:** The fix targets the implement budget path. Audit entries are handled separately (WL-0MW8D4UQH002TWJV already fixed the audit counterpart).

**Key Files:** (predicted — confirm during implementation)

- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.ts` — `reduceLedgerCounts`, `isEntryStale`, `HOST_BUDGET_STALE_WINDOW_MS`, `reap`, `liveCount`
- `packages/herdr/src/host-budget-status.ts` — `readHostBudgetStatus`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-claims.ts` — reserve/confirm call sites
- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.test.ts` — reduction/`liveCount` coverage (`reduceLedgerCounts`, `isEntryStale`, `reap`)
- `packages/herdr/src/host-budget-status.test.ts` — the display reader: stale-but-live counted, ledger bytes unchanged (AC3)
- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.acceptance.test.ts` — admission-vs-display agreement (AC4) and the 3 fresh + 5 stale-but-live = 8 regression (AC6)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — gate table and implement-tier liveness wording (AC2 requires the docs liveness update)

## Related Work

- **WL-0MW9VQX5T001GCUP** — Host budget reap treats a failed pane-list read as 'no panes', deleting live entries (open, high) — potential related fix or dependency.
- **WL-0MW8D4UQH002TWJV** — Audit budget header must not count a dead (pane-gone) audit entry (completed, high) — audit counterpart, already fixed.
- **WL-0MVXWQFGV000D2AB** — Host-wide concurrency budget for implement and audit dispatches (completed, high) — original budget implementation.

## Appendix

- No interview conducted — the work item description already provides a comprehensive problem statement, root cause analysis, proposed fix options, and acceptance criteria sufficient for intake to proceed directly to planning.


## Plan (auto — below effort/risk threshold)

Effort **Extra Small**, risk **Low** → full decomposition unnecessary; no child
work items. Single vertical slice through one module pair plus docs:

1. **Red tests first** (`host-dispatch-budget.test.ts`, `host-budget-status.test.ts`,
   `host-dispatch-budget.acceptance.test.ts`): stale-but-live counted (fixed clock,
   heartbeat 5 h old), display bytes unchanged, admission/display agreement, and
   the 3 fresh + 5 stale-but-live = 8 replay.
2. **Shared pure rule**: pane-derived freshness inside `reduceLedgerCounts`
   (confirmed entry whose `paneId` is in the trusted live list counts regardless
   of heartbeat age); keep the reap for stale **and** pane-absent; no heartbeat
   write-back on either path.
3. **Consumers**: `liveCount` (admission) and `readHostBudgetStatus` (display)
   inherit the rule with no second counting path; `readHostBudgetStatus` stays
   read-only; `reduceAuditDisplayCounts` / `reduceMarkerCounts` untouched.
4. **Docs**: module-header liveness table and the docs gate-table `implement` row
   + implement-tier prose re-qualify the `stale | yes | no` row.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-11T15:48:33Z — auto-plan (skip threshold) review pass: AC2 re-qualified to name the exact
  docs artefacts (module-header table + docs gate-table `implement` row and prose);
  the Option-1 risk mitigation reworded so it no longer contradicts AC3/AC4 (shared
  pure rule, no heartbeat write-back, display stays read-only); **Key Files** split
  per file and `host-dispatch-budget.acceptance.test.ts` added for the admission-vs-
  display agreement (AC4) and 3+5=8 regression (AC6). AC coverage review: proceed,
  6/6 ACs, no children created. Stage → `plan_complete`.

# Host budget reap treats a failed pane-list read as 'no panes', deleting live entries

## Problem Statement

A failed, unparseable or unwired `herdr pane list` read is converted into an
**empty** live-pane list (`hostBudgetLivePanes`, `packages/herdr/src/index.ts:
381-405`), which is indistinguishable from "herdr reports no live panes". The
ledger's liveness reduction then treats that emptiness as authoritative and
**permanently deletes** every ledger entry whose heartbeat is at least 2 h old
— including entries for panes that are still running. A transient herdr
hiccup therefore destroys the machine-scoped record of in-flight work, the
implement cap silently under-counts from then on, and the dispatcher can
over-admit implements on top of an already-saturated host.

**Origin:** found while investigating why the worklist budget header read
`implement 3/2` while 8 implement panes were live (sibling defect
[WL-0MW9VQ08W000SN63] — "Implement budget header under-counts: panes running
>2h are dropped from the counter"). 5 of those 8 live implement panes had **no
ledger entry at all**; this item is that missing half.

## Users

- **Herdr operators** monitoring the worklist header (`[budget: implement
  X/Y]`) — as an operator I want the counter to keep reflecting work that is
  still running, so that I can trust the header instead of reconciling it
  against the pane list by hand.
- **The downtime dispatcher** — as the admission path enforcing `maxImplement`
  across every instance and project on the machine, I want a failed pane read
  to make me *more* conservative, never to erase the evidence I rely on.
- **An engineer firing `/skill:implement` / `/skill:audit`** — as a human who
  owns the decision, I want a herdr hiccup to neither block my shortcut nor
  quietly delete the accounting for my other running panes.

## Root Cause (diagnosis carried forward)

`hostBudgetLivePanes` is **fail-open**: any failure — resolver error,
`{ok:false}`, unparseable payload, or a wiring gap — returns an **empty
array**:

```ts
async function hostBudgetLivePanes(readRunningPanes, cwd): Promise<HostBudgetLivePane[]> {
  try {
    const running = await readRunningPanes(cwd);
    if (!running.ok) return [];
    ...
    return [];
  } catch {
    return [];
  }
}
```

The ledger write paths (`reap`, `liveCount`, `freshCount`, and the repair path)
consume it as authoritative:

```ts
// reduceLedgerCounts — host-dispatch-budget.ts:444-459
const stale = isEntryStale(entry, now, staleWindowMs);
if (stale && !hasLivePane) {
  reaped.push(entry);   // DELETED from the ledger
  continue;
}
```

Three concrete deletion / corruption paths follow from the same value:

1. **`reap` / `liveCount`** — `liveCount` reaps stale, pane-less entries on
   read, so even an *admission* read mutates the ledger (heartbeats are only
   written at reserve/confirm, so a stale-but-live entry never comes back).
2. **Audit repair** — `readAuditBudgetState` (`host-dispatch-budget.admission.ts:
   300-325`) rewrites an unreadable ledger *from the pane list*; with the
   fail-open empty list it rewrites an **empty** ledger, deleting every entry.
3. **Interactive gate** — `prepareInteractiveAgentDispatch` calls
   `liveCount` for the implement tier, so the human-fired path reaps on an
   untrusted list too. It already tracks `livePanesTrusted` (a thrown-error
   heuristic) for the audit *display* count only; the implement branch never
   consults it, and a `{ok:false}` result (no throw) is wrongly reported as
   trusted.

The asymmetry is documented in the helper's own comment: fail-open is
justified because "a herdr hiccup never silently wedges dispatch" — correct
for **admission**, wrong for **reap**, where an empty list means *delete live
state*. The same value cannot safely serve both directions.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A failed/unusable pane read causes **no** ledger deletion: with a stale
   entry present and the pane read failing, the ledger file is byte-identical
   after (a) the dispatcher admission read, (b) the interactive gate read, and
   (c) **both** ledger-repair paths — audit (`readAuditBudgetState`,
   `host-dispatch-budget.admission.ts:506`) and implement
   (`admitHostBudgetDispatch`, `:724`) — i.e. an unreadable ledger plus a
   failed pane read must **not** be rewritten as an empty ledger.
2. A successful read that genuinely lacks the pane still reaps the entry —
   existing behaviour preserved, asserted in the same test file as AC1 so the
   two directions are pinned together.
3. Counting semantics on an unknown pane state are explicit and tested on
   every path: the pane-derived liveness requirement is dropped and the
   documented **freshness rule** applies (fresh entries count, nothing is
   reaped). Unknown is never treated as "no panes", and a broken herdr does
   not refuse a tick on its own (the existing fail-open rationale is
   preserved).
4. `hostBudgetLivePanes` no longer returns a bare `[]` that callers cannot
   distinguish from a real empty result: it returns a tri-state (mirroring the
   `InFlightPanes` precedent in `downtime-worker.types.ts`), and a test pins
   the tri-state through at least one call site, asserting the ledger layer
   receives an explicit unknown marker rather than `[]`.
5. All four `index.ts` call sites — audit repair, implement admission,
   `readHostBudgetStatus`, and the interactive `readLivePanes` (the fourth, not
   the third) — are updated consistently; no
   second pane-read helper is introduced; the interactive path's
   `livePanesTrusted` heuristic is derived from the tri-state rather than from
   a caught throw, and the display path (`readHostBudgetStatus`) stays
   non-mutating.
6. Module header (`host-dispatch-budget.ts`), `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`
   (gate table + fail-direction table) and `packages/herdr/README.md`
   record the empty-vs-unknown distinction and why reap must not act on
   unknown; all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
   including code comments.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A transient herdr hiccup can no longer wipe the dispatch-budget ledger's
knowledge of work that is still running, so the implement cap keeps counting
long-running panes and the dispatcher stops losing track of in-flight work.

## Constraints

- **No new daemons, pollers or heartbeat refreshers** — the ledger stays
  read-modify-write on demand under the existing coordination lock.
- **One pane-read helper** — `hostBudgetLivePanes` stays the single machine-wide
  pane read; the fix changes its *return shape*, not the number of readers.
- **Preserve the fail-open intent for admission**: a herdr hiccup must not
  wedge dispatch by itself. The fix must not turn an unknown pane read into a
  refusal.
- **`readHostBudgetStatus` is a non-mutating display read** — it may not
  rewrite the ledger in any case.
- **Scope boundary:** `sweepClosedPanes` call sites (`index.ts:1317`,
  `pane-close-cli.ts:131`) already receive lists gated on a successful raw
  pane read, so they are out of scope — do not restructure the pane reaper.
- Repository boundary: changes belong in `packages/herdr/` and the two docs
  files; do not edit `.pi/`, `skill/` or `command/`.

## Existing State

- `RunningPanesResult` (`downtime-worker.types.ts:778`) is already a two-arm
  union (`{ok:true, count, paneIds?, records?}` | `{ok:false, error?}`), so the
  information needed to distinguish unknown already exists at the resolver
  boundary — `hostBudgetLivePanes` is what discards it.
- `InFlightPanes` (`downtime-worker.types.ts:807-812`) is the documented
  tri-state precedent for exactly this hazard (`available: true | false`).
- `auditDisplayCount` (`host-budget-status.ts:215`) already implements the
  fallback rule for the **audit** display figure: an `undefined` live-pane set
  means "fall back to the freshness rule", an empty set means "authoritatively
  no panes". The equivalent is **missing for the implement figure**, which uses
  `livePaneIdSet(opts.livePanes ?? [])` (`host-budget-status.ts:203`) and so
  reads unknown as "zero implements"; the dispatcher/reap paths lack it too
  (Plan correction C2).
- `reduceLedgerCounts` is the single pure reduction used by `reap`,
  `liveCount` and the closed-pane sweep; `HOST_BUDGET_STALE_WINDOW_MS` is 2 h
  and `heartbeatAt` is written only at reserve/confirm (there is no refresh
  path), which is why a reaped live entry never reappears.
- `prepareInteractiveAgentDispatch` already computes `livePanesTrusted` — a
  caught-throw heuristic that cannot see `{ok:false}`.
- The helper's doc comment explicitly argues for fail-open on admission
  grounds; there is no equivalent statement about reap.

## Desired Change

Make "pane state unknown" a first-class value and thread it to the ledger:

1. **Tri-state pane read.** `hostBudgetLivePanes` returns
   `{ ok: true, panes: HostBudgetLivePane[] } | { ok: false }` (mirroring
   `InFlightPanes`), keeping its fail-open *decision* but no longer lying about
   *why* the list is empty.
2. **No reap on unknown.** `reap`, `liveCount` and the repair path take an
   explicit "pane liveness known" input; when it is false they retain every
   entry (no writes at all, so an admission read is a pure read) and skip the
   repair rewrite.
3. **Count by the freshness rule on unknown.** When pane liveness is unknown,
   the implement tier counts fresh entries without the pane-membership
   requirement — the rule the display path already uses when its pane set is
   `undefined`. This over-counts rather than under-counts (conservative: fewer
   admissions), never deletes, and does not refuse the tick, preserving the
   documented "a herdr hiccup never silently wedges dispatch".
4. **One rule, every path.** Dispatcher admission (`index.ts:1371`, audit
   repair at `:714`), the interactive gate (`:1866`) and the display read
   (`:1758`) all pass the tri-state through; no call site converts unknown to
   `[]`.
5. **Docs.** Record empty-vs-unknown in the module header contract, the
   dispatcher gate/fail-direction tables and the herdr README budget section.

**Rejected alternative:** refusing the tick on an unknown pane read (fail
closed). It would be a one-line change, but it converts a broken herdr install
into a dispatch wedge that persists until the CLI is fixed — the panel of
gates does *not* already stop dispatch on a failed pane read (`runningPanes`
is decision-log evidence only, fail-open), so it would be a new failure mode.
The freshness fallback keeps a broken herdr conservative instead of fatal.

**Key Files:** (predicted — confirm during implementation)

- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `hostBudgetLivePanes` tri-state return; four
  call sites (`:714` audit repair, `:1371` implement admission, `:1758`
  `readHostBudgetStatus`, `:1866` interactive `readLivePanes`).
- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.ts` — `reduceLedgerCounts` (single

  shared tri-state type home.

  `host-dispatch-budget.interactive.test.ts`, `host-budget-status.test.ts` —
  AC1–AC5.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `packages/herdr/README.md` — AC6.

## Related Work

- **WL-0MW9VQ08W000SN63** — Implement budget header under-counts: panes running
  >2h are dropped from the counter (open, `plan_complete`, high). Sibling half
  of the same observed under-count; changes the *freshness* rule in
  `reduceLedgerCounts`/`liveCount` while this item changes what happens when
  the pane list is **unknown**. Not a duplicate (no overlap in ACs) but they
  touch the same functions, header table and test files — coordinate landing
  order and expect a rebase on whichever lands second.

  fail direction this item amends.
- **WL-0MW5KC8J300942EA** — Stale audit dispatch-budget ledger entry survives
  its closed pane (completed): `sweepClosedPanes`, whose doc already warns

- **WL-0MVXY0YG7009JMHI** — F3 — Implement-tier admission (completed): the
  implement counting rule (`fresh AND pane live`) that needs the fallback.
- **WL-0MW8D4UQH002TWJV** — Audit budget header must not count a dead
  (pane-gone) audit entry (completed): established the trusted-vs-untrusted
  distinction on the display path.
- **WL-0MW50EHZ6007QBPB** — Generalise host dispatch budget to any work item
  type (open): will re-touch the same admission module; no ordering
  dependency.
- **WL-0MW9X7EJ6009EL6E** — Host-budget refusal early-returns from head scans
  (open): concerns refusal tokens/ordering, adjacent but independent.
- **WL-0MWAMSMBH001BE5G** — Document proxy-owned audit budget and vocabulary
  (blocked): also edits the budget documentation; coordinate the same
  `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` / README budget wording.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk — freshness fallback under-admits while herdr is broken.** Counting
  fresh entries without the pane requirement is deliberately conservative (a
  fresh-but-unconfirmed reservation now counts). Bounded by the 2 h window and
  self-corrects on the next successful pane read. Mitigation: documented in
  the module contract and asserted by test.
- **Risk — collision with WL-0MW9VQ08W000SN63.** Both edit `reduceLedgerCounts`,
  the header liveness table and the same test files. Mitigation: land this as
  the narrow tri-state change and rebase rather than reformatting shared code.
- **Risk — type churn across fixtures.** Changing the public `livePanes`
  parameters to the tri-state touches many test fixtures. Mitigation: keep

  explicit unknown marker only at the reap-bearing entry points
  (`reap`, `liveCount`, admission options, `readHostBudgetStatus`), defaulting
  to "known" so existing behaviour is unchanged.
- **Risk — repair starves.** Guarding the repair rewrite on a trusted list
  means a corrupt ledger plus a broken pane read stays corrupt for that tick.
  Intended: it already fails closed, and the next pane-carrying tick repairs.
- **Risk — scope creep.** The closed-pane sweep, `pane-close-cli` and the
  interactive trust heuristic all look like the same hazard; only the ones fed
  by `hostBudgetLivePanes` are in scope. Further opportunities get their own
  work items.
- **Assumption — a trusted list that lacks the pane is conclusive.** Unchanged
  from the existing liveness model (WL-0MVXY0WQF0069YDJ); a successful
  empty/filtered read still reaps, which AC2 pins.
- **Assumption — `{ok:false}` is the only "unknown" signal** worth modelling;
  a malformed-but-`ok:true` payload (neither `records` nor `paneIds`) is
  treated as unknown too, since a repair from it would discard state.

- **Correction recorded (2026-11-11 plan re-run) — the display path is only

  do not repair", so the audit-repair half of AC1(c) needs no new semantics.

data.description:
# Host-budget refusal early-returns from head scans, starving plan/intake behind an implement candidate

## Problem Statement

The host dispatch budget deliberately gates only the two *budgeted* tiers
(`implement` and `audit` — `HostBudgetKind = 'implement' | 'audit'`,
`host-dispatch-budget.ts:206`), so `plan`, `intake` and `risk-effort` are never
budget-gated in principle. In practice the two Herdr **head-scan** paths end the
whole scan on a budget refusal instead of stepping to the next candidate, so prep
work ranked behind a refused implement (or audit) candidate is never reached.

Because the canonical within-group ordering puts `plan_complete` (the implement
stage) before `intake_complete` (`grouping.ts:160-165`), a budget-refused
implement candidate sits ahead of the plan/intake work in its own priority band
on every tick. The refusal is a neutral hold — no strike, no cooldown, no attempt
budget — so the dispatcher simply ends the tick on `host-budget-implement` and
repeats the same ordering and the same early return on the next idle tick, until
the ledger drains (up to the 2 h staleness window).

**Origin:** found while verifying whether intake/plan can still dispatch when the
implement budget is consumed. Follow-up to [WL-0MW9VQ08W000SN63] ("Implement
budget header under-counts") and [WL-0MW9VQX5T001GCUP] ("Host budget reap treats
a failed pane-list read as 'no panes'").

## Users

- **Idle-machine operators** relying on the downtime dispatcher to keep the
  backlog moving overnight — as an operator I want a full implement tier to cost
  me only *implement* throughput, so that prep work (plan/intake) still drains
  and the next morning is not full of un-refined items waiting behind a drained
  ledger.
- **The downtime dispatcher (leader and non-leader instances)** — as the
  component that composes one terminal reason per tick, I want a refusal on one
  candidate to be recorded as *that candidate's* hold while I keep evaluating
  the rest of the window, so that my terminal reason stays truthful
  (`host-budget-implement` with `{live, max}`) without abandoning dispatchable
  work.
- **Reviewers of the dispatch pipeline** — as an engineer reading
  `downtime-worker.head-scan.ts` / `downtime-worker.dispatch-filter.ts`, I want
  the continuable-vs-terminal outcome rule stated once and applied consistently,
  so that the next refusal class does not re-introduce the same starvation.

## Root Cause (diagnosis carried forward)

The head scans treat only lost-claim outcomes as continuable, and `return` on
every other non-dispatched outcome.

`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.head-scan.ts` (`dispatchFromOwnHead`,
lines ~313-324):

```ts
if (outcome.dispatched) return outcome;
// A lost CAS race / marker-recovery rollback applies to one candidate.
if (ctx.skipOnLostClaim && (outcome.reason === 'claim-failed' || outcome.reason === 'claim-rolled-back')) {
  continue;
}
// Any other terminal outcome ... is returned unchanged
return outcome;
```

`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-filter.ts` (`dispatchFromHerdrList`)
has the same shape in **both** loops — critical-first (lines ~200-206) and the
normal scan (lines ~353-356):

```ts
if (outcome.dispatched) return outcome;
if (outcome.reason === 'claim-failed') continue;
if (outcome.reason === 'claim-rolled-back') continue;
return outcome;
```

A `host-budget-implement`, `host-budget-audit` or `host-budget-unknown` refusal
therefore ends the scan for that tick.

The coordination-**offer** path already gets this right
(`downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts:643-649`) and is the reference
implementation:

```ts
if (outcome.reason === 'host-budget-implement' || outcome.reason === 'host-budget-unknown') {
  hostBudgetHold ??= outcome;   // keep the offer, no strike, no attempt budget
  continue;                     // other offers are still tried
}
```

The head scan also already contains the correct *pattern* for a whole-machine
hold: the host-CPU gate sets `ctx.holds.cpu` and `continue`s
(`head-scan.ts:255-259`), and the leader folds `ownHeadHolds` into its terminal
reason (`coordination-leader.ts:828-839`). Host-budget refusals are emitted by
the admission seam in `dispatch-claims.ts:~384-400` (neutral, carrying
`{live, max}`) for both budgeted kinds, and the filter's `flags` already carry a
`hostBudgetReason` / `hostBudget` evidence pair for the audit single-flight path.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **A budget refusal is a continuable hold on every head-scan path.** In
   `dispatchFromHerdrList` (normal scan and critical-first scan) and in
   `dispatchFromOwnHead` (own-backlog fallback and registered-root sweep), an
   outcome whose reason is `host-budget-implement`, `host-budget-audit`,
   `host-budget-unknown`, or one of the proxy-owned audit refusals
   `audit-budget-saturated` / `audit-budget-unknown` (plus the one-release
   legacy `audit-host-saturated`; see Appendix R1) records the hold and steps to
   the next candidate instead of returning — asserted with an `admitHostDispatch`
   mock refusing the budgeted kind and a head of `[implement, plan]` for the
   implement case and `[audit, intake]` for the audit case. The audit-batch
   continuation is the one exception: it records the hold and ends the batch
   (AC5).
2. **The prep candidate actually dispatches.** With the implement budget at cap
   and a head ordering an implement candidate ahead of a plan candidate, the
   plan candidate is dispatched (claim + marker + spawn), both in
   `dispatchFromHerdrList` and in `dispatchFromOwnHead`; for the registered-root
   sweep the scan crosses to the next registered root when the current root only
   offers budget-refused candidates. A regression test replays the starve
   scenario over consecutive ticks: `[implement (budget-refused), plan]`
   dispatches the plan on the first tick, deterministically.
3. **The neutral terminal reason is preserved when nothing else dispatches.**
   With the budget at cap and no other dispatchable candidate, the outcome is
   still the neutral `host-budget-implement` / `host-budget-audit` /
   `host-budget-unknown` (or the proxy-owned `audit-budget-saturated` /
   `audit-budget-unknown`) carrying its `{live, max}` evidence — no strike, no
   cooldown, no attempt-budget consumption and no `no-candidate` cooldown (the
   existing neutral-refusal contract is preserved). The hold is a dedicated
   field (e.g. `hostBudget` on `HeadScanHolds` plus the evidence) rather than
   being conflated with the attempt-budget (`holds.budget`) or host-CPU
   (`holds.cpu`) flags, and its precedence in the caller's terminal-reason
   composition is documented.
4. **Every other terminal outcome keeps returning immediately.** `wl-error`,
   `spawn-failed`, `marker-write-failed`, `anchor-unavailable` and any other
   strike-worthy outcome are **not** converted into continuable holds, pinned by
   a test per scan path; the existing lost-claim (`claim-failed` /
   `claim-rolled-back`) semantics are unchanged.
5. **The audit-batch continuation keeps its no-hop contract.** A budget refusal
   during the audit-batch continuation records the hold and ends the batch (it
   does not step to another audit target), so "a batch never hops to another
   target" still holds while the batch's terminal reason stays neutral — pinned
   by a test.
6. **Documentation and code contracts are updated.**
   `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (the host-budget gate table, whose
   "skip the tick" wording becomes "skip that candidate and keep scanning", plus
   the decision-log/vocabulary notes), `packages/herdr/README.md`, and the module
   headers of `downtime-worker.head-scan.ts` / `downtime-worker.dispatch-filter.ts`
   record the continuable-vs-terminal rule; all related documentation is updated
   to reflect the changes, including code comments.
7. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Impact

A consumed implement (or audit) budget now costs only budgeted work: plan and
intake tasks ranked behind a budget-refused candidate keep dispatching instead of
being starved for up to two hours.

## Constraints

- **No new gates, no new budget semantics.** The host-budget admission seam
  (`dispatch-claims.ts`) is unchanged; only the *outcome handling* in the head
  scans changes. `HostBudgetKind` stays `implement | audit`.
- **Neutral stays neutral.** The fix must not turn a budget refusal into a
  strike, a cooldown, an attempt-budget charge or a `no-candidate` cooldown.
- **Bounded work per tick.** Continuing must stay inside the existing bounded
  head window / extension (`DOWNTIME_DISPATCH_EXTEND_MAX`); no unbounded loop,
  no re-read of the head inside the loop, no second ranking.
- **One rule, one place per path.** The continuable-hold predicate should be
  expressed once (a shared helper/predicate) and applied in both scans rather
  than copy-pasted, so `dispatchFromOwnHead` and `dispatchFromHerdrList` cannot
  drift apart.
- **Audit-batch contract preserved** — one dispatch per continuation invocation.
- **Scope boundary:** the coordination-offer path is already correct (reference
  implementation) and must not be restructured; the direct non-scan dispatch
  path (`dispatch.ts`) is out of scope.
- Repository boundary: changes belong in `packages/herdr/src/` and the docs
  files listed; do not edit `.pi/`, `skill/` or `command/`.

## Existing State

- `HeadScanHolds` (`head-scan.ts:68`) already has the hold-accumulator shape
  (`budget`, `cooldown`, `inFlight`, `review`, `cpu`) folded into the leader's
  terminal composition (`coordination-leader.ts:828-839`) — `hostBudget` is a
  new sibling field, not a new mechanism.
- `DowntimeDispatchOutcome` already carries `reason` and the optional
  `budget: { live, max }` evidence for host-budget refusals
  (`dispatch-contract.ts:431-448`), so no contract change is needed to report the
  neutral reason.
- `dispatchFromHerdrList`'s `flags` already hold `hostBudgetReason` /
  `hostBudget` (used by the audit single-flight path), so the evidence a
  continued refusal must preserve is already collected there.
- `dispatchFromOwnHead` has no equivalent host-budget evidence slot: the hold
  field must carry the evidence (or the reason token) so the leader can compose
  `{live, max}`.
- The audit-batch continuation passes `skipOnLostClaim: false` and
  `kinds: ['audit']`; the sweep passes `skipOnLostClaim: true`.
- The offer path (`coordination-leader.ts:643-649`) is the working precedent;
  the host-CPU gate (`head-scan.ts:255-259`) is the in-scan precedent for a
  whole-machine hold that still lets prep work through.

## Desired Change

1. **One continuable-hold predicate.** Extract a predicate (e.g.
   `isContinuableHoldOutcome(outcome)` in the dispatch contract or head-scan
   module) covering `claim-failed`, `claim-rolled-back` (where the path already
   continues) plus `host-budget-implement`, `host-budget-audit` and
   `host-budget-unknown`.
2. **Record, then continue.** On a host-budget refusal, store the first refusal
   (reason + `{live, max}`) in the path's hold accumulator and `continue`; on a
   lost claim, keep today's continue behaviour.
3. **Compose the terminal reason from the hold.** `HeadScanHolds` gains
   `hostBudget?: { reason, budget }`, folded into the leader's terminal chain
   with a documented precedence so a budget hold reports the neutral refusal
   rather than falling through to `no-candidate`. The filter path composes the
   same way from its existing `flags`.
4. **Audit-batch continuation:** on a refusal, record the hold and end the batch
   (return the neutral refusal to the caller); no hop.
5. **Docs:** update the dispatcher gate table wording, the decision-log
   vocabulary notes and both module headers.

**Rejected alternative A — budget-gate the stage instead of the tier** (never
offer an implement candidate when the budget is at cap): rejected because
candidate classification happens before the ledger read that the admission seam
performs, and because a refused candidate must still be *observed* to report the
neutral terminal reason.

**Rejected alternative B — make the refusal fail-closed on the tick** (strike,
so the candidate is skipped for a cooldown): rejected because a budget refusal is
intentionally not the item's fault; a strike would push a healthy item toward the
attempt budget and `needsProducerReview`.

**Rejected alternative C — continue past `host-budget-audit` only in the normal
scan:** rejected (producer decision, see Appendix Q1) because the audit refusal
is the same neutral hold from the same admission seam; a narrow fix leaves a
known starvation path and forces a second round of the same changes and tests.

## Key Files

**Key Files:** (predicted — confirm during implementation)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.head-scan.ts` — `dispatchFromOwnHead`
  outcome handling, `HeadScanHolds` gains the host-budget hold.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-filter.ts` —
  `dispatchFromHerdrList` critical-first and normal loops; fold the hold into
  `flags`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts` — terminal-reason
  composition from `ownHeadHolds`; unchanged reference behaviour on the offer
  path.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-contract.ts` — shared
  continuable-hold predicate (if placed here) and reason-token documentation.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch.test.ts` (own-backlog fallback
  and normal scan), `downtime-worker.critical-first.test.ts`
  (`dispatchFromHerdrList` owner), `downtime-worker.audit-tier.test.ts`
  (audit tier + batch continuation) and
  `coordination-registered-root-sweep.test.ts` (registered-root sweep) — the
  unit tests for AC1–AC5. The cross-tick starvation replay lives in
  WL-0MWCAMU2M007Y3PC. (`downtime-worker.head-scan.test.ts` does not exist.)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — host-budget gate table wording and
  decision-log vocabulary notes (AC6).
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — dispatcher summary of the continuable-hold rule
  (AC6).

## Risks and Assumptions

- **Assumption:** a host-budget refusal is always a *machine-wide* condition, so a
  continued candidate of the same kind behind it will also be refused. Continuing
  is therefore expected to cost at most one admission round trip per budgeted
  candidate in the bounded window, and to pay for itself the first time a prep
  candidate sits behind a refused one. If a per-item refusal ever appears (e.g. a
  reservation conflict rather than a tier cap), the rule still holds — the refusal
  is neutral and the next candidate is independent.
- **Risk — hold precedence.** The leader's terminal chain is ordered
  (`code-freeze` → CPU → review → cooldown → attempt-budget → in-flight → pin); a
  new `hostBudget` branch could shadow or be shadowed by a hold that also fired in
  the same tick. Mitigation: AC3 requires the precedence to be stated in the
  module contract and covered by a test where a budget hold and another hold
  coexist.
- **Risk — accidental strike.** The refactor touches the same `if` chain that
  decides which outcomes strike. A mis-ordered predicate could swallow
  `spawn-failed`/`wl-error` into a `continue`, turning a real failure into a silent
  retry loop. Mitigation: AC4 pins each strike-worthy outcome per path, and the
  shared predicate is allow-list shaped (explicit reason tokens), never a
  "not-dispatched means continue" default.
- **Risk — audit-batch regression.** Relaxing the continuation's early return
  must not let a batch hop targets (AC5). Mitigation: the continuation passes
  `kinds: ['audit']` and its own test asserts a single dispatch per invocation.
- **Risk — scope creep.** While touching the chains it is tempting to also fix
  the sibling budget defects ([WL-0MW9VQ08W000SN63], [WL-0MW9VQX5T001GCUP]) or to
  re-plumb the offer path. Those are separate work items: this item changes only
  the head-scan outcome handling. New opportunities found during implementation
  are recorded as linked items (`discovered-from:WL-0MW9X7EJ6009EL6E`), not
  absorbed here.
- **Risk — documentation drift.** The dispatcher gate table currently documents
  the refusal as "skip the tick"; leaving it stale would keep the next reader
  believing prep work is intentionally starved. AC6 makes the wording change part
  of the deliverable.

## Related Work

- **WL-0MW9VQ08W000SN63** — Implement budget header under-counts: panes running
  >2h are dropped from the counter (open, `plan_complete`). Changes the
  implement-tier *count*; this item changes what a refusal *does* to the scan.
  No AC overlap, but both touch the budget docs/README — coordinate landing order.
- **WL-0MW9VQX5T001GCUP** — Host budget reap treats a failed pane-list read as
  "no panes" (open, `plan_complete`). Changes ledger liveness/reap; this item is
  about the refusal outcome. `host-budget-unknown` (this item's AC1/AC3) is the
  token that reap item protects — sequential rather than conflicting.
- **WL-0MW50EHZ6007QBPB** — Generalise host dispatch budget to any work item type
  (open, `intake_complete`). Widens *which tiers* reserve a slot; this item
  assumes the current `implement | audit` split but its continuable-hold rule is
  what keeps a widened budget from starving whatever ranks behind a refused
  candidate. Worth re-reading when either lands.
- **WL-0MWAMSMBH001BE5G** — Document proxy-owned audit budget and vocabulary
  (blocked, `intake_complete`). Shares the vocabulary/decision-log documentation
  surface with AC6.
- **WL-0MVR8GDJ3008WY3Y** — registered-root sweep parent (completed,
  `in_review`), the third caller of `dispatchFromOwnHead` — the sweep flavour AC2
  must cover.

## Related work (automated report)

- **WL-0MW9VQ08W000SN63** – Implement budget header under-counts: panes running >2h are dropped from the counter (open)
- **WL-0MW50EHZ6007QBPB** – Generalise host dispatch budget to any work item type (absent = unlimited, audit-only over-hold) (open)
- **WL-0MWAMSMBH001BE5G** – Document proxy-owned audit budget and vocabulary (blocked)

Repository files the automated sweep matched on keywords (for the implementer's
orientation; the authoritative list is **Key Files** above):
`docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `packages/herdr/README.md`, `CLI.md`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (asked, agent):** Should the refusal tokens converted into continuable
  holds extend to `host-budget-audit` (not just `host-budget-implement` /
  `host-budget-unknown`)? The audit tier reserves through the same admission
  seam and the same early-return shape starves prep work behind an audit
  candidate.
  - Options offered: (A) implement + audit + unknown — one hold class, one rule;
    (B) implement + unknown only, file the audit case separately; (C) implement +
    unknown now, audit only if a test proves it bites.
  - **Answer (producer):** *A* — accepted with the instruction to continue.
    Source: interactive reply ("continue" accepting the stated recommendation).
  - Research: `dispatch-claims.ts:~384-400` refuses both budgeted kinds through
    one code path with the same neutral contract and `{live, max}` evidence;
    `dispatchFromHerdrList` and `dispatchFromOwnHead` apply one early-return
    shape to both kinds, so a token-specific fix would duplicate the change and
    leave a known starvation path.
- **Q2 (asked, agent):** What should the audit-batch continuation do on a budget
  refusal, given it is contractually "one dispatch per invocation, never hop to
  another target"?
  - Options offered: (A) record the hold and end the batch; (B) continue to the
    next audit target, matching the ordinary scan; (C) leave the continuation
    untouched.
  - **Answer (producer):** *A* — accepted with the instruction to continue.
    Source: interactive reply.
  - Research: every audit target behind the refusal passes the same host-wide
    admission check, so continuing only spends admissions to reach the same
    refusal; ending the batch preserves the documented no-hop invariant while
    still keeping the tick's terminal reason neutral.
- **Duplicate check (agent):** `wl search "host budget starve"` plus the
  find-related sweep found no completed item covering these acceptance
  criteria — no duplicate, no rewrite needed beyond this brief.
- **R1 (research finding, agent — applied, flagged for producer):** parent AC1
  names only the `host-budget-*` tokens, but the audit tier's refusal tokens are
  now **proxy-owned**. `host-dispatch-budget.admission.ts`
  (`HostBudgetAuditRefusalReason`, ~line 158) can refuse the audit kind with
  `audit-budget-saturated` (proxy verdict `available: false`) or
  `audit-budget-unknown` (fail-closed read), and the one-release legacy path
  still emits `audit-host-saturated` / `host-budget-audit` /
  `host-budget-unknown`. All of them are emitted by the *same* admission seam
  (`downtime-worker.dispatch-claims.ts` ~384-400) with the *same* neutral
  contract (`{live, max}`, no strike, no cooldown), so a `host-budget-*`-only
  allow-list would re-open exactly the audit-tier starvation path Q1 rejected.
  **Decision (applied, consistent with Q1 answer A):** the child predicate AC
  covers `host-budget-implement`, `host-budget-audit`, `host-budget-unknown`,
  `audit-budget-saturated`, `audit-budget-unknown` and `audit-host-saturated`.
  Evidence: `downtime-worker.dispatch-filter.ts:247-249` already carries those
  proxy tokens in `flags.hostBudgetReason` for the audit single-flight path;
  `downtime-worker.types.ts:756-774` types them as refusal reasons.
  **Producer:** say if the audit-tier tokens should stay out of scope (they
  would then need their own item); no blocker for planning.
- **R2 (research finding, agent — applied):** parent AC1 as originally written
  listed the *audit-batch continuation* among the paths that "step to the next
  candidate", contradicting AC5 ("records the hold and ends the batch"). AC5 and
  Appendix Q2 answer A are authoritative (the code comment at
  `downtime-worker.head-scan.ts:~322` also states AC3's no-hop rule), so AC1 now
  names the batch continuation as the explicit exception.
- **R3 (key-files accuracy check, agent):** `HostBudgetKind` is at
  `host-dispatch-budget.ts:206` (the Root Cause section was corrected from the
  stale `:167`), and `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.head-scan.test.ts` does not
  exist; the Key Files list now names the real owners
  (`downtime-worker.dispatch.test.ts`, `downtime-worker.critical-first.test.ts`,
  `downtime-worker.audit-tier.test.ts`,
  `coordination-registered-root-sweep.test.ts`).

## Plan: changelog

- **2026-11-11 (plan re-run, agent):** re-ran planning over the existing two
  children (created 2026-11-11T07:40Z by the previous plan run, which never
  advanced the stage). Actions: resolved the AC1/AC5 contradiction (R2);
  widened the refusal-token allow-list to the proxy-owned audit tokens (R1,
  consistent with Q1 answer A); corrected the Key Files test list and the
  `HostBudgetKind` line reference (R3); created the test-first verification
  child WL-0MWCAMU2M007Y3PC (parent AC1/AC2/AC3/AC4/AC5 end-to-end pinning,
  depending on WL-0MWBT76WY00298AY); rewrote WL-0MWBT76WY00298AY's ACs to restate
  the parent ACs they cover (AC1/AC3/AC4/AC5) and added the per-path
  strike-worthy pinning AC; extended WL-0MWBT7PQ7004O95C's ACs to the widened
  token vocabulary and the no-stale-wording check. No children were duplicated.
