# Downtime offers: fill empty buckets from the rest of the project backlog, not just the visible list

## Problem statement

The dispatcher can only dispatch what an instance *offers*, but each herdr instance computes its offers in `computeMostImportantItem` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination.ts`) by partitioning its **sprint-view window only** — the live `browseItemCount`, currently 20 items — into the `implement` / `audit` / `prep` buckets. A bucket that yields no nominee inside that window nominates nothing, and the window is deliberately never widened to fill it (WL-0MWDDHQON0015T3P AC3). The existing whole-backlog extension (`fetchExtendedHerdrItems` / `fetchWholeBacklogTail`, WL-0MW9XS0XR007K1TH) feeds only the *single* legacy offer, never the nominee buckets.

Live evidence from 13 Nov 2026 (`~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-coordination.json`):

```
AI_Hell              offers=[implement, audit, prep]   ← 3 buckets
ContextHub           offers=[implement, audit, prep]   ← 3 buckets
tce-the-rising       offers=[audit]                    ← 1 bucket
SorraAgents          offers=[audit]                    ← 1 bucket
tce-main-street      offers=[audit]                    ← 1 bucket
Tableau-Card-Engine  offers=[audit]                    ← 1 bucket
```

`tce-the-rising`'s ranked head is three `plan_complete` items followed by 16 `in_review` audits; the first two plan items are filtered out (a 24 h dispatched marker and a live pane). The window's audit bucket therefore fills, the other buckets nominate nothing, and the leader has no prep or implement offer to fall through to when the audit is refused. Its backlog beyond item 20 — and every other ready item in the project — is invisible to the dispatcher.

## Users

- **As the producer**, I want each project's ready work to be reachable by the dispatcher even when it sits below the visible worklist, so projects with large backlogs stop appearing idle.
- **As an agent debugging a root that offers only audits**, I want the offer computation to explain that it widened, or that every candidate was gated.

### User stories

1. When `tce-the-rising`'s visible top 20 items contain only audits, its check-in advertises an `implement` and a `prep` nominee drawn from items 21+, so the leader has a fall-through when the audit is refused.
2. When the leader refuses an audit for the entered entry, the same entry's `prep` nominee is dispatched in the same tick (no re-offer round trip).
3. When a deeper candidate is gated (producer-review flag, dispatched marker, in-flight pane, review-queue hold), it never becomes a nominee merely because the scan went deeper.
4. When a root genuinely has nothing dispatchable in its whole backlog, the outcome is the same `noCandidate` result with the same attribution as before.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The nominee scan is no longer window-only: for each `implement` / `audit` / `prep` bucket without a nominee after the visible window is scanned, the scan continues through the geometric whole-backlog extension (reuse the existing loop over `fetchExtendedHerdrItems`, `DOWNTIME_DISPATCH_EXTEND_MAX` growth and `DOWNTIME_DISPATCH_EXTEND_MAX_ROUNDS` cap; `fetchWholeBacklogTail` is the same primitive wrapped to exhaustion and is used by the batch path, not by this function) until that bucket has a nominee or the tail is exhausted.
- The extension is a WINDOW WIDENING of the same canonical ranking (`getHerdrListHead`), never a second ranking and never a second `wl` spawn per bucket: one read path, buckets partitioned from the same ordered stream.
- Every sequential filter is applied unchanged to extended candidates: classification (producer-review gate, freshness/recency, risk/effort caps), dispatched-marker exclusion (24 h TTL), attempt budget, non-terminal cooldown, code-freeze split-by-skill, in-flight guard, and the review-queue depth hold. No filter is relaxed or reordered, and a gate-held candidate never becomes a nominee just because it is deeper.
- Cost is bounded and observable: the extension only runs when a bucket is unfilled, growth is geometric, rounds are capped, and the existing fail-open behaviour holds (an absent/`{ok:false}`/throwing extension leaves the pre-change result byte-identical and never blocks dispatch).
- A `nomineesFilledBeyondWindow` (or equivalent) signal is recorded on the check-in / decision-log entry naming which buckets needed the extension and how many extra items were read, so an operator can see a root being reached past its visible list.
- Tests (added to `packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.test.ts` and any new sibling): (a) a 20-item window whose buckets are fully gated but whose tail holds one eligible `plan` and one eligible `implement` yields both nominees, in canonical order; (b) after a refused audit the same entry still dispatches its prep nominee — the fall-through the leader's phase-2 ladder already supports; (c) a tail with nothing eligible still resolves `noCandidate` with unchanged attribution; (d) the extension is not entered when the window already fills every bucket (no extra reads); (e) a `wl` failure in the extension leaves the window result unchanged.
- Docs: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` states that the visible window bounds rendering only, and that buckets are filled from the whole ranked backlog — the "Nothing is widened to fill a bucket" paragraph is rewritten accordingly, and the "window is never widened to fill a bucket" statements in `downtime-worker.coordination.ts` (and the AC3 note in `coordination-dispatch.test.ts`) are updated.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
- **Explicitly out of scope, recorded rather than silently absorbed:** (i) candidates held by the 24 h dispatched-marker or by a still-open in-flight pane stay invisible regardless of widening — separate items own those (they are why `RISE-0MWC9J1OD001CT26` and `RISE-0MW6M69LE004Z0QG` are not offered today); (ii) the leader's registered-root sweep (`downtimeWorklogRoots`) stays a separate, independent mechanism; (iii) the audit-admission budget fix and the round-robin charge are separate items — this change must not touch either.

## Impact

Every project can offer its dispatcher a full set of buckets drawn from its whole backlog, so a root whose visible top 20 items are all audits no longer hands the leader an empty menu while its ready work waits below the fold.

## Constraints

- One read path: bucket partitioning and the single offer must come from the same ordered stream produced by `getHerdrListHead`; no per-bucket `wl` spawn and no second ranking implementation.
- Filter order is load-bearing (it decides attribution and side effects such as `flagBudgetExhausted`); the extension must run the same `scanOfferable` chain unchanged, only over more items.
- Extra reads are paid only when needed: no widening when the window already fills every bucket, and the walk stops as soon as all buckets are filled.
- Fail-open is non-negotiable: an extension that fails or adds nothing must leave the pre-change result byte-identical (same `noCandidate` / hold tokens and attribution).
- Backwards compatibility: entries whose nominees are all window-sourced stay byte-identical; v1-era leaders keep reading `workItemId` as the first offer.
- Run-time budget: the leader tick cost must stay within the existing benchmark ceiling (`npm run benchmark:leader-tick-cost`), since the entry may now carry nominees sourced from more reads on the owner side.

## Existing state

- `computeMostImportantItem` (`downtime-worker.coordination.ts`) reads the sprint-view window once via `deps.getHerdrListHead(cwd, sprintWindow)`, then calls `scanOfferable(head.items, true, offerState)` to accumulate the single offer **and** the per-bucket nominees.
- The whole-backlog loop below it calls `scanOfferable(extendedItems, false, offerState)` — extension candidates feed only the single offer; the `withNominees:false` flag is the coded form of "the window is never widened to fill a bucket" (AC3 of WL-0MWDDHQON0015T3P, documented at `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, "Nothing is widened to fill a bucket").
- `scanOfferable` already implements the full sequential filter chain (classification → bucket skip → dispatched marker → attempt budget → non-terminal cooldown → code-freeze → in-flight guard → review-queue hold), with first-gate-wins rejection attribution.
- `fetchExtendedHerdrItems` (gates) grows geometrically (`max(current + DOWNTIME_DISPATCH_EXTEND_MAX, current * 2)`), returns only items beyond `current`, and is fail-open; `fetchWholeBacklogTail` loops it to exhaustion under the same round cap and is used by `downtime-worker.coordination-batch.ts` — `computeMostImportantItem` runs its own equivalent loop (`DOWNTIME_DISPATCH_EXTEND_MAX_ROUNDS`) and stops at the first single offer.
- `downtime-worker.coordination-checkin.ts` writes the v2 `offers` payload from `result.nominees`, falling back to a single-offer payload when `nominees` is empty; it logs `emptyOfferLogFields(result.attribution)` on the empty path.
- `downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts` iterates an entry's offers via `orderAdmissibleOffers` and already `continue`s to the next nominee when the audit budget refuses one.

## Desired change

When the visible list yields no nominee for a bucket, keep walking the SAME canonical ranking deeper into the project's backlog until each bucket has a nominee (or the backlog is exhausted). The visible window is a rendering bound, not a dispatch bound — the same principle already applied to the single-offer path. Concretely: run the extension whenever at least one bucket is unfilled (not only when the single offer is missing), pass the nominees flag through to the extended scan, stop as soon as all buckets are filled, and record which buckets were filled beyond the window plus how many extra items were read.

## Plan (plan skill, 13 Nov 2026)

**Decomposition decision: single leaf — no child items.** This is a Small/Medium `feature` whose ACs already enumerate the exact test cases (a)-(e), the docs edits and every touched file, and whose siblings of comparable size (`WL-0MWDDHQON0015T3P`, `WL-0MWDVMZNV0011FDT`) shipped as single items. Splitting it would duplicate the AC list across children without isolating any independently deliverable slice, so planning stops at `plan_complete` and implementation continues on this item.

### Vertical slice, test-first

One vertical slice (code + tests + docs + observability), delivered in this order:

1. **Red tests first** — extend `packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.test.ts` with cases (a) and (b): a 20-item window whose buckets are all gated but whose tail holds an eligible `plan` and an eligible `implement` yields both nominees in canonical `COORDINATION_OFFER_BUCKETS` order; and a refused audit still leaves the entry's `prep` nominee dispatchable in the same tick. Cases (c), (d) and (e) are written in the same batch as regression guards (they must stay green before and after). Verify: changed-scope run via `/skill:test` fails on (a)/(b) and passes (c)/(d)/(e) pre-change.
2. **Signal plumbing (types)** — add an optional, additive field to the success variant of `MostImportantItemResult` (e.g. `filledBeyondWindow?: { buckets: CoordinationOfferKind[]; itemsRead: number }`), leaving every legacy union member untouched. Verify: build (typecheck) plus a check-in snapshot showing a window-sourced entry rendered byte-identically (field absent).
3. **Widening in `computeMostImportantItem`** — the whole-backlog loop runs while `offerState.singleOffer === null || nomineesByBucket.size < COORDINATION_OFFER_BUCKETS.length`, scans extended batches with `withNominees: true`, accumulates `itemsRead` per round **before** the early `break`, records the buckets first filled beyond the window, and stops as soon as every bucket is filled. `scanOfferable`'s own early stop stays the term-limit (single offer found AND all buckets filled). Verify: tests (a)-(e) green, plus the existing nominee/window and single-offer extension suites unchanged.
4. **Observability write** — `downtime-worker.coordination-checkin.ts` records the signal on the check-in entry and/or coordination decision-log entry (field or log fields naming buckets + items read); the `noCandidate` attribution path keeps reporting `windowSize = head.items.length + extendedTotal` exactly as today. Verify: a check-in test asserting the signal appears for a widened entry and is absent for a window-only entry.
5. **Docs and comment rewrite** — `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` "Per-bucket nominees from one head read" / "Nothing is widened to fill a bucket" (line ~170) and the window statement at ~297 become "the visible window bounds rendering only; buckets are filled from the whole ranked backlog"; the AC3 commentary in `downtime-worker.coordination.ts` (`withNominees:false` doc) and `coordination-dispatch.test.ts` (~line 1134) is rewritten to match. Verify: grep for "never widened"/"Nothing is widened" returns only the new wording.
6. **Benchmark** — re-run `npm run benchmark:leader-tick-cost` on the owner side to confirm the tick stays within the existing ceiling with more reads per entry.

Between steps 3 and 4, re-read this description and the leader-side fall-through tests: any AC now covered differently is updated before the next step starts.

### Filters, cost, and fail-open (implementation invariants)

- **One read path:** bucket partitioning and the single offer both come from `getHerdrListHead`; the extension is a window widening of the same ordered stream, one `wl` spawn per round (never per bucket).
- **Filter chain unchanged:** the extended batches go through the identical `scanOfferable` sequence (classification → bucket skip → dispatched marker → attempt budget → non-terminal cooldown → code-freeze → in-flight guard → review-queue hold), first-gate-wins attribution included.
- **Bounded:** extension entered only when at least one bucket is unfilled; geometric growth; `DOWNTIME_DISPATCH_EXTEND_MAX_ROUNDS` cap; walk stops when all buckets are filled.
- **Fail-open:** an absent/`{ok:false}`/throwing extension leaves the pre-change result (same tokens, same attribution, `nominees` unchanged) and never blocks dispatch.

### Decisions taken at plan time

- **`flagBudgetExhausted` side-effect amplification — accepted, documented in code.** Widening may now flag deeper attempt-exhausted items that were previously never visited. Gating the flag for extended candidates would make the filter chain conditional on scan depth, contradicting the "same filters, unchanged order" constraint; the flag is a producer-review marker, and the existing single-offer extension already exhibits exactly this behaviour. The implementation records this decision in a comment beside the flag call and in the docs paragraph.
- **Signal shape — union-additive.** An optional field rather than a new discriminant, so v1/v2 leaders and the check-in fallback keep byte-identical behaviour for window-only entries (see AC "Backwards compatibility").
- **`extendedTotal` accounting — unchanged on the empty path, corrected for the new signal.** `extendedTotal` is still only incremented for rounds that yield no offer, so `summariseEmptyOffer` window sizes do not shift; the new `itemsRead` counts every extended item read, including the round that filled the last bucket.

**Key Files:**

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination.ts` — `computeMostImportantItem`: the whole-backlog loop currently passes `withNominees:false` and only runs when the single offer is missing; the `scanOfferable` early-stop condition and the AC3 commentary need updating. `scanOfferable`, `emitNominees`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.types.ts` — `MostImportantItemResult` / `CoordinationNominee`: carry the "filled beyond window" signal (bucket names + items read) without changing the legacy union members.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination-checkin.ts` — write the signal onto the check-in entry and/or the coordination log entry.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.gates.ts` — `fetchExtendedHerdrItems` (`fetchWholeBacklogTail` is its exhaustion wrapper for the batch path; this change reuses `fetchExtendedHerdrItems` only — likely no change beyond doc comments).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts` — `orderAdmissibleOffers` fall-through after a refused audit (regression coverage only).
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.test.ts` — nominee/window tests, including the existing "never widened" assertion near AC3 (must be rewritten).
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — "Per-bucket nominees from one head read" and "Nothing is widened to fill a bucket" paragraphs; window-bounds-rendering statement.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher-post-fix-verification.md` — verification steps for a widened offer (if it enumerates offer evidence).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the ranked head beyond the window is stable between reads (same ranking function, same `wl` store); a concurrently changing backlog can yield a slightly different tail — acceptable, as it already is for the single-offer extension.
- **Risk — attribution drift:** deeper candidates now produce rejection entries; `summariseEmptyOffer` window sizes must keep reporting the window that was actually scanned (the existing `extendedTotal` already accumulates this) so operator diagnostics do not shift.
- **Risk — side-effect amplification:** `scanOfferable` flags attempt-budget-exhausted items (`flagBudgetExhausted`). Widening the scan can flag items that were previously never visited; this is the same side effect the existing extension already exhibits, but it becomes more likely — review that this is acceptable or gate it (document the decision in the implementation).
- **Risk — load:** each widened round is a `wl` list spawn on the owner instance's check-in path; bounded by geometric growth and the round cap, but visible on roots with thousands of items. The leader-tick benchmark should be re-run.
- **Risk — scope creep:** related opportunities (dispatched-marker TTL, in-flight invisibility, registered-root sweep) are recorded as separate items — do not absorb them here.
- **Assumption:** `prep` buckets (`plan`/`intake`/`risk-effort`) are as eligible for widening as `implement`/`audit`; the classifier order is unchanged.

## Related work

- **WL-0MWDDHQON0015T3P** (completed) — tier-aware offers. Its AC3 ("the window is never widened to fill a bucket") is **superseded** by this item; a comment has been recorded on that item.
- **WL-0MWDVMZNV0011FDT** (completed) — per-bucket nominees from one shared head read: the structure this item extends.
- **WL-0MW9XS0XR007K1TH** (completed) — made every work item a dispatch candidate; this item extends the same principle to the nominee buckets.
- **WL-0MVR8GDJ3008WY3Y / WL-0MW4ZOSD6004SAVD** — registered-root sweep (a *cross-root* mechanism, currently unconfigured on this machine); independent of this change.
- **WL-0MWFIZ8H5005FVNN** (round-robin charge) and the audit-admission fix — the other two blockers in the 13 Nov dispatch starvation, on separate items.
- **WL-0MWC9J1OD001CT26 / WL-0MW6M69LE004Z0QG** — the two gated `tce-the-rising` plan items that motivated the evidence; out of scope here.

### Related work items (automated find-related report)

- **WL-0MWDVN2HN004CQ1O** — Leader iterates offers through unchanged filter chain with drain-aware tie-break (completed): the leader-side half this item relies on for fall-through.
- **WL-0MWDVMZNV0011FDT** — Per-bucket nominees computed from one shared head read (completed): the owner-side half being widened.
- **WL-0MWDVMVX50012RSU** — Coordination schema v2: bounded offers array with v1 migration-read (completed): the `offers` payload that will carry widened nominees unchanged.

### Related files (automated report)

- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — the offers/window documentation to update (references WL-0MWDDHQON0015T3P, WL-0MW9XS0XR007K1TH, WL-0MVR8GDJ3008WY3Y).
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — dispatcher feature notes referencing the same offer/bucket work.
- `CLI.md` — herdr CLI surface; only relevant if a diagnostic token is documented there.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q:** Does intake need a producer interview for this item? — **Answer (agent, autonomy):** No. The item was created from a completed investigation with live evidence, a desired change, explicit ACs and a documented out-of-scope list; the remaining uncertainties are implementation-level and recorded as risks. Source: item description at intake time; repo inspection of `downtime-worker.coordination.ts`, `downtime-worker.gates.ts`, `downtime-worker.coordination-checkin.ts`, `downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts` and `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`.
- **Q:** Is `WL-0MWDDHQON0015T3P` (tier-aware offers) a duplicate of this item? — **Answer (agent):** No, partial overlap only. That item deliberately excluded per-bucket widening (its AC3); this item supersedes exactly that constraint while keeping its one-read-per-bucket partitioning. Source: `wl show WL-0MWDDHQON0015T3P`, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` §"Per-bucket nominees from one head read".
- **Q:** Should the dispatched-marker TTL and in-flight invisibility be fixed here? — **Answer (agent):** No — explicitly out of scope, already tracked elsewhere (`RISE-0MWC9J1OD001CT26`, `RISE-0MW6M69LE004Z0QG`). Source: item description, "Explicitly out of scope".
- **Q:** Does the review-queue depth hold need to change so a deep implement can be offered? — **Answer (agent):** No. The hold stays an unchanged sequential filter; a deep implement nominee that the hold refuses must not become a nominee. Source: `scanOfferable` filter chain; `isImplementHeldByReviewGate`.

### Plan session (13 Nov 2026, agent-routed, autonomy)

- **Q:** Does this Small/Medium item need child work items, or is it small enough to implement as a single leaf? — **Answer (agent, autonomy):** Single leaf, no children. The ACs already enumerate the exact tests (a)-(e), the docs edits and every touched file, and comparably sized siblings (`WL-0MWDDHQON0015T3P`, `WL-0MWDVMZNV0011FDT`) shipped as single items; decomposition would only duplicate the AC list. Source: `wl show --children` (no children at plan time), `docs/dev/plan-skill-reference.md`, sibling item histories.
- **Q:** Should the widened scan gate `flagBudgetExhausted` so deeper attempt-exhausted items are not flagged for producer review? — **Answer (agent, autonomy):** No — accept and document. Making the flag conditional on scan depth would make the filter chain depth-dependent, contradicting the "filters applied unchanged, order load-bearing" constraint, and the existing single-offer extension already exhibits the same side effect. Recorded in the decisions block and to be noted in a code comment beside the flag call. Source: `scanOfferable` (`downtime-worker.coordination.ts` ~line 455), item "Risks & assumptions".
- **Q:** Does the "filled beyond the window" signal need a new `MostImportantItemResult` discriminant? — **Answer (agent, autonomy):** No — an optional additive field on the existing success variant, so window-only entries (and v1-era leaders reading `workItemId`) stay byte-identical. Source: `MostImportantItemResult` union in `downtime-worker.types.ts`; check-in `offers` fallback in `downtime-worker.coordination-checkin.ts`.
- **Q:** Should the widening call `fetchWholeBacklogTail` directly instead of the per-round `fetchExtendedHerdrItems` loop? — **Answer (agent, autonomy):** No — reuse the loop already in `computeMostImportantItem` so each round's newly visible items are scanned incrementally and the walk can stop mid-tail as soon as all buckets are filled; `fetchWholeBacklogTail` exhausts the tail and is used by the batch path. Source: `downtime-worker.gates.ts` (`fetchExtendedHerdrItems`, `fetchWholeBacklogTail`), `downtime-worker.coordination-batch.ts` line ~96.

# RCA: the worklist header reported `implement 3/6` while 10 implement dispatches were running

## Symptom

The worklist header segment `[budget: implement n/max · audit n/max]`
(`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`, fed by `host-budget-status.ts`) reported
`implement 3/6` on 2026-11-13 ~21:55 while `herdr pane list` showed **10**
running implement dispatches across four projects.

## Measurement (reproduced from the live host)

```
ledger ~/.herdr/downtime/dispatch-budget.json: 4 implement entries
  AH-0MW0KSCU20096B02  w50:p64  pane DEAD   started 19:27:53
  AH-0MW25VH540078FDK  w50:p65  pane live   started 20:07:33
  SA-0MWE4BT63005N8OE  w57:pMC  pane live   started 21:38:36
  WL-0MWDD2JE6006CL7I  w5M:p72  pane live   started 21:40:54
live implement-labelled panes: 10   (w50:p65, w50:p5B, w50:p5N, w50:p5Q,
  w50:p5Y, w50:p50, w50:p62, w5M:p72, w57:pMC, w5S:p4J)
budget.json: maxImplement 6
```

The number is not a count of running work: it is the count of machine-ledger
entries that (a) exist, (b) are confirmed (carry a `paneId`), (c) whose pane is
in the live pane list, and (d) are not stale-and-dead. Six running dispatches
had been confirmed (each has a dispatch-log enrichment row carrying its pane
id), yet had no ledger entry, so the ledger had silently lost them.

## Root causes (see the child items)

1. `release(itemId)` is the only release primitive and is keyed on the item id
   alone, so any aborted dispatch attempt or any pane close for an item deletes
   *any* entry for that item, including one belonging to a still-running
   dispatch (`anchor-unavailable` alone fired 211 times that day).
2. `repairLedgerFromLivePanes` is triggered *automatically* by any
   not-fully-valid ledger read and rewrites the whole document from live panes,
   but only reconstructs panes whose title starts with `Downtime` — which
   excludes `⚠️`/`🚫`-decorated and `Manually triggered` panes (6 of the 10
   live implement panes that day).
3. Nothing reconciles the ledger against live panes: the display is read-only by
   design, and the dead-pane sweep runs only from the pane-close reaper (which
   had not run since 12 Nov), so a dead entry (`w50:p64`) lingers while a live
   pane's entry is missing.
4. Ledger mutations are unaudited, so individual deletions cannot be attributed
   (this is why the RCA could not be closed conclusively).

## Impact (why this is not cosmetic)

The same under-counted `live` figure is what admission compares with
`maxImplement` (`host-dispatch-budget.admission.ts`), so the cap is effectively
unenforced — 10 implement panes against a cap of 6, with no
`host-budget-implement` refusal logged all day. The header is faithfully
reporting a ledger that has drifted.

## Scope

Ledger identity/retention, counting truthfulness, reconciliation cadence and
observability. **Out of scope:** generalising the budget to all
`DowntimeSkillKind` members (WL-0MW50EHZ6007QBPB) and the proxy-owned audit
budget contract.

## Acceptance Criteria

- No dispatch's confirmed entry can be deleted by another dispatch attempt, by
  another kind, or by another pane for the same work item.
- No confirmed entry is ever dropped without a durable, queryable record of the
  deletion (operation, reason, actor, item, pane).
- The worklist counter and admission both agree with the observed set of live
  implement panes within one reconciliation cadence, demonstrated against the
  2026-11-13 state (10 live panes must read 10, not 3).
- Repair from live panes is never triggered automatically by an admission read,
  and an operator-initiated repair reconstructs every live downtime pane
  regardless of label decoration.
- Reconciliation runs on the worker tick with a bounded cadence and surfaces its
  failures instead of swallowing them.

## Impact

Operators can trust the worklist's in-flight count and the host dispatch cap
again: the number shown matches the dispatches actually running, and the cap
actually stops new work at `maxImplement` instead of letting the host run
double the configured limit.
data.title: Host dispatch budget ledger integrity: count in-flight work truthfully

data.description:
# Never delete another dispatch's budget entry

## Problem

`release(itemId)` (`packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.ts`) is the only
release primitive and is keyed on the **item id alone** — it takes no kind, no
`paneId`, no attempt identity and no `instanceId`. Consequences:

- Every pre-spawn abort of the claim pipeline calls it
  (`releaseHostBudgetForFailure` in `downtime-worker.dispatch-claims.ts`, invoked
  from the admission-refusal rollback, the marker-write failure, the spawn
  failure and `abortForAnchorUnavailable`). An abort therefore deletes **any**
  entry for that item, including one created by an earlier, still-running
  dispatch of the same item.
- `recordPaneClose` (`packages/herdr/src/index.ts`) and the pane-close reaper
  also release by item id, so closing one pane of an item (e.g. its finished
  `intake` or `plan` pane) deletes the live `implement` entry of the same item.
- An audit dispatch and an implement dispatch for the same item collide: the
  second `reserve` overwrites the first's `kind` and the first's release removes
  the second.

Evidence (2026-11-13): `anchor-unavailable` aborts fired 211 times (42 in the
15:00 hour, 38 in the 16:00 hour). Six running implement dispatches had each been
confirmed (their dispatch-log enrichment rows carry their pane ids) and yet had
no ledger entry.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `release` identifies an entry by its full identity — `itemId` + `kind` +
  (`paneId` or the reserving attempt's `startedAt`/`instanceId`) — and removes at
  most the entry the caller owns. A release that would match an entry created by
  a different attempt, kind or pane is refused and reported.
- Every abort path in `downtime-worker.dispatch-claims.ts` releases only its own
  reservation; each of the four abort paths (admission refusal, marker-write
  failure, spawn failure, `anchor-unavailable`) has a test in which another
  confirmed, live-pane entry for the same item survives the abort.
- A pane close releases only the entry whose `paneId` matches the closed pane;
  closing a sibling pane of the same item leaves the live entry intact.
- An implement and an audit dispatch of the same item are recorded as two
  distinct entries and neither release/confirm touches the other.
- Missing entries remain a successful no-op (idempotency preserved), and no
  release path ever throws.

## Impact

A running dispatch keeps its in-flight slot no matter how many aborted attempts,
sibling pane closes or kind changes that work item sees.
data.title: Never delete another dispatch's budget entry (release keyed by item id only)

data.description:
# Stop automatic whole-ledger repair from silently dropping confirmed entries

## Problem

`readBudgetAt` treats the ledger as untrusted if **any single** entry is invalid
(`normalizeLedgerDocument`), and `admitHostDispatch`
(`packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.admission.ts`) responds by calling
`repairLedgerFromLivePanes`, which **rewrites the entire document**
(`replaceBudget`) from the live pane list. Reconstruction
(`entriesFromLivePanes`) only keeps a pane whose title starts with
`DOWNTIME_PANE_LABEL_PREFIX` (`Downtime`), so it silently drops:

- panes decorated by herdr's UI (`⚠️ Downtime triggered …`,
  `🚫 Downtime triggered …`), and
- `Manually triggered …` panes,

which on 2026-11-13 was 6 of the 10 live implement panes. A single malformed
entry (or a ledger written by a different version mid-upgrade) can therefore
delete most confirmed entries, and nothing records that it happened.

## Acceptance Criteria

- No admission read (implement tier or audit pre-check) rewrites the ledger. On
  an unreadable ledger the tick still fails closed, the ledger stays
  byte-identical, and a decision-log entry names the corruption
  (`host-budget-corrupt`) so the operator can act.
- Repair becomes an explicit operator action, and its pane→entry reconstruction
  accepts every dispatcher pane title form: `Downtime triggered …`,
  `Manually triggered …`, and any leading decoration (emoji/status markers and
  surrounding whitespace) is stripped before prefix/kind/item-id parsing.
- `kindOf`/item-id parsing derive the kind conservatively (unknown ⇒ counted
  against `implement`) after decoration is stripped, so over-counting, never
  under-counting, is the failure direction.
- A repair refuses to write unless it can account for every live implement/audit
  pane (no silent partial reconstruction), and reports the reconstructed set.
- Tests cover: decorated and manual labels, an unknown-kind label, a partially
  reconstructable list (refuses), and the admission path leaving a corrupt
  ledger byte-identical.

## Impact

A damaged or mid-upgrade ledger can no longer quietly erase the host's in-flight
accounting; recovery is deliberate, complete and visible.
data.title: Stop automatic whole-ledger repair from dropping confirmed entries

data.description:
# Count in-flight implement work from live panes, not just the ledger

## Problem

Both operator-facing surfaces derive "how many dispatches are in flight" from
the ledger alone: `readHostBudgetStatus` (worklist header) and
`admitHostDispatch` / `prepareInteractiveAgentDispatch` (the cap decision).
A live implement pane whose ledger entry was never written or was lost is
invisible to both — on 2026-11-13 that hid 6 of 10 running dispatches and let
the host run 10 implements against `maxImplement: 6` without a single
`host-budget-implement` refusal.

The ledger is a side-effect ledger (best-effort reserve/confirm/release), so it
can never be the sole source of truth for "what is running". The pane list
already carries the evidence: dispatch pane titles end in ` - <work-item-id>`
(`paneLabelItemId`, shared by `stalled-work.ts`, `long-running-panes.ts` and the
pane-close classifier).

## Acceptance Criteria

- One shared counting rule (no forked copy) unions ledger entries with live
  downtime implement panes that have no entry, for **both** the worklist header
  and admission (dispatcher and interactive gate), so the two can never
  disagree.
- No double counting: a pane that owns an entry is counted once.
- Applied to the 2026-11-13 state the figure reads 10 (not 3) and the
  dispatcher refuses the next implement dispatch with `host-budget-implement`
  quoting `live=10, max=6`.
- A failed pane read (liveness UNKNOWN) still counts entries by the freshness
  rule and never invents a zero.
- Dead-but-present ledger entries stay excluded from the count (unchanged
  semantics).
- The header gains no new chrome; any extra detail (e.g. "unreserved panes") is
  surfaced only in the budget dialog.
- Unit tests: ledger+panes, entry-only, pane-only, panes-unknown, dead entry.

## Impact

The in-flight number an operator reads is the number of dispatches actually
running, and the host cap is enforced against real work rather than against a
ledger that may have drifted.
data.title: Count in-flight implement work from live panes, not just the ledger

data.description:
# Reconcile the budget ledger on the worker tick and surface failures

## Problem

The two reconciliation primitives — `reap` (stale, pane-less) and
`sweepClosedPanes` (confirmed but pane gone) — run only from the pane-close
reaper (`index.ts` `sweepBudgetLedger`, `pane-close-cli.ts`) and from
`liveCount`'s opportunistic reap. The pane-close reaper had not run since
12 Nov, so:

- a dead confirmed entry (`AH-0MW0KSCU20096B02` / `w50:p64`, heartbeat
  19:27) still sat in the ledger hours after its pane closed;
- a pane-less entry (confirm missed) is permanently uncountable — the implement
  tier requires a live pane — and is only removed when something happens to call
  a reaping read;
- reap/sweep write failures are swallowed (`liveCount` falls back to the
  pre-reap count and returns), so a failing write looks identical to "nothing to
  reap".

## Acceptance Criteria

- `sweepClosedPanes` + `reap` run on the worker tick at a bounded cadence
  (documented constant) using the machine-wide trusted pane list; an UNKNOWN
  pane read performs no write.
- A confirmed entry whose pane has closed is removed within one cadence
  (regression test built from the 2026-11-13 dead entry).
- A pane-less implement entry is adopted (its `paneId` written back) when a
  matching live downtime pane for the same item id appears — the confirm is no
  longer a single racy attempt with no retry.
- A reap/sweep/confirm write failure is surfaced: one stderr line plus a
  decision-log entry, and it never changes a dispatch decision.
- Tests: tick wiring, unknown-list no-write, adapt-pane-less-entry, write-failure
  visibility, idempotency (a second tick is a pure read).

## Impact

The in-flight figure self-heals within one tick of a dispatch starting or
finishing, instead of drifting until someone notices the numbers are wrong.
data.title: Reconcile the budget ledger on the worker tick and surface failures

data.description:
# Append-only audit trail for budget ledger mutations

## Problem

`dispatch-budget.json` is rewritten wholesale on every mutation and keeps no
history. During the 2026-11-13 RCA it was impossible to establish *which* code
path deleted six confirmed entries — the ledger records current state only, the
dispatch log records dispatches, and nothing records reserve / confirm / release
/ reap / sweep / repair events. Any future drift is equally undiagnosable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every mutation writes one JSONL line to
  `~/.herdr/downtime/dispatch-budget.log` with at least:
  `at`, `op` (`reserve` | `confirm` | `release` | `reap` | `sweep` | `repair`),
  `kind`, `itemId`, `paneId`, `instanceId`, `reason`, `actor`, `liveBefore`,
  `liveAfter`.
- Rotation/retention reuses the coordination-log policy
  (`downtime-log-storage.ts`: per-file cap + numbered siblings, bounded disk).
- Fail-open: a logging failure never throws, never blocks a dispatch and never
  changes an admission/refusal decision.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` documents the trail and the RCA procedure
  that reads it, and the operator-facing budget dialog names the log path.
- Tests: one line per operation, rotation bound, log-write failure leaves the
  dispatch outcome unchanged, malformed/locked log never blocks a dispatch.

## Impact

When the in-flight count ever disagrees with reality again, the operator can
point at the exact operation, item and pane that changed the number.
data.title: Append-only audit trail for budget ledger mutations

# Audit admission must acquire a proxy lease — availability-only reads are not race-safe across hosts

Discovered-from: WL-0MWFJ4LRH0025GGX (intake scope decision).

## Problem statement

The dispatcher's audit admission reads `GET /llama/local/audit/availability` and dispatches when the proxy says `available`. That is a **point-in-time observation**, not a reservation: two hosts that read `{"live":0,"available":1}` in the same window both dispatch, and both audits land on the one shared GPU. The 2026-11-03 incident (two concurrent audits on one GPU) is exactly this race — moving the cap from per-host `budget.json` to the proxy removed the *steady-state* disagreement but left the *admission* step unarbitrated.

The proxy already ships the arbiter: `POST /llama/local/audit/lease` is atomic and answers `429` with `reason: audit-budget-saturated` + bounded `retry_after_s` when a different session holds the budget, `503` with `audit-budget-unavailable` on a registry failure, and `200` on a new idempotent renew. `DELETE /llama/local/audit/lease/{session_id}` releases at clean run exit; `POST /llama/local/audit/lease/renew` extends. herdr calls **none** of them — `grep -r "/audit/lease" packages/herdr/src` finds nothing.

## Users

- **As the producer**, I want the host-wide audit cap to be *enforced* under concurrency, so a cross-host race can never put two audits on the GPU again.
- **As an operator reading the decision log**, I want a refusal to name the proxy's own token and `retry_after_s`, so a saturated budget is distinguishable from an unknown budget.

## Existing state

- `decideAuditAvailability` (`packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.admission.ts`) is the single admission point; it consumes only the availability read and never reserves anything.
- Local lease discipline exists only for the host-budget ledger; there is no proxy lease client, no acquire/renew/release calls.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` already documents the lease protocol (200/429/503, `retry_after_s`) and states "Herdr does **not** call it yet: lease acquisition is deferred to **WL-0MWFJH3NW006F5GN**".
- `AUDIT_BUDGET_SATURATED_REASON = 'audit-budget-saturated'` and `AUDIT_BUDGET_UNKNOWN_REASON = 'audit-budget-unknown'` exist in `downtime-worker.audit-availability.contract.ts`.

## Desired change

Insert a lease acquisition step between the availability pre-check and dispatch: admission acquires a proxy lease keyed to the dispatched pane/item, dispatch proceeds only on `200`, refusals map to the shared tokens with the proxy's cooldown honoured, and the lease is released on every terminal path. The availability read is demoted to a pre-check that is never sufficient to dispatch on its own.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An audit-lease client exists (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.audit-lease.ts` or equivalent) with one bounded call per verb: acquire, renew, release. Session id is stable per dispatch attempt and derived from the dispatched pane/item, so a retry renews rather than competes.
- Admission acquires before dispatch: `decideAuditAvailability` (or its caller in `host-dispatch-budget.admission.ts`) must obtain a lease, and the dispatch only proceeds on `200`. A `429` maps to `AUDIT_BUDGET_SATURATED_REASON` with the proxy's `retry_after_s` honoured as the cooldown; `503` maps to `audit-budget-unavailable` and falls back per the documented bounded wait; a transport error still fails closed.
- Release is guaranteed on every terminal path — dispatch spawn failure, audit verdict, and abort — mirroring the existing host-budget ledger release discipline. A leaked lease must not hold the audit tier past its expiry.
- The availability read is no longer the admission decision: either it is demoted to a diagnostic/observation signal, or it is retained only as a pre-check whose result is never sufficient to dispatch. State which on the item and pin it in a test.
- Regression tests cover the acquire/renew/release verbs against captured 200/429/503 payloads, the retry-after cooldown, the release-on-failure path, and a two-session race (`acquire` → second `acquire` gets `429`).
- An end-to-end check against the live proxy (skipped when unreachable) acquires, renews, and releases a lease for a synthetic session id and asserts the availability read then reports `live: 0`.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` records the lease protocol, the token mappings, and the release discipline alongside the availability contract — the protocol paragraph already exists and must be kept accurate (add token mappings + release discipline; drop the "does not call it yet" note once wired).
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Audits of completed work become safely concurrent across machines: the host-wide cap is enforced at admission time rather than hoped for, so the GPU can never be double-booked by a cross-host race.

## Constraints

- Do not widen WL-0MWFJ4LRH0025GGX — that item fixes the path and the verdict type only.
- Lease expiry units on the availability read are epoch milliseconds as pinned; the acquire response's expiry shape is unverified and must be read through the same tolerant normaliser.
- `AUDIT_BUDGET_SATURATED_REASON` / `AUDIT_BUDGET_UNKNOWN_REASON` spellings are shared with the proxy — never rename locally. The `503` token per the documented protocol is `audit-budget-unavailable` (distinct from the local fail-closed `audit-budget-unknown`); pin the mapping in a captured payload rather than assuming.
- The new lease client joins the reader allowlist pinned by `downtime-worker.audit-availability.contract.ts` — widening the dispatch-path consumers is a deliberate, reviewed change.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Acquire-response expiry shape is unverified** — must be read through the same tolerant normaliser as the availability read and pinned in a captured payload; regression tests guard the mapping.
- **Leaked lease holds the audit tier** — mitigated by release on every terminal path plus the proxy's own lease expiry; a TTL-bound assertion in tests prevents silent leakers.
- **Scope creep into the path/verdict fix (WL-0MWFJ4LRH0025GGX)** — explicitly out of scope; this item only wires leasing.
- **Assumption:** the live-proxy E2E check is skipped when the proxy is unreachable, so CI stays green offline.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.audit-lease.ts` — new client mirroring `downtime-worker.audit-availability.ts`'s bounded-call, one-typed-outcome shape.
- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.admission.ts` — `decideAuditAvailability` is where the acquire belongs.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.constants.ts` — lease path constants beside `AUDIT_AVAILABILITY_PATH`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.audit-availability.contract.ts` — the reader-allowlist test that a new consumer must join.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — *Proxy audit availability* section (lease protocol paragraph already present).

## Related work

- **WL-0MWFJ4LRH0025GGX** — the path/verdict-type fix (blocking: this item assumes a working availability read).
- **WL-0MWAMSK9H005BOHD** — admission choke point, divergence log and legacy flag (completed); the admission funnel this lease step joins.
- **WL-0MW95GBEG005ERHS** — proxy-managed audit budget (completed); LP-0MW95FYMH006XYNK shipped the lease protocol.
- **WL-0MWAMSCOP003R837** — fail-closed availability client (completed), the shape to mirror.
- **WL-0MWAMSDNW000SL0E** — audit gate reads proxy availability (completed).
- **WL-0MWAMSLBL001JNKO** — cross-host audit serialisation acceptance proof (completed).
- **WL-0MWAMS1PW000O3OS** — pin the proxy audit-availability wire contract (completed).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- No clarifying questions were required: the item was created complete by the intake scope decision of `WL-0MWFJ4LRH0025GGX`, and the description already carried a full problem statement, users, ACs, constraints, key files, and related work. Source: existing work-item description (verified against repo on 2026-11-14).
- Duplicate-work detection performed: `wl search "lease"` / `wl search "audit"` returned only leader-election, model-lease, per-slot capacity, and audit-budget siblings — all completed and non-overlapping. No duplicate found. Source: worklog FTS.
- Context verification: leasing endpoints confirmed in the proxy OpenAPI enumeration recorded in `downtime-worker.constants.ts`; `decideAuditAvailability` confirmed in `host-dispatch-budget.admission.ts`; docs lease-protocol paragraph confirmed at `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` ~line 1286.
data.title: Acquire a proxy audit lease before dispatch (availability-only admission is not race-safe across hosts)

Parent: WL-0MWFIZ8H5005FVNN (post-dispatch round-robin cursor charge).

## Goal

Encode the new **dispatch-driven** charge contract as executable tests and rewrite the existing tests that currently assert selection-time charging, so the failing-first red baseline exists before any production code moves. Tests are written deliberately so every one fails on the current (buggy) code.

## Why this item is first

The parent's AC5 forbids "deleting the old tests to make the suite green": the existing assertions are the regression encoding, so they are rewritten to the dispatch-driven expectation *with the reason recorded*, not removed. This item holds that rewrite plus the new failing-first coverage.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.test.ts` — new failing-first test: root A (selected, lowest cursor timestamp) holds its offer while root B (second position) dispatches; asserts B's cursor timestamp **advances** and A's does **not**. Currently fails (B is never charged).
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.test.ts` — table-driven per-outcome charge test over every offer outcome: charge on `dispatched`, `spawn-failed`, `marker-write-failed`; no charge on `claim-failed`, `claim-rolled-back`, reservation `admit: false`, `anchor-unavailable`, `host-budget-*`, `audit-budget-*`, and on non-dispatchable filter-chain removal. Currently fails for every charge case.
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.test.ts` — selection-purity test: a tick where every offer is held leaves the cursor file **byte-identical** (compared against a pre-tick snapshot of `downtime-round-robin-by-root.json`). Currently fails.
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.test.ts` — four-root fairness integration test over a coordination file: four roots with interleaved dispatch/hold outcomes; asserts no root with an admissible offer is skipped for more than one tick while surplus capacity exists. Currently fails (the inversion reproduces with four roots).
- Rewritten (not deleted) selection-time assertions, each carrying an inline comment naming WL-0MWFIZ8H5005FVNN as the reason: `:744-748` header comment, `:771-774` (`after['/roots/contexthub']).not.toBe(...)` → not advanced), `:887-892` ("all entries stale" case → cursor untouched, replaced by the byte-identical assertion).
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination-registered-root-sweep.test.ts` — sweep charge test: a sweep dispatch charges the dispatching root; a sweep where every visited root holds charges none; both currently failing.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-round-robin-by-root.test.ts` — selection purity assertions (`selectLeastRecentlyServed` writes nothing, takes no coordination lock) added as failing tests; existing `advanceRoot` coverage retained unchanged.
- Every new/rewritten test fails on the current code for the expected reason (red baseline recorded in the item comment), and each test's name states the outcome class it pins.
- No production source file under `packages/herdr/src/` (non-test) is modified by this item.

- (parent AC1) A successful dispatch charges the dispatching root's cursor whether or not that root was the tick's selected root: the failing-first test seeds root A (selected) and root B (second position) with equal timestamps, has B dispatch, and asserts B's timestamp advances after the tick.
- (parent AC1, mirrored) The mirrored fixture — B selected and holding its offer while A (second position) dispatches — asserts A's timestamp advances, proving the charge is independent of selection position.
- (parent AC3) A table-driven test covers each neutral reason class: claim-failed, claim-rolled-back, anchor-unavailable, reservation admit: false, host-budget-* and audit-budget-*, plus a non-dispatchable offer dropped during the filter chain, asserting no cursor write for any of them.
- (parent AC9) New and updated tests cover selection purity, per-outcome charge/neutral behaviour, non-front dispatch charging, sweep charging and the four-root fairness invariant.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.test.ts` (new tests; rewrite `:744-748`, `:771-774`, `:887-892`)
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination-registered-root-sweep.test.ts` (sweep charge tests)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-round-robin-by-root.test.ts` (selection purity tests)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts` (read-only — the code under test)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-round-robin-by-root.ts` (read-only — the code under test)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.head-scan.ts` (read-only — the code under test)

## Definition of Done

- Red baseline captured: the changed-scope test run shows the new tests failing for the charge-semantics reason (not for a compile/import error), recorded as a comment on this item.
- Existing tests that only asserted the old behaviour are rewritten with the reason comment, never silently deleted.
- No source change outside `*.test.ts`.

## Constraints

- Do not weaken or delete an assertion merely to get a green run; a rewritten assertion must state the new contract.
- Use the project test skill for any test execution (`/skill:test`, `run_tests.py`) — never ad-hoc `vitest`/`node --test`.
## Impact

The dispatcher fairness contract is now pinned by executable tests, so a project can no longer silently monopolise dispatch slots: any regression in dispatch-driven cursor charging turns the suite red instead of starving other projects unnoticed.

data.description:
Parent: WL-0MWFIZ8H5005FVNN (post-dispatch round-robin cursor charge).

## Goal

Make root selection a **pure read**: `selectLeastRecentlyServed` reads the cursor, returns the least-recently-served root and writes nothing — no `saveRoundRobinCursor` call and no coordination-lock acquisition. `advanceRoot` becomes the only cursor writer, behind one public charge helper.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `selectLeastRecentlyServed` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-round-robin-by-root.ts:149`) takes no coordination lock and performs no write: the locked helper `selectLeastRecentlyServedLocked` is reduced to a read-only selection (may be inlined or renamed). A missing/corrupt cursor still fails open to the first-in-array root, unchanged.
- `selectLeastRecentlyServed` remains null-safe for an empty root set and non-blocking under lock contention (it never acquires the lock, so contention cannot affect it).
- `advanceRoot` stays the sole writer of `downtime-round-robin-by-root.json` and keeps its fail-open contract: lock contention or an I/O error skips the charge and never throws.
- Structural purity is asserted mechanically, not only behaviourally: the purity test seeds an existing cursor whose oldest root is **not** first in the input array and asserts the returned root is that oldest root while the file bytes stay unchanged — i.e. the read-only path yields the same ordering a writer-backed selection would have produced.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-round-robin-by-root.test.ts` selection-purity tests from WL-0MWFJSOKM000V8IQ pass; the existing `advanceRoot` tests still pass unmodified.
- A coordination tick that selects a root and dispatches nothing leaves the cursor file byte-identical (parent AC4 half) — covered by the purity test, verified here against the pure implementation.
- No cursor-file format change (`{ "<worklogRoot>": "<ISO-8601>" }`); live machine state written by the current build stays readable.
- The module's header doc comment no longer claims that selection writes the cursor; it states that selection is pure and only a consumed offer charges.

- (parent AC4) A root that is selected but consumes nothing is not charged: selectLeastRecentlyServed is a read-only selection (no cursor write, no coordination lock) and advanceRoot remains the only writer, with a test asserting the cursor file is byte-identical after a tick where every offer is held.

## Impact

The dispatcher no longer charges a project merely for being next in line — only a project whose offer is actually consumed moves to the back of the rotation, so empty turns stop silently starving projects with matured, ready work.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-round-robin-by-root.ts` (`selectLeastRecentlyServed` `:149`, `selectLeastRecentlyServedLocked` `:181`, `advanceRoot` `:240`)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-round-robin-by-root.test.ts`

## Definition of Done

- Selection purity tests pass; `git grep` shows no `saveRoundRobinCursor`/`tryAcquireCoordLock` call reachable from `selectLeastRecentlyServed`.
- Cursor file unchanged after a selection-only tick.
- Changed-scope test gate passes for the herdr package.

## Constraints

- Selection must not become slower or spawn any `wl` process — removing the lock write strictly reduces work.
- Fail-open behaviour preserved: never throw on a missing/corrupt cursor or a concurrent writer.

Parent: WL-0MWFIZ8H5005FVNN (post-dispatch round-robin cursor charge).

## Goal

Charge the dispatching root's cursor at the moment its offer is **consumed** in `dispatchFromCoordination`'s per-offer loop, using one shared consumed-outcome predicate so the neutral holds and filter-chain drops never charge.

## Acceptance Criteria

- After `removeOffer` on the `outcome.dispatched` path (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts:730`) the dispatching root is charged via `advanceRoundRobinCursor(opts.coordinationDir, worklogRoot, now)`.
- After `removeOffer` on the `spawn-failed` / `marker-write-failed` path (`:796`) the dispatching root is charged the same way.
- No charge is applied on: `claim-failed` (`:747`), `claim-rolled-back` (`:752`), reservation `admit: false` (`:736`), `anchor-unavailable` (`:784`), `host-budget-*`, `audit-budget-*`, nor when a non-dispatchable offer is dropped in the filter chain (`:572`, `:612`).
- The consumed-outcome decision lives in **one** exported predicate/helper (e.g. `isConsumedDispatchOutcome(outcome)`) used by both the offer loop and (WL-0MWFJTCJ5004BKE4, the sweep item) the registered-root sweep — not duplicated inline.
- Charging is fail-open: lock contention or an I/O error during the charge skips the charge and continues the tick, never blocks or fails a dispatch.
- At most one extra coordination-lock acquisition per consumed offer; no additional `wl` spawns introduced.
- The per-outcome charge table test and the non-front-dispatch test from WL-0MWFJSOKM000V8IQ pass.
- The in-code comment block above the selection call (`:483-496`) is corrected: selection no longer advances the cursor; the charge belongs to the consume paths.
- Dispatch correctness is untouched: CAS claim ordering, dispatched markers, in-flight panes, `removeOffer` semantics and gate evaluation are unchanged.

- (parent AC2) The charge is applied on every consumed-offer path in the leader loop — outcome.dispatched (offer removed, downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts:730) and spawn-failed / marker-write-failed (offer removed, :796) — and each of these paths has a test asserting the charge.
- (parent AC3) The charge is not applied on the neutral holds that keep the offer: claim-failed, claim-rolled-back, anchor-unavailable, reservation admit: false, host-budget-* and audit-budget-*, nor when a non-dispatchable offer is dropped during the filter chain (:572, :612); the table-driven test covers each reason class.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts` (`:483-509` selection block, `:730`, `:796`)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.selection.ts` (`advanceRoundRobinCursor` `:665`, new shared predicate)
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.test.ts`

## Definition of Done

- Charge/neutral table test green in both directions (each charge case charges, each neutral case does not).
- Non-front dispatch test green: a root that dispatches from the second position is charged.
- No neutral hold produces a cursor write (asserted by the byte-identical cursor check).
- Changed-scope test gate passes for the herdr package.

## Constraints

- Fail-open charging only — a missed charge costs at most one tick of rotation, never a blocked dispatch.
- No new ranking, no per-tier cursors, no change to critical-tier ordering.
- Do not fold in unrelated dispatch changes; record any discovery as a separate work item.

## Impact

Idle dispatch capacity now rotates across projects based on who actually received work: a project that wins a dispatch from any position in the rotation is charged for it, while a project that only sat at the front and dispatched nothing is no longer pushed to the back.
data.title: Implement: charge the consumed-offer outcome in the leader loop

# Test baseline: pin the non-expiring offer contract

Child of WL-0MWFIZIAU007RBER (prune dead-instance coordination entries).

Test-first item. Before any pruning code exists, pin the behaviour that must
survive it, so the new dead-entry prune can never regress the retired
wall-clock TTL decision (`WL-0MTMPIQBE001J41P`, `WL-0MTOBZZNU0009MW1`) or the
liveness-aware peer predicate (`WL-0MVR8GDJ3008WY3Y`). Every test in this item
must pass against today's tree — it is the green baseline the pruning change
has to keep green.

## Scope

Extend `packages/herdr/src/coordination.test.ts`, reusing the existing
`makeEntry` / `makePeer` fixtures, with explicit regression tests for the
contract that pruning must not touch:

- `pruneStaleEntries` remains a no-op: returns `0`, never mutates the file, and
  the coordination file is byte-identical before and after (both with and
  without an explicit `nowMs` argument).
- An entry whose `lastUpdated` is far older than any staleness window is still
  returned by `readCoordinationFile` / `getEntry` and is not removed by
  `upsertEntry` or `mergeEntries` — removal happens only at dispatch time
  (`removeOffer` / `removeEntry`).
- `hasPeerOffer`'s 24 h liveness predicate is unchanged: a peer refreshed
  within `DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_MARKER_STALE_WINDOW_MS` counts, one older than the
  window does not, an unparseable `lastUpdated` does not, the caller's own
  entry never counts, and an entry with an empty `workItemId` is not an offer.
- A live-but-idle entry (no `offers`, fresh `lastUpdated`) survives a
  read → merge cycle unchanged.

No production code changes in this item.

## Acceptance Criteria

- New tests assert `pruneStaleEntries` returns `0` and leaves the coordination file byte-identical, with and without an explicit `nowMs`.
- New tests assert an entry whose `lastUpdated` is older than 24 h is still present after `upsertEntry`/`mergeEntries`, and is removed only by `removeOffer`/`removeEntry`.
- Tests assert `hasPeerOffer` is true for a peer refreshed within 24 h, and false for one older than 24 h, an unparseable `lastUpdated`, the caller's own entry and an entry with an empty `workItemId`.
- A test asserts a live entry with no offers and a fresh `lastUpdated` is unchanged after a read-then-merge cycle.
- Every test in this item passes against the current (pre-prune) tree; the changed-scope test gate is green via `/skill:test`.

## Key Files:

- `packages/herdr/src/coordination.test.ts` — new `describe` blocks beside the existing `pruneStaleEntries (no-op)` and `hasPeerOffer` suites.
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination.ts` — read-only reference for the contract under test (`pruneStaleEntries`, `hasPeerOffer`, `mergeEntries`).

## Constraints

- Tests only — no production behaviour change, no new exports.
- Reuse the existing `makeEntry` fixture and the `HERDR_COORDINATION_DIR` temp-dir isolation in the file's `beforeEach`.

## Impact

Future dead-instance pruning cannot silently break the non-expiring offer contract: live offers stay dispatchable regardless of age, and peer liveness keeps its unchanged 24 h read-side predicate.

# Pin the shipped audit-availability wire contract in regression tests (test-first)

## Summary

Make the contract tests describe the proxy as **shipped** (LP-0MW95FYMH006XYNK), so the
path mismatch and the numeric-verdict mismatch each fail a test before either is fixed.

## Context

The live proxy was probed on 13 Nov 2026 (`http://192.168.0.199:8000`):

```
GET /llama/local/audit/availability  -> 200 {"cap":1,"live":0,"available":1,"leases":[],"max_audits":1}
GET /llama/local/audit/status        -> 404 {"detail":"Not Found"}
```

The current contract test still pins the provisional literal
`AUDIT_AVAILABILITY_PATH === '/llama/local/audit/status'` and asserts only that a real
boolean verdict parses, so nothing in the suite notices either mismatch. This child is
created **first** and must be red before the two implementation children land.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A regression test parses the exact captured payload `{"cap":1,"live":0,"available":1,"leases":[],"max_audits":1}` at HTTP 200 and asserts `{ cap: 1, live: 0, available: true, leases: [] }`, plus a table of malformed verdicts that still resolve `null`.
- The pinned path assertion expects the shipped endpoint `/llama/local/audit/availability` (and the documented override) instead of the provisional `/llama/local/audit/status` literal.
- The verdict alias set is covered: `can_admit: 1` coerces to `available: true`, and an unparsable earlier alias never shadows a usable later alias.
- The new cases are demonstrably red against the current implementation (numeric verdict returns `null`; path assertion fails) and green only after the two implementation children land.

## Minimal Implementation

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.audit-availability.contract.test.ts`: replace the provisional path assertion with the shipped path plus the override cases.
- Add a "shipped payload" case parses exactly the captured body at status 200 and asserts the typed result.
- Extend the malformed-verdict table so `2`, `-1`, `"true"`, `"1"`, `null`, `{}` and `[]` each resolve `null`; keep the existing "never derived from cap/live" cases intact.
- Keep the reader-allowlist tests unchanged — no new production consumer is introduced by this item.
- Record the intentionally-red run (command plus the failing assertions) on the work item before the implementation children start.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.audit-availability.contract.test.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.audit-availability.contract.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.constants.ts`

## Dependencies

- None — this child is created and implemented first (test-first ordering). The implementation children depend on it.

## Deliverables

- Updated contract test file with shipped-payload, path/override and verdict-alias cases.
- A work-item comment recording the red run (`/skill:test`-driven), proving the tests gate the fix.

## Notes

- Parent AC3 (regression payload + malformed table) is this child's core; parent AC1/AC2 edge
  cases appear here first as failing assertions.
- Do not widen the contract test's reader allowlist: this item adds no dispatch-path consumer.

## Impact

The audit-availability contract tests now describe the proxy as shipped, so a future path or verdict-shape mismatch fails a test instead of silently refusing every audit.
data.title: Pin the shipped audit-availability wire contract in regression tests (test-first)

# Prune dead coordination entries on the leader check-in path

Child of WL-0MWFIZIAU007RBER. This is the tracer bullet: after it lands, a
dead instance's entry disappears from the machine coordination file and a
`prune` record explains why — end to end (module → leader tick → coordination
log), with tests.

## Target outcome

`~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-coordination.json` holds only live herdr
instances. A crashed or killed instance that stops checking in is removed on
the leader's next check-in tick, so `entryRoots`, the round-robin cursor and
the dispatch walk never see a ghost offer.

## Implementation sketch

1. `packages/herdr/src/coordination.ts` — add
   `pruneDeadEntries(coordDir, opts: { nowMs, staleWindowMs, leaderInstanceId? })`
   returning the pruned entries (`PrunedEntry[]`: `instanceId`, `worklogRoot`,
   `lastSeen`). One `withCoordLock` read-modify-write: read the file; keep every
   entry whose `lastUpdated` parses and is within the window; write **only**
   when at least one entry was removed (nothing stale ⇒ no write, file
   byte-identical); return the removed entries. `nowMs` and `staleWindowMs`
   injectable for tests, defaulting to `Date.now()` and the new default constant
   (`2 × DEFAULT_COORDINATION_CHECK_IN_MS`). Fail-open on every error path
   (missing/corrupt file, lock contention, write failure) → return `[]`, never
   throw. Reconcile the header comment and the deprecated
   `pruneStaleEntries` doc block: dead-entry pruning is back, **live** offers
   still never expire.
2. `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.orchestrator-tick.ts` — call the prune
   exactly once per **leader** tick inside `runLeaderElectionAndCheckIn`, in the
   `if (ctx.leaderState)` block, **before** `runCheckInCycle(...)` and therefore
   before the dispatch path reads `entries`. Followers never prune.
3. `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log-coordination.ts` —
   `CoordinationLogEntry` gains the optional `worklogRoot` (string) and
   `lastSeen` (ISO timestamp) fields, and gives the existing `prunedCount` a
   meaning: `1` on each per-entry record (a tick's tally is the number of
   `prune` records). Additive/optional, so every earlier entry shape is
   unchanged.
4. Emit **one** `kind: 'coordination', operation: 'prune'` record per pruned
   entry, carrying `instanceId`, `worklogRoot`, `lastSeen` (the entry's
   `lastUpdated`), the window used, `prunedCount: 1` and
   `reason: 'staleness-window'`, through `appendCoordinationLogEntry` with the
   configured rolling policy (one record per pruned entry, never one per tick).
5. `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts` — replace the
   "No wall-clock prune (WL-0MTMPIQBE001J41P)" comment with the new
   dead-entry-only rule and note that `entryRoots` de-duplication follows from
   the prune.

## Plan finding (recorded deviation from the parent's Key Files)

The parent lists `downtime-worker.coordination-checkin.ts` as the prune call
site, but `runCoordinationCheckIn` runs for leader **and** follower alike (it is
shared verbatim with the offer-only path). A prune inside it would run on every
instance, violating the leader-only AC. The leader-only call site is therefore
`runLeaderElectionAndCheckIn` in `downtime-worker.orchestrator-tick.ts`, where
`ctx.leaderState` is decided. The check-in module is unchanged by this child.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An entry whose `lastUpdated` is older than the bounded staleness window is removed from the machine coordination file on the leader's check-in path, and the removal is logged as one coordination-log record per pruned entry naming that entry's `instanceId`, `worklogRoot` and last-seen timestamp (`operation: 'prune'`).
- Each pruned entry produces exactly one `operation: 'prune'` coordination-log record carrying the entry's `instanceId`, `worklogRoot` and last-seen timestamp, its `prunedCount`, the window used and `reason: 'staleness-window'`; no record is written when nothing is pruned.
- Pruning is fail-open: an unreadable or corrupt coordination file, a lock-contended prune or a write failure never blocks a dispatch and never throws out of the tick — the prune is skipped and retried on the next tick.
- Pruning never removes a live entry: an entry refreshed within the staleness window survives unchanged, and when nothing is stale the coordination file is not rewritten at all (byte-identical, no-op).
- Duplicate entries for one `worklogRoot` resolve deterministically: only stale duplicates are pruned, the freshest live entry and its offers are untouched, and `entryRoots` therefore contains no root twice for a dead/live pair.
- The existing non-expiring offer contract is preserved: offers of a live instance never expire by age (they still persist until dispatched or dropped by the dispatch-time eligibility check), and `hasPeerOffer`'s 24 h liveness predicate is unchanged.
- Tests cover: (a) one live plus one stale entry → only the live one remains after a tick; (b) a stale duplicate for a root that also has a live entry → stale pruned, live offers intact; (c) a corrupt or unreadable file → left untouched, tick proceeds; (d) the prune is idempotent (a second tick prunes nothing, no write); (e) a live-but-idle instance (no offers, refreshed within the window) is never pruned.
- `pruneDeadEntries` performs one `withCoordLock` read-modify-write and returns the pruned entries with their `worklogRoot` and last-seen timestamp; `nowMs` and `staleWindowMs` are injectable.
- A test asserts the prune runs on a leader tick and does not run on a follower tick (leader-only trigger), and that the same tick's `entryRoots` sees the pruned set.
- No existing assertion in `coordination*.test.ts` is weakened or deleted (`hasPeerOffer` 24 h predicate, `pruneStaleEntries` no-op compatibility).
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (enforced by the dev-push gate), with no regression in the coordination, leader or dispatcher suites.

## Key Files:

- `packages/herdr/src/coordination.ts` — new `pruneDeadEntries` + reconciled non-expiring contract comment.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.orchestrator-tick.ts` — leader-only call site in `runLeaderElectionAndCheckIn`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log-coordination.ts` — `worklogRoot` / `lastSeen` log fields, `prunedCount` semantics.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts` — stale "No wall-clock prune" comment replaced with the dead-entry-only rule.
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination.test.ts` — unit tests (a)–(e) + fail-open + no-write-when-clean.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.orchestrator-tick.test.ts` — leader-vs-follower trigger test (or the nearest existing leader-tick test file).

## Constraints

- No new npm dependency; the coordination module stays dependency-free.
- The prune is leader-only and inside the existing `withCoordLock` read-modify-write — never a separate unlocked pass.
- Do not re-introduce offer expiry: only entries that stop checking in are pruned; a live instance's offers keep their non-expiring contract.
- The coordination log stays bounded: one record per pruned entry, never per tick.
- This child hard-codes the default window (`2 × DEFAULT_COORDINATION_CHECK_IN_MS`); the settings key and clamp arrive in the sibling settings child.

## Impact

A crashed or killed herdr instance's stale coordination entry — and its ghost offers — is automatically removed by the leader within ~10 minutes of that instance stopping check-in, so the machine coordination file, the round-robin cursor and the dispatch walk only ever see live instances, with one prune log record per removal explaining why.
data.title: Prune dead coordination entries end-to-end

# Point the audit-availability path at the shipped endpoint, with a documented override

## Summary

Change `AUDIT_AVAILABILITY_PATH` to the endpoint the proxy actually serves and make a future
path change a config edit rather than a code edit.

## Context

`/openapi.json` on the live proxy lists exactly `/llama/local/audit/availability`,
`/llama/local/audit/lease`, `/llama/local/audit/lease/renew` and
`/llama/local/audit/lease/{session_id}` — there is no `/audit/status`, which is why every read
resolves `endpoint-absent`/`http-404` and `decideAuditAvailability()` refuses with
`audit-budget-unknown`. The "PROVISIONAL" doc comment on the constant (and on the contract and
client modules) claims the proxy has not shipped; it must be rewritten as shipped.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `AUDIT_AVAILABILITY_PATH` points at the proxy's shipped endpoint (`/llama/local/audit/availability`), with a documented override (env or setting) so a future path change is a one-line change plus config, not a code edit.
- The override is resolved per call by the audit-availability client; a blank, whitespace-only or non-absolute value falls back to the constant so a typo can never produce a silently broken URL.
- Unit tests cover the default, a valid override, a blank override and an invalid override, and assert the request URL the client builds for each.
- The "PROVISIONAL" wording is removed from `downtime-worker.constants.ts`, `downtime-worker.audit-availability.contract.ts` and `downtime-worker.audit-availability.ts`, replaced by the shipped path, the probe date and the captured payload.

## Minimal Implementation

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.constants.ts`: point the constant at `/llama/local/audit/availability`, add the env-var name constant (`HERDR_AUDIT_AVAILABILITY_PATH`) and a small `resolveAuditAvailabilityPath(env)` helper beside it, mirroring the existing `HERDR_AUDIT_LOCAL_BUDGET` precedent (env var, not a persisted setting).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.audit-availability.ts`: build the request URL from the resolver instead of the bare constant; no change to the typed outcome, the timeout or the fail-closed classification.
- Add resolver + URL cases to `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.audit-availability.test.ts`.
- Leave the import graph alone: the resolver lives in the already-allowlisted constants module, so the contract test's reader allowlist needs no entry.
