## Goal

As an operator relying on the downtime dispatcher, I want the hydrator to treat a
live dispatch pane as evidence the item is being worked on **wherever that pane
lives**, so a claim is never released seconds after its pane spawns — otherwise the
item falls back into the dispatch pool while an agent is still working it (churn,
and a duplicate-dispatch window).

## Reported symptom (measured 2026-11-15, ContextHub)

Five seconds after a downtime dispatch spawned a working pane, the hydrator
released the dispatch claim under it:

```
01:11:14.792Z  downtime worker  dispatched WL-0MWFKDH78002T2CR (kind: plan) -> pane w6B:p3
01:11:15.429Z  herdr-downtime  Auto-dispatched … running /skill:plan WL-0MWFKDH78002T2CR
01:11:19.468Z  herdr-hydrator  released because no matching pane; previous assignee: dispatcher
```

At the moment of release the pane was demonstrably alive:

```
herdr pane list --workspace w6B
  w6B:p3  w6B:t2  'Downtime triggered plan finish moves … - WL-0MWFKDH78002T2CR'  agent_status: working
```

and the work item was back to `status=open`, `assignee:""` (dispatchable) while that
agent kept running.

The same release had already hit this item's earlier intake dispatch:

```
00:50:37.481Z  dispatched WL-0MWFKDH78002T2CR (kind: intake)
00:50:06.219Z  herdr-hydrator  released because no matching pane; previous assignee: dispatcher
```

That is the mechanism behind the repeated re-nomination of prep items: dispatch →
claim → hydrator release → item dispatchable again → dispatch, indefinitely.

## Root cause 1 — pane evidence is scoped to the plugin's own workspace, but fallback placement puts panes in the Dispatcher workspace

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts:5733` and `packages/herdr/src/index.ts:1758-1760`
  build the hydrator with `workspaceId: process.env.HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID` — the
  **plugin pane's** workspace (ContextHub: `w5M`).
- `createProductionHydratorDeps().listActivePanes(workspaceId)` runs
  `herdr pane list --workspace w5M`, so only the plugin's own panes are returned.
- `collectPaneWorkItemIds(panes, workspaceId)` then filters any pane whose
  `workspace_id` differs (`packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts:409-431`).
- `runHydrationOnce` derives `const hasActivePane = paneIds.has(item.id)`
  (`hydrator.ts:~897`); false ⇒ `decideDemotion` releases the claim.

Downtime placements that cannot use the project-workspace path are deliberately
placed in the **Dispatcher** workspace's per-prefix tab
(`downtime-worker.dispatch-placement.ts` precedence: project workspace + item tab →
per-prefix Dispatcher tab → legacy Dispatcher anchor). Today that is *every*
ContextHub dispatch, because the plugin pane reports
`HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD=/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/packages/herdr`, so
`resolveProjectWorkspace` returns `null` and the fallback is used. The resulting
pane (`w6B:p3`) is in a different workspace from the plugin (`w5M`) and is therefore
invisible to the hydrator: **`hasActivePane` is deterministically false, not
racily false.**

The same trap applies to any future root whose primary placement path fails, so this
is not ContextHub-specific.

## Root cause 2 — the claim-holder backstop does not cover prep/audit dispatches

The "busy = pane OR live claim holder" protection (`WL-0MVWDB3IG004NRIU`,
`claim-lock.ts`) is the intended second signal. But it reads
`<worklog>/locks/child-<id>.lock`, which is taken by the *implement* work-item lock,
not by `/skill:intake`, `/skill:plan` or audit runs — verified: there is no
`child-WL-0MWFKDH78002T2CR.lock` while its plan pane was live. So for the prep tier
pane visibility is the **only** signal, and that signal is workspace-scoped
(Root cause 1). The release comment says `released because no matching pane` rather
than `… and claim holder dead`, confirming no live holder was seen.

## Root cause 3 (residual) — no grace window between spawn and pane visibility

Even within one workspace, a hydrator tick that lands between `send-to-pi.sh`
spawning a pane and the pane title/marker becoming readable sees no pane for a
just-claimed item. Nothing bounds that window: `decideDemotion` consults only
`hasActivePane`, `blocked` and `held`.

## Proposed fix

**A. Cross-workspace pane evidence (the actual fix).**
Derive the demotion signal from a workspace-agnostic pane read (or from the union of
the plugin workspace and the Dispatcher workspace(s) in use), while keeping the
*display* marker scoped to the plugin workspace as today. Two different questions —
"is this item being worked on?" (anywhere) vs "does this item have a pane in my
workspace?" (display) — must not share one filter.

**B. Fail-open when the wider read is unavailable.** If the cross-workspace pane
list cannot be read, do not release (fail-open to keeping the claim), matching the
existing fail-open rule for an unavailable dep lookup.

**C. Bound the spawn→visible window.** Do not release an item whose dispatch marker
/ claim is younger than a documented grace window (reuse the existing marker
recency concept rather than a new timestamp field if one already exists).

**D. Keep the claim-holder backstop honest.** Either the dispatcher records a claim
holder for prep/audit spawns, or the hydrator's decision documents that pane
evidence is the only signal for those tiers — with a test pinning the chosen
contract.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Cross-workspace pane prevents release.** With a pane titled
   `Downtime triggered plan … - WL-XXXX` alive in the **Dispatcher** workspace and
   the item `in-progress` with `assignee: dispatcher`, `runHydrationOnce` makes **no**
   release and writes no `released because no matching pane` comment. Regression test
   reproduces today's exact state (plugin workspace `w5M`, pane in `w6B`).
2. **Display marker scope unchanged.** The selection-list "working" marker
   (`applyActivePaneMarkers` / `markItemsActiveByPane`) still reflects only panes in
   the plugin's own workspace — a cross-workspace pane must not light up the marker.
   Pinned by a test so AC1 does not silently widen the display path
   (`WL-0MV1BWETT005GSUJ` intent preserved).
3. **Genuine absence still releases.** An `in-progress` item with no pane in **any**
   workspace and no live claim holder is still released, with today's comment text.
   Pinned by a test (no over-correction into never releasing).
4. **Fail-open on an unreadable wider read.** When the cross-workspace pane read
   fails/returns null, the hydrator does not release (keeps the claim) and does not
   spam release comments. Pinned by a test.
5. **Grace window bounded.** An item claimed within the configured grace window is
   never released even if no pane is visible yet; after the window, today's rule
   applies. Test covers both sides of the boundary with an injected clock.
6. **No release storm / no duplicate dispatch.** After a dispatch, while its pane is
   live, the item is not returned to the dispatchable pool: a test asserts that a
   dispatched prep item is not re-offered/nominated on subsequent cycles while its
   pane exists (today it is re-offered every cycle).
7. **Prep-tier signal contract recorded.** The chosen contract for prep/audit tiers
   (Root cause 2: pane evidence only, or a recorded claim holder) is documented in
   the hydrator header comment and covered by a test for whichever option is chosen.
8. **Diagnostics.** A release records the evidence that justified it (panes seen,
   workspaces scanned, age of the claim) so a future mis-release is diagnosable from
   the comment/log without reading pane state by hand.
9. **Docs.** `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` (or the hydrator section of
   `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`) states: demotion evidence is cross-workspace;
   display markers stay workspace-scoped; the grace window and its default.
10. **No latency regression.** The wider pane read reuses the existing pane-list
    call where possible (no new per-item spawn); hydrator step budgets
    (`HYDRATOR_STEP_TIMEOUT_MS`) and the responsiveness suite stay green.
11. **Full suite green.**

## Immediate mitigation (not the fix)

The dispatcher re-claiming the item after each release is what keeps work moving
today, so it is self-limiting but churny — and it leaves a duplicate-dispatch window
if the item is re-selected before the running pane finishes. No manual action is
required; this is recorded so the operator knows today's behaviour is a workaround,
not correct behaviour.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts` — `collectPaneWorkItemIds` (workspace filter),
  `runHydrationOnce` (`hasActivePane`), `decideDemotion`, `createHydratorRunner`,
  `createProductionHydratorDeps` (`listActivePanes` → `pane list --workspace`).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — hydrator wiring with
  `process.env.HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID` (~line 5733); `applyActivePaneMarkers` display use
  (~line 1994 in `index.ts` parallels it).
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `hydratorDeps` / `hydratorWorkspaceId` (~1758-1760).
- `packages/herdr/src/claim-lock.ts` — claim-holder heldness probe (the backstop that
  does not apply to prep tiers).
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-title.ts` — title builders and
  `truncatePaneTitlePreservingSuffix` (the id-as-suffix contract the scan relies on).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-placement.ts` — why fallback panes land
  in the Dispatcher workspace (the trigger condition).
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.test.ts`, `hydrator-responsiveness.test.ts` — test homes.
- `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md`, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — docs.

## Non-goals

- Changing the placement precedence (project workspace → per-prefix tab → legacy
  anchor). Panes landing in the Dispatcher workspace is intended behaviour.
- Changing how `pane-title.ts` builds or truncates titles.
- Making display markers cross-workspace (explicitly excluded by AC2).
- Removing the demotion mechanism: releasing genuinely pane-less claims stays.
- Retroactively re-claiming items that were released during this bug's lifetime.

## Decisions already taken

- **Keep the claim on ambiguity.** Every ambiguous read (unreadable pane list,
  pane-list inside the grace window) keeps the claim. A stuck claim is recoverable;
  a released claim under a live agent is not.
- **One filter per question.** Demotion evidence is workspace-agnostic; display is
  workspace-scoped. They must not share a helper call with a shared workspace
  argument.

## Related

- `WL-0MWH50EN4007C6YH` — the Dispatcher-anchor wedge that forces ContextHub onto the
  fallback placement path (this bug's trigger condition). Discovered-from that item.
- `WL-0MV1BWETT005GSUJ` — pane-title-based active matching and the
  truncate-preserving-suffix contract; its `workspaceId` scoping is the code under
  change (the display half must be preserved).
- `WL-0MVWDB3IG004NRIU` — "busy = pane OR live claim holder" cycle wiring (the
  backstop that does not cover prep tiers).
- `WL-0MVW9UQQ6004KSXY` — hydrator demoting pane-less driven sessions (the previous
  hydrator over-release bug; this item is its cross-workspace sibling).
- `WL-0MVWDB7F2003SORI` / `WL-0MVWDBF71005EJM0` — claim release naming the previous
  holder (the comment format relied on by AC8).
- `WL-0MUR5FUWD00024XN` — placement precedence that sends fallback dispatches to the
  Dispatcher workspace.

## Impact

An agent's claim is no longer released seconds after its pane spawns, so operators
stop seeing items bounce back into the dispatch list while an agent is still working
them — and the duplicate-dispatch window that churn created is closed.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MU2EOHK900425VU** – dispatcher workspace has useless pane (completed)
- **WL-0MTRBOU0Y002M2CX** – Downtime dispatches land in Podcast workspace instead of Dispatcher workspace (completed)
- **WL-0MWAM5N75004ROSW** – Host-wide release barrier: pause new implement/audit dispatch on every root while a release runs (in-progress)

- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: 0mur5fuwd00024xn, 0mv1bwett005gsuj, 0mvwdb3ig004nriu, 0mvwdb7f2003sori, absence (+349 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: 0mur5fuwd00024xn, absence, ac1, ac2, ac8 (+346 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: absence, ac2, action, active, actual (+272 more)

# Goal

Add nice-value checking to `propose_remediations()` in `pressure_analysis.py` so renice actions are only proposed when the target process is not already at the desired priority.

## Background

`propose_remediations()` currently proposes renice for every large RSS contributor under memory/swap pressure without inspecting the target's current nice value. In practice this meant:
- Processes already at nice 19 (max) would be proposed for no-op renice.
- Processes at nice 0 (default) would be proposed for +10 renice, potentially slowing live work (e.g. test suites).

The renice action in `actions.py` uses a default increment of +10. The target nice is therefore current_nice + 10, capped at 19. A renice is a no-op when current_nice >= 19 (the maximum).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1**: A new helper function `get_nice_value(pid, proc_root="/proc")` reads the nice value from `/proc/<pid>/stat` (field 19, kernel 2.6.22+) and degrades gracefully to `None` on failure.
- **AC2**: `propose_remediations()` calls `get_nice_value()` for each renice target. When the minimum nice value across all target PIDs is >= 19, the renice action is suppressed (not added to the actions list).
- **AC3**: When a renice action IS proposed, the `target` dict includes `"nice"` (int) — the current nice value — and the `reason` string includes the current nice value, e.g. `"node consumes 3072 MB RSS (current nice 10)"`.
- **AC4**: Unit tests in `tests/test_pressure_analysis.py` cover:
  - TC1: Process at nice 19 → renice suppressed (no renice action emitted).
  - TC2: Process at nice 0 → renice proposed with nice value in target/reason.
  - TC3: Multi-PID contributor where min(nice) >= 19 → all renice suppressed.
  - TC4: Multi-PID contributor with mixed nice values where min < 19 → renice proposed with min nice value.

## Key Files

- `skill/machine-hygiene/scripts/pressure_analysis.py` — add `get_nice_value()`, modify `propose_remediations()`
- `skill/machine-hygiene/tests/test_pressure_analysis.py` — add test cases TC1–TC4

## Risks

- Low: the `/proc/<pid>/stat` field layout is stable (nice is field 19 since kernel 2.6.22). Graceful degradation to `None` handles unreadable entries.
- Low: only affects renice proposals, not kill/prune/pace.

## Open Questions

- **RESOLVED (producer):** suppressed renicces are dropped silently — "silent is OK" (answer recorded on WL-0MVNR3ZV30098BI6, 2025-11-15). AC2 stands as written; no visible/skipped record, no extra test case.
- **OPEN QUESTION (implementer default):** when `get_nice_value()` returns `None` for some (but not all) target PIDs, how is the "min over target PIDs" computed? Default expectation: unreadable PIDs are excluded from the min; if no PID yields a readable nice, treat as not-suppressed (propose as today). Confirm or override during implementation.

## Goal

As a maintainer, I want the prep/audit-tier busy-signal contract pinned and the
duplicate-dispatch window closed by test, so nobody "fixes" the release by

- AC7 (contract): a prep-tier dispatch (`/skill:plan`, `/skill:intake`) has **no**

  returned to the dispatchable pool — it stays `in-progress` with the dispatcher

None (test-first).

## Goal

As an operator, I want a bounded, documented grace window between a dispatch
claim and the first hydrator tick that could release it, so a tick landing in the
spawn→pane-title gap never releases a live claim.

## Scope (parent fix C, parent AC5)

- Reuse an existing recency signal, no new timestamp field: `wl list --json`
  already returns `updatedAt` and `activityAt`, so propagate them through
  `normaliseItem` into `HydratorItem` and derive the claim age as
  `now − max(updatedAt, activityAt)` (max = fail-open toward "recently active").
  The claim write itself (`wl update --assignee`) moves `updatedAt`.
- New bounded constant `HYDRATOR_CLAIM_GRACE_MS` (proposed default `120_000`,
  documented next to the other `HYDRATOR_*` budgets), overridable via a
  `claimGraceMs` option on `createHydratorRunner` / `HydratorDeps`.
- Settings surface (matching the existing `downtimeMarkerStaleWindowMs`
  pattern in `settings.ts`: default in `defaultSettings`, number-typed read with
  a clamp): key `hydratorClaimGraceMs`, wired in `worklist.ts` where the runner
  is created.
- Precedence: the grace branch behaves like `held` — evaluated **after**
  `in_review → completed` and `blocked`, and only suppresses the release to
  `open`. Ambiguity keeps the claim (parent decision "keep the claim on
  ambiguity"). Absent/unparseable timestamps: keep the claim for the window
  (documented, fail-open), pinned by test.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Parent AC5** — **Grace window bounded.** An item claimed within the configured grace window is never released even if no pane is visible yet; after the window, today's rule applies. Test covers both sides of the boundary with an injected clock. — Delivered here as the grace-window tests asserting both sides of the boundary with an injected clock.

- An item claimed inside the grace window is never released, even with no pane visible (AC5 test child green).
- An item past the window follows today's rule exactly (AC5 test child green, both boundary sides).
- The grace branch never overrides `in_review → completed` or `blocked` (asserted by test; existing suite green).
- `normaliseItem` propagates `updatedAt`/`activityAt` and a missing/invalid value degrades to the documented fail-open direction.
- The grace window is configurable through the plugin settings key `hydratorClaimGraceMs`, clamped like the neighbouring settings, with its default recorded in `settings.ts` and the docs child.
- The release log line names the claim age and the window when a release is allowed past the window.

## Minimal Implementation

- `hydrator.ts`: `HydratorItem`, `normaliseItem`, constants, `runHydrationOnce` grace branch, `createHydratorRunner` opts.
- `settings.ts`: `hydratorClaimGraceMs` (+ default constant location used by the other defaults).
- `worklist.ts`: pass the setting into `createHydratorRunner`.

- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.test.ts`

must keep it a single named constant so a change is one line.

## Goal

Land the **test-only safety net** for the anchor self-healing work before any
production file changes, so the behaviour we must *not* regress (dead pane with
a live workspace re-resolves; an unreadable herdr fails closed and provisions
nothing; two racing callers create exactly one workspace) is pinned by tests
that are green against today's tree.

Parent: WL-0MWH50EN4007C6YH (parent AC2 and the duplicate-workspace half of
parent AC3).

## Context

The parent's regression risk is asymmetric: the fix touches the shared
provisioning path (`getDispatcherAnchor`) and adds a recovery branch to
`getDispatcherTabAnchor`, both of which already carry carefully-tuned
fail-closed semantics. The recorded pre-fix state (workspace `w6A` gone, anchor
files pointing at it) must be reusable verbatim by the sibling item that
implements the fix, so it is committed here as a shared fixture.

Evidence for the fixture shape (from the parent item, 2026-11-15):

```json
// downtime-dispatch-anchor.json
{"paneId":"w6A:p1","workspaceId":"w6A"}
// downtime-dispatch-tab-anchors.json
{"workspaceId":"w6A","byPrefix":{"WL":{"tabId":"w6A:t2","paneId":"w6A:p5"}}}
```

A pre-fix backup also exists on the live machine at
`~/.herdr/downtime/backup-anchors-20261115T011052Z/` — do not depend on that
path from a test; commit the contents as literals.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A committed fixture reproduces the recorded pre-fix anchor state exactly
   (both files, both ids `w6A`), exposed for reuse by the sibling fix item — no
   test reads `~/.herdr`.
2. **Dead pane still heals (parent AC2).** The existing behaviour is preserved:
   a persisted prefix entry whose pane is dead (workspace alive) still
   re-resolves/re-creates the tab and persists the new mapping. Pinned as a
   passing test against today's tree so the fast path cannot regress.
3. **No duplicate workspaces — a transient/unreadable herdr still fails closed**
   (parent AC3, first half). When `tab list`/`pane list` is unreadable (CLI error
   or unparseable output), `getDispatcherTabAnchor` returns `null` with
   `anchor-unavailable` and provisions nothing: `createWorkspace` is **never**
   called. Pinned as a passing test against today's tree.
4. **No duplicate workspaces — concurrent first-dispatchers create at most one**
   (parent AC3, second half). Two concurrent `getDispatcherAnchor` callers with a
   stale anchor produce exactly one `createWorkspace` call (coordination lock plus
   double-check) and both receive the same anchor; pinned as a passing test
   against today's tree, because the fix must reuse this mechanism, not replace
   it.
5. No production file is modified by this item; the full existing suite stays
   green.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add a `describe('regression fixtures: stale anchors (WL-0MWH50EN4007C6YH)')`
  block to `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.test.ts` with a shared
  `seedStaleAnchorState(tmpDir)` helper writing the two recorded files.
- Pin AC2/AC3 above with injected deps only (`vi.fn()`), following the existing
  stale-pane cases in that file.
- For AC4, drive two concurrent `getDispatcherAnchor` calls against a stale
  persisted anchor and assert `createWorkspace` was called once (the
  coordination lock is already exercised through `HERDR_COORDINATION_DIR`).
- Extend `tests/herdr/dispatcher-anchor.integration.test.ts` only if the
  end-to-end fixture is not already reachable there; otherwise leave it alone.

**Key Files:**
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.test.ts` — new fixture + three guard tests.
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.contract.ts` — read-only (fixture shapes).
- `tests/herdr/dispatcher-anchor.integration.test.ts` — only if an integration
  seam is needed.

## Dependencies

None. Must land **before** the fix items (test-first ordering).

## Out of scope

- Any production code change (including the workspace probe).
- The AC1 stale-**workspace** regression (it is red today by definition and
  lands with the fix).
## Impact

Dispatchers now get a committed regression fixture and green guard tests pinning the three behaviours the self-healing fix must not break: a dead pane in a live workspace still re-provisions its tab, an unreadable herdr still fails closed without provisioning anything, and two racing first-dispatchers still create exactly one workspace.

data.description:
## Goal

Add a **three-state workspace existence probe** to the anchor family so a
persisted Dispatcher `workspaceId` can be classified as *alive*, *positively
missing*, or *unreadable* — the classification the self-healing fix needs, and
the only way to keep "a vanished workspace is recoverable" strictly separate
from "an unreadable herdr must still fail closed".

Parent: WL-0MWH50EN4007C6YH (parent AC3 distinction; parent decision
"Missing ≠ unreadable").

## Context

`readDispatcherWorkspaceId()` returns the persisted id verbatim, so nothing can
tell whether the workspace still exists. Today's CLI evidence (measured on the
live machine, 2026-11-15):

```
herdr workspace list
  -> {"result":{"type":"workspace_list","workspaces":[{"workspace_id":"w57",...}]}}
herdr tab list --workspace wZZZ
  -> exit 1, stdout {"error":{"code":"workspace_not_found","message":"workspace wZZZ not found"}}
```

So existence can be positively established by reading `herdr workspace list`
**once**, and `missing` may only be concluded when that list was read and parsed
successfully and the id is absent from it. Any CLI error, unparseable output or
absent dep is `unreadable` → the caller fails closed and provisions nothing.

Design constraints:

- The probe is an **optional additive member** of the existing
  `DispatcherAnchorDeps` type (no new barrel export — the split guard freezes a
  38-symbol public surface with `expect(exported.size).toBe(38)`, see
  `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.split-guard.test.ts` and
  `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.split-baseline.json`). Declare the member
  as an **inline** string-literal union
  (`probeWorkspace?(workspaceId: string): Promise<'alive' | 'missing' | 'unreadable'>`)
  rather than a new named alias, so the barrel and the baseline stay untouched.
- **Alternative if the workspace-list probe proves unreliable** (zero extra
  spawn): classify the `workspace_not_found` CLI error code on the `tab list`
  call the resolver already issues in `resolvePrefixTab`. The three-state
  contract above is the invariant either way; the implementation may switch
  mechanisms without changing any consumer or AC.
- **No `wl` spawn** and no extra herdr call on the healthy path: the probe is
  only consulted on the recovery path (after a stale-pane fast-path miss) by
  the consuming item.
- Fail-closed default: an absent/undefined probe dep is treated exactly as
  `unreadable`, never as `missing`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `DispatcherAnchorDeps` gains an optional
   `probeWorkspace?(workspaceId): Promise<'alive' | 'missing' | 'unreadable'>`
   member; every existing caller/test that omits it still compiles (additive),
   and the barrel's exported symbol set is unchanged.
2. `createDispatcherAnchorDeps` supplies the probe, implemented over
   `herdr workspace list` (new module-local helper + parser tolerating
   `result.workspaces[]` with `workspace_id` / `workspaceId` / `id`, and log
   lines before the JSON envelope).
3. Unit tests: an id present in the list → `alive`; an id absent from a
   successfully read list → `missing`; a CLI error → `unreadable`; unparseable
   or empty output → `unreadable`; a thrown/absent dep → `unreadable`.
4. The probe issues no `wl` invocation (assert via a mocked `child_process`
   that only a `herdr workspace list` spawn occurs).
5. The split guard stays green with the frozen 38-symbol surface and export
   kinds unchanged (`packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.split-baseline.json`
   is **not** regenerated by this item).
6. The existing anchor suites are unchanged and green.

## Minimal Implementation

- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.contract.ts`: add the optional
  `probeWorkspace?` member with an inline literal-union return type (no new
  exported alias).
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.herdr-cli.ts`: module-local
  `probeWorkspace(cwd, workspaceId, herdrBin)` using `execFileStdout` +
  a workspace-list parser (`null` on CLI/parse failure), wired into
  `createDispatcherAnchorDeps`.
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.test.ts` (or a
  `dispatcher-anchor.probe.test.ts` sibling): the five probe cases.

**Key Files:**
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.contract.ts` — optional dep member + type.
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.herdr-cli.ts` — CLI wrapper + wiring.
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.cli-parsers.ts` — only if the parser is
  shared instead of module-local (prefer module-local: no new barrel export).
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.test.ts` — probe cases.

## Dependencies

None technically; sequenced after the guard tests (test-first ordering).

## Out of scope

- Any recovery/re-provisioning behaviour (the consuming item does that).
- Pruning, diagnostics and docs.
- Regenerating the split-guard baseline.

## Impact

A vanished Dispatcher workspace is now positively distinguishable from an unreadable herdr (alive / missing / unreadable), so the self-healing fix can safely re-provision a genuinely missing workspace without ever risking a live one.
data.title: Workspace existence probe (alive / missing / unreadable)

data.description:
## Goal

Make the persisted Dispatcher anchor **self-heal when the workspace it points at
no longer exists**: validate the persisted `workspaceId` on read, and when it is
positively missing, provision exactly one replacement Dispatcher workspace
(reusing the existing provision-under-lock + double-check path) and resolve the
per-prefix tab in it — instead of failing closed with `anchor-unavailable`
forever.

Parent: WL-0MWH50EN4007C6YH — this is the actual unblock (parent AC1, AC3, AC5;
parent "Proposed fix A").

## Context

The current failure chain (measured 2026-11-15, `w6A` gone):

1. `getDispatcherTabAnchor` step 2 detects the dead cached **pane** correctly
   (`isPaneAlive` → false) and falls through.
2. Step 1 `ensureDispatcherWorkspace` returns the persisted `w6A` **verbatim** —
   nothing validates a *workspace*.
3. `resolvePrefixTab` → `listTabs('w6A')` → CLI error → `null` → `unknown`.
4. `unknown` fails closed by design → `getDispatcherTabAnchor` returns `null`.
5. `resolveDispatchPlacement` → `{ok:false}` → `anchor-unavailable`, claim
   rolled back, and the next tick repeats it (124 occurrences in the reported
   window).

`getDispatcherAnchor` *does* self-heal (pane liveness → re-provision under the
coordination lock with an in-lock double-check) but is unreachable from the
per-prefix resolver, which deliberately never falls back to it.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Stale workspace self-heals (parent AC1).** With both anchor files pointing
   at a workspace that does not exist, `getDispatcherTabAnchor(cwd, deps, 'WL')`
   provisions a fresh Dispatcher workspace and returns a live anchor for a new
   `WL` tab — instead of `null`. The regression test seeds the exact recorded
   pre-fix state (`w6A`, from the sibling guard-test fixture) against injected
   deps whose probe reports `missing`.
2. **One recovery mechanism.** The provision-under-lock + in-lock double-check
   block is extracted from `getDispatcherAnchor` into a single shared helper used
   by **both** `getDispatcherAnchor` and the new recovery path — no second
   implementation of provisioning.
3. **No duplicate workspaces — missing ≠ unreadable (parent AC3, first half).**
   A transient/unreadable herdr (probe `unreadable`, or an absent probe dep)
   still fails closed with `anchor-unavailable` and provisions nothing: it
   returns `null` **and calls `createWorkspace` zero times**; only a positively
   `missing` workspace provisions.
4. **No duplicate workspaces — racing callers create one (parent AC3, second
   half).** Two concurrent first-dispatchers that both observe `missing` create
   **exactly one** replacement workspace (`createWorkspace` called once, via the
   coordination lock and the in-lock double-check) and both return the same
   anchor.
5. **Recovered anchor is persisted and reused.** Recovery rewrites
   `downtime-dispatch-anchor.json` with the new `{paneId, workspaceId}` and the
   tab-anchors map with the new workspace id, and a second resolution reuses
   them without calling `createWorkspace` again (idempotent, no per-tick
   re-provisioning loop).
6. **End-to-end unblock (parent AC5).** `resolveDispatchPlacement(deps, …)`
   returns `{ok:true}` in the reproduced stale-anchor state, and an
   orchestrator-level test with a stale anchor store shows **no repeated
   `anchor-unavailable`** decisions on consecutive ticks (the second tick
   dispatches, or is refused for an unrelated, non-anchor reason).
7. **Dead pane still heals (parent AC2).** The guard tests from the sibling
   test-first item stay green (fast path preserved).
8. **No `wl` spawn, no extra herdr call on the healthy path (parent AC10).** A
   healthy resolution issues the same herdr calls as today (the probe is only
   consulted after a stale-pane fast-path miss); the placement code path adds no
   `wl` invocation. Asserted with counting spies.
9. No new barrel export and no changed export kind: the split guard stays green
   without regenerating the baseline.

## Minimal Implementation

- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.tab-anchors.ts`
  - extract `provisionDispatcherAnchorUnderLock(dir, deps): Promise<DispatcherAnchor | null>`
    (lock → in-lock double-check → create workspace → adopt root pane → write
    anchor → release) and call it from `getDispatcherAnchor`.
  - `ensureDispatcherWorkspace(deps)` → `{ workspaceId, recovered: boolean } | null`:
    persisted id + `probeWorkspace` → `alive` reuse; `missing` → recovery via the
    shared helper (returns the fresh id); `unreadable`/absent probe → `null`
    (fail closed, nothing provisioned). No persisted id → provision as today.
  - `getDispatcherTabAnchor`: when the workspace was recovered (or the cached
    prefix entry belongs to a different workspace id), ignore the cached entry
    and resolve/provision the prefix tab in the new workspace, persisting the new
    mapping.
  - Keep the `unknown → null` fail-closed rule for unreadable tab/pane lists.
- Tests in `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.test.ts` (AC1, AC3, AC4, AC5,
  AC7) and an orchestrator-level case in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch*.test.ts`
  or `coordination-dispatch.test.ts` for AC6.

**Key Files:**
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.tab-anchors.ts` — the fix (validate,
  recover, shared provisioning helper).
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.persistence.ts` — read/write helpers
  (read-only here; pruning is a sibling item).
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.test.ts` — AC1/AC3/AC4/AC5/AC7 tests.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-placement.ts` — unchanged
  behaviour; AC6 exercises it.
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.test.ts` (or
  `downtime-worker.dispatch.test.ts`) — consecutive-tick regression.

## Dependencies

- `Test: pin healthy anchor paths` (tests first).
- `Workspace existence probe` (the `alive | missing | unreadable` classification).

## Out of scope

- Pruning stale `byPrefix` entries (sibling item), diagnostics detail (sibling
  item), docs (sibling item).
- Falling back to the legacy anchor from the per-prefix resolver (an explicit
  non-goal).
- Any TTL/reaper for anchor files.
- `resolveProjectWorkspace` matching-rule changes.

## Impact

Downtime dispatch now self-heals after a herdr restart: a persisted Dispatcher workspace that no longer exists is detected on read and re-provisioned exactly once (under the coordination lock), so dispatches stop wedging forever on `anchor-unavailable` — while an unreadable herdr still fails closed and provisions nothing.
data.title: Validate persisted workspace on read and re-provision

data.description:
## Goal

Make the persisted per-prefix tab-anchor map **self-pruning**: when the map is
rewritten for a (possibly new) Dispatcher workspace, drop every `byPrefix` entry
that cannot belong to that workspace, so dead workspace ids cannot accumulate
and mask a later wedge.

Parent: WL-0MWH50EN4007C6YH (parent AC4).

## Context

`persistPrefixTab` upserts one entry and keeps `{ ...current.byPrefix }`
verbatim, so entries pointing into a superseded workspace survive indefinitely:

```json
{"workspaceId":"w6A","byPrefix":{"WL":{"tabId":"w6A:t2","paneId":"w6A:p5"},
                                "TCE":{"tabId":"w6A:t6","paneId":"w6A:p31"}}}
```

After a recovery to workspace `w6B` the map must not still carry `w6A:*`
entries: they can never resolve (the workspace is gone) and they make the
persisted state lie about where dispatch lands.

Herdr ids are workspace-scoped with a `<workspaceId>:` prefix (`w6A:t2`,
`w6A:p5`), so membership is decidable from the ids themselves — no CLI call is
needed and this stays a pure persistence-side change.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `persistPrefixTab(dir, workspaceId, prefix, tabId, paneId)` writes a map
   containing only entries whose **both** `tabId` and `paneId` start with
   `<workspaceId>:` — plus the upserted entry (itself validated the same way).
2. An entry whose ids belong to a different (dead) workspace is dropped on the
   next write; the surviving same-workspace entries for other prefixes are
   preserved.
3. The map-level `workspaceId` is always the workspace being written (never a
   stale id).
4. **Stale prefix entries pruned.** Rewriting the tab-anchor map drops
   `byPrefix` entries whose workspace id is the dead one; a test asserts the
   persisted file after recovery contains no `w6A`-style dead ids (seeded from
   the recorded pre-fix map) and does contain the recovered workspace's entry.
5. Test: two prefixes in the same live workspace are both retained across a
   rewrite (pruning never drops a live sibling entry).
6. An ill-formed id (no `<workspaceId>:` prefix, e.g. a hand-edited file) is
   dropped rather than retained — it can never resolve in that workspace.
7. The write remains atomic (tmp + rename) and fail-closed (`false` on any
   error), exactly as today; no `wl`/herdr spawn is added.
8. Existing tab-anchor persistence suites stay green.

## Minimal Implementation

- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.persistence.ts`: in `persistPrefixTab`,
  build `byPrefix` by filtering `current.byPrefix` on
  `tabId.startsWith(`${workspaceId}:`) && paneId.startsWith(`${workspaceId}:`)`
  before upserting; keep `writeTabAnchors` as-is (a `writeTabAnchors` caller that
  passes an explicit map keeps full control).
- Tests in `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.test.ts` (persistence describe
  block) for AC2–AC6.

**Key Files:**
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.persistence.ts` — the prune rule.
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.test.ts` — persistence tests.

## Dependencies

- `Test: pin healthy anchor paths` (tests first).
- `Validate persisted workspace on read and re-provision` (AC4's post-recovery
  assertion runs through the recovery path).

## Out of scope

- Purging dead entries for workspaces that are still alive (only id-membership
  pruning is in scope here).
- Any TTL/reaper job; recovery remains on-read validation.

## Impact

After a workspace recovery, rewriting the per-prefix tab-anchor map now prunes
entries owned by the dead workspace, so stale ids can no longer accumulate and
the persisted map truthfully reflects where dispatches land.
data.title: Prune stale prefix entries when rewriting the tab-anchor map

data.description:
## Goal

Make a genuine `anchor-unavailable` refusal **diagnosable from the log alone**:
carry a machine-readable detail naming the failing boundary (persisted workspace
missing vs unreadable herdr vs item-tab unavailable …) from the placement
resolver through to the `no-dispatch` decision entry.

Parent: WL-0MWH50EN4007C6YH (parent AC6; parent "Proposed fix B").

## Context

`resolveDispatchPlacement` collapses every failure into `{ ok: false }`, and
`abortForAnchorUnavailable` records the flat reason `anchor-unavailable`. In the
reported incident the log showed 124 identical `anchor-unavailable` entries with
no way to tell a vanished workspace from a broken CLI — which is a large part of
why the wedge went undiagnosed for hours.

The decision-log entry schema (`CoordinationLogEntry` in
`packages/herdr/src/downtime-log-coordination.ts`) is additive/optional by
convention, so a new optional `detail` field is compatible with every existing
entry shape.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `DispatchPlacementResult`'s failure variant carries
   `detail: PlacementFailureDetail` — a string union of at least
   `persisted-workspace-missing`, `herdr-unreadable`,
   `dispatcher-workspace-unprovisionable`, `prefix-empty`, `item-tab-unavailable`
   (extended by the sibling mismatch item with `project-workspace-mismatch`).
2. The detail is collected from the anchor resolvers without changing their
   existing signatures for current callers — an **optional trailing report
   callback** on `getDispatcherTabAnchor` / `getDispatcherAnchor`
   (additive; callers that pass no callback behave exactly as today), collected
   inside `resolveDispatchPlacement` so no cross-dispatch state is introduced.
3. The recovery outcome from the sibling fix item maps to the detail correctly: a
   workspace observed **missing** that recovers successfully yields `{ok:true}`
   (no detail recorded); a probe that is **unreadable** yields
   `detail: herdr-unreadable`; a persisted workspace positively missing whose
   replacement cannot be provisioned yields
   `dispatcher-workspace-unprovisionable`.
4. `DowntimeDispatchOutcome` for a placement abort carries the detail, and the
   `no-dispatch` decision entry records it (additive `detail?: string` field);
   `reason` stays `anchor-unavailable` so every existing consumer, budget and
   starvation heuristic is unchanged.
5. **Diagnosable refusal (parent AC6).** When placement genuinely fails closed,
   the `anchor-unavailable` decision entry includes a machine-readable detail
   naming the failing boundary (`persisted-workspace-missing` vs
   `herdr-unreadable`), and a test asserts the field is present. The stale-anchor
   state with an unreadable probe records `detail: 'herdr-unreadable'`; the
   prefix-empty and item-tab-unavailable paths each record their own detail.
6. Tests assert `reason` is still `anchor-unavailable` and the claim rollback /
   host-budget release behaviour is byte-for-byte unchanged.
7. No new barrel export, no changed export kind (split guard green), no `wl`
   spawn added.

## Minimal Implementation

- **Barrel-surface constraint (must not be missed).** The split guard asserts
  exactly 38 barrel exports (`expect(exported.size).toBe(38)` in
  `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.split-guard.test.ts`) and the baseline is
  frozen, so `PlacementFailureDetail` must **not** become a new barrel export.
  Declare the string-literal union locally on each side that needs it — a
  family-local alias in `dispatcher-anchor.contract.ts` (not re-exported) and the
  union in `downtime-worker.dispatch-placement.ts` — cross-referenced by comment;
  TypeScript's structural typing makes them assignable where they meet, so no
  consumer imports a non-barrelled symbol (which would also fail the
  "exports every symbol a live consumer imports" gate).
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.contract.ts`: declare the family-local
  detail alias and add the optional report callback parameter to the two resolver
  functions (type-level only; runtime behaviour is unchanged when no callback is
  passed).
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.tab-anchors.ts`: report the boundary at
  each `return null` in `getDispatcherTabAnchor` / `getDispatcherAnchor`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-placement.ts`: create the local
  collector, pass it to the anchor resolvers, return `{ ok: false, detail }`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-claims.ts`: forward the detail
  through `abortForAnchorUnavailable` into the outcome and the decision entry.

## Goal

Make the **primary-path near-miss visible**: when `resolveProjectWorkspace`
cannot match a worklog root but a herdr plugin pane reports a *different*
`HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD`, record a diagnostic naming expected vs actual — and
document the operator remedy — while **leaving the matching rule unchanged**.

Parent: WL-0MWH50EN4007C6YH (parent AC7 and AC8; parent "Proposed fix C").

## Context

`resolveProjectWorkspace` matches on the plugin pane's `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD`
only. The ContextHub "Work Items" pane reports
`HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD=/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/packages/herdr` (the
plugin directory), not the worklog root `/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub`, so:

```
resolveProjectWorkspace('/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub', deps, <same>) -> null
```

Other roots match (AH, RISE, TCE, SA), which is why only ContextHub fell through
to the wedged fallback. Fixing the stale-workspace bug restores dispatch, but
ContextHub panes then land in the `Dispatcher` workspace's `WL` tab rather than
in the ContextHub workspace — an invisible misplacement until it is logged.

### Plan-time decision (recorded)

The parent defers the question "broaden the matching rule?": **the rule stays
unchanged in this item.** Rationale: (a) parent AC8 explicitly makes broadening
conditional on an unambiguous ambiguity resolution, and two panes can legitimately
claim roots related by ancestry (this very project reports
`…/ContextHub/packages/herdr`, whose ancestor is the worklog root), so
ancestor/descendant matching would make ContextHub's own panes ambiguous;
(b) the item's user-visible unblock does not require it; (c) the operator remedy
is cheap and now documented. Broadening, if ever wanted, deserves its own item
with the AC8 ambiguity test.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Primary-path mismatch is visible.** A diagnostic is recorded when
   `resolveProjectWorkspace` fails to match a root whose plugin pane reports a
   different `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD` (naming expected vs actual), and the failure is
   documented in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` with the operator remedy.
2. `resolveProjectWorkspace` reports the near-miss **only** when it returns
   `null` and at least one plugin pane reported a non-empty `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD`
   that differs from the wanted root: the record names the expected root, the
   actual `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD`, and the pane/workspace ids. Reporting is additive
   (an optional report callback or equivalent), so every existing caller and test
   is untouched.
3. No diagnostic is emitted when a match **is** found, or when the panes carry no
   `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD` at all (an absent env is not a mismatch).
4. `resolveDispatchPlacement` records the mismatch as a `project-workspace-mismatch`
   diagnostic detail on the decision entry (expected vs actual), visible even when
   the fallback subsequently succeeds — i.e. a successful fallback placement still
   logs the mismatch.
5. **Matching rule unchanged unless unambiguous (parent AC8).**
   `resolveProjectWorkspace`'s match semantics are unchanged in this item: no
   ancestor/descendant or prefix matching is added, the existing ambiguity rules
   (two panes claiming the same root resolve deterministically — focused first,
   then lowest pane id) still hold, and every existing
   `resolveProjectWorkspace` test stays green with no behavioural change.
6. `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.placement.ts`'s doc comment states the
   rule is exact-root only, and that the reporting is diagnostic-only.
7. No new barrel export, no export-kind change (split guard green).

## Minimal Implementation

- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.placement.ts`: collect per-pane
  `{ expectedRoot, actualRoot, paneId, workspaceId }` near-misses while scanning
  candidates; report them when returning `null` (via the optional callback added
  to the resolver signature); keep the match logic byte-for-byte identical.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-placement.ts`: forward the
  mismatch record into the decision detail (`project-workspace-mismatch`),
  including when the Dispatcher fallback then succeeds.
- Tests: near-miss produces the record; a matched root produces none;
  missing-env produces none; existing ambiguity tests unchanged.

**Key Files:**
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.placement.ts` — near-miss reporting.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-placement.ts` — record forwarding.
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.test.ts` — resolver diagnostics tests.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch.test.ts` — decision-entry test.

## Dependencies

- `Diagnosable anchor-unavailable refusal` (shares the placement-detail plumbing).

## Out of scope

- Any change to the matching rule, including ancestor/descendant matching
  (recorded plan-time decision above).
- Changing `send-to-pi.sh` or the project-workspace tab placement policy.

# Intake Brief — Adopt-or-clean: orphaned Dispatcher workspaces accumulate per herdr restart (WL-0MWHD0V41007ESWR)

> **Headline:** Recovery adopts a dormant `Dispatcher` workspace instead of provisioning a
> fresh one, and the existing ~30 orphans get a documented safe cleanup — so the herdr
> workspace list stops accumulating one husk per restart.

## Problem statement

Every herdr restart / recovery invalidates the persisted Dispatcher workspace id, so
`ensureDispatcherWorkspace` / `getDispatcherAnchor` provision a **fresh** `Dispatcher`
workspace and the previous one is left behind with its `WL` tab and (often) its panes.
Measured live (2026-11-15): **35 workspaces, 30 labelled `Dispatcher`** (w6C–w76), almost
all dormant 2-pane husks (dead root pane + done dispatch pane). This is workspace
**accumulation** — not the stale-anchor wedge of WL-0MWH50EN4007C6YH and not a TTL/reaper
(an explicit non-goal). The herdr workspace list is becoming noisy, and the growth is
unbounded without either adoption or operator cleanup.

## Users

- **Operator / producer** — runs herdr 0.9.x with the downtime dispatcher. Wants the
  workspace list to stay usable without manual housekeeping after every restart.
  - *As an operator, I want recovery to prefer an existing dormant `Dispatcher` workspace
    so restarts stop adding one husk per restart.*
  - *As an operator, I want a documented, safe procedure for clearing the ~30 already-orphaned
    workspaces, so I can reclaim them without disturbing a live dispatch.*

## Decision (RECORDED — producer answered 2026-11-15)

**Adopt going forward + document backlog cleanup (both).** The recovery path prefers an
existing dormant `Dispatcher` workspace (deterministic oldest-id pick among candidates
with no live dispatch pane) instead of always provisioning a fresh one, **and**
`docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` gets a safe procedure for the existing ~30 orphans.
Adoption stops future growth at the source; docs handle the already-accumulated backlog.
Decisions: Q1 = both; Q2 = oldest-id pick among no-live-dispatch-pane candidates,
provision fresh only when no clean candidate or herdr unreadable (fail-closed); Q3 = no
hard threshold — any unbounded growth is unacceptable.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Decision recorded** — the adopt-an-existing + operator-cleanup decision, its
   rationale, and the safety rule are stated in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`.
2. **Adoption on recovery:** when the persisted Dispatcher workspace id is missing/dead,
   the recovery path prefers an existing dormant `Dispatcher`-labelled workspace —
   deterministic pick (the lowest workspace id) among candidates with **no live dispatch
   pane** (no pane labelled `Downtime triggered …` with a live agent session) — and
   provisions a fresh workspace only when no clean candidate exists. The ambiguity rule
   is unit-tested (≥2 dormant candidates pick deterministically; a live-pane candidate
   is excluded; an unreadable pane probe excludes its candidate and never guesses).
3. **Backlog cleanup docs:** `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` documents how to identify
   and safely close the existing orphaned Dispatcher workspaces (`herdr workspace close`
   one at a time, skip workspaces with a live `Downtime triggered …` pane), superseding
   the current single-sentence "duplicates are harmless" note.
4. **No new TTL/reaper** — recovery remains on-read validation (WL-0MWH50EN4007C6YH
   non-goal); this item adds no age-based reaper and no automatic workspace deletion.
5. **No regression, full suite green** — the stale-anchor self-heal
   (WL-0MWH50EN4007C6YH AC1/AC3), the fail-closed `unreadable` path, and the
   no-duplicate-workspace concurrency guard remain green; the full project test suite
   passes with the new changes, and all related documentation (code comments, README,
   wiki/docs site entries) is updated to reflect the changes.

## Impact

A herdr restart no longer leaves a new orphaned `Dispatcher` workspace behind, and the
already-accumulated orphans get a documented safe cleanup path — the workspace list stops
growing and stays usable without manual housekeeping.

## Constraints

- **No TTL / age-based reaper** for anchor files or workspaces (parent non-goal; recovery
  is on-read validation only). An adopted/dormant workspace is reused because the thing it
  points at is *dead*, not because it is *old*.
- **Never disturb a live dispatch pane** — a candidate workspace is adoptable only when no
  pane in it is a live `Downtime triggered …` session (same liveness semantics the
  anchor code already uses, `isPaneAlive`).
- **Fail-closed on unreadable herdr** — an unreadable `workspace list`/pane probe must
  keep today's fail-closed behaviour (provision nothing, `anchor-unavailable`), never
  guess.
- **No new barrel exports** — the split guard freezes the 38-symbol public surface
  (WL-0MWHCUPGQ001FASL precedent: inline literal-union dep members, module-local helpers).
- **Deterministic selection** with ≥2 candidates — "unambiguous" cannot mean "exactly one
  candidate" once 30 orphans exist; the rule must pick deterministically (recommended:
  lowest workspace id) among *dormant* candidates, or provision fresh.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Adopting carries a dead root pane forward.** An adopted husk keeps its dead root
  pane (tab `1`) and done dispatch panes; they are inert but never auto-closed (no
  reaper). Acceptable: the listener stays quiet until dispatch writes into it. Mitigation
  guardrail: only workspaces with no live dispatch pane are adoptable.
- **Sequencing dependency.** Adoption reuses the parent's workspace-list probe
  (`WL-0MWHCUPGQ001FASL`); this item must land after it (Blocked-by) or carry its own
  probe — implementer must not duplicate the probe.
- **Scope-creep risk: an automated reaper looks tempting.** Recording extra opportunities
  as linked work items, not scope: an age-based workspace reaper is explicitly a non-goal
  (AC4); auto-closing abandoned root panes inside adopted husks is a possible follow-on
  but out of scope here.
- **Assumptions:** herdr workspace labels are stable across restarts (verified live:
  30/35 workspaces labelled `Dispatcher`); `herdr workspace list` id-membership is a
  reliable positivity signal for adoption candidates (same mechanism the parent probe
  uses); pane liveness semantics (`isPaneAlive` + `Downtime triggered …` label) reliably
  distinguish dormant husks from a live dispatch workspace.

## Existing state

- `ensureDispatcherWorkspace` (tab-anchors.ts) returns the persisted id verbatim, no
  existence check; `getDispatcherAnchor` re-provisions a fresh workspace under the
  coordination lock when the persisted pane is dead. Each restart → +1 `Dispatcher` husk.
- Live evidence (2026-11-15): 35 workspaces, 30 `Dispatcher`; orphans are uniform
  2-pane/2-tab husks (tab `1` dead root pane + tab `WL` done dispatch pane); the live
  workspace (w76) has 21 panes; anchors currently point at w76.
- Docs today: single sentence "Duplicate `Dispatcher` workspaces are harmless — the
  persisted anchor file is the authority, not the label count; close surplus idle ones one
  at a time without disturbing active `Downtime triggered …` panes."

## Desired change

On the recovery path (persisted Dispatcher workspace missing/dead), instead of always
`createWorkspace("Dispatcher")`:

1. Read the workspace list once (the same read the parent's existence probe issues —
   WL-0MWHCUPGQ001FASL) and collect workspaces with label exactly `Dispatcher`.
2. Filter to *dormant* candidates — deterministically verifiable: `pane list` per candidate
   shows no live dispatch pane (best-effort; a probe failure excludes the candidate).
3. Pick the deterministic candidate (oldest id) and rewrite the anchors to it; the normal
   tab-anchor fast path then finds-or-creates the per-prefix tab inside it.
4. No clean candidate (or unreadable herdr) → fall back to today's fresh provisioning /
   fail-closed behaviour unchanged.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.tab-anchors.ts` — `ensureDispatcherWorkspace` /
  `getDispatcherAnchor` / `getDispatcherTabAnchor` (fresh-provision path to make
  adoption-aware; reuses the coordination lock + in-lock double-check).
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.herdr-cli.ts` — workspace list / pane-list CLI
  helpers (the parent's `probeWorkspace` wiring lands here via WL-0MWHCUPGQ001FASL).
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.contract.ts` — optional dep members for the
  dormant-candidate scan (inline literal unions, no new barrel export).
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.test.ts` — adoption-eligibility tests: dormant
  candidate adopted deterministically, live-pane candidate excluded, unreadable probe →
  provision fresh, concurrency single-provision guard.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — placement/anchor docs: adoption rule + backlog
  cleanup procedure (supersedes the "duplicates are harmless" note).

## Related work

- `WL-0MWH50EN4007C6YH` — parent: stale-anchor wedge self-heal (validate on read,
  re-provision); source of this follow-on and of the workspace-existence probe this item
  builds on. This item must sequence after the probe child (`WL-0MWHCUPGQ001FASL`).
- `WL-0MWHCUPGQ001FASL` — workspace existence probe (alive / missing / unreadable); the
  workspace-list read is shared with the adoption scan.
- `WL-0MUJMXVPO0016DZM` — pane-triage skill (approval-gated pane cleanup precedent; pane
  closure, not workspace closure — complementary).
- `WL-0MU308WSF0002JWN` — auto-close of completed dispatch panes (why orphans are
  pane-light 2-pane husks; the workspace itself is never closed).
- `WL-0MU2EOHK900425VU` — root-pane adoption into a tab ("useless pane"); explains the
  consistent tab-`1` + tab-`WL` orphan shape.
- `WL-0MTRQT482001SNXC` — per-prefix Dispatcher tabs (the resolver family touched here).

**Duplicate-work detection performed** (2026-11-15): `wl search` over
`herdr workspace` / `dispatcher workspace` / `orphan workspace cleanup` found no
overlapping item whose ACs are fully satisfied by this one — the nearest completed items
(pane-triage WL-0MUJMXVPO0016DZM, auto-close WL-0MU308WSF0002JWN) are pane-level and
complementary, not workspace-level adoption/cleanup. No duplicate closed.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Adopt an existing dormant Dispatcher workspace on recovery, or accept accumulation
  and document operator cleanup only — or both?" —
  **Answer (producer, 2026-11-15):** "Both." Source: interactive reply to
  `WL-C0MWHPY4P5001G1K9`. Final: adoption stops future growth; docs cover the ~30
  existing orphans. Research: live `herdr workspace list` shows 30/35 `Dispatcher` and
  growing (evidence recorded in the brief; repo search of the dispatcher-anchor family
  confirms fresh `createWorkspace` on every recovery, no reuse path exists today).
- Q: "How should 'adoptable candidate' be defined once 30 orphans exist (exactly-one
  candidate is never true)?" —
  **Answer (producer, 2026-11-15):** "As recommended." Final: deterministic
  lowest-workspace-id pick among candidates with **no live dispatch pane** (pane list;
  dormant husks are 2-pane vs 21-pane live workspace w76); fresh provision only when no
  clean candidate or herdr unreadable (fail-closed). Research: verified the orphan shape
  live (`w6H` = tab `1` dead root pane + tab `WL` done dispatch pane, 2 panes total) and
  that `herdr workspace close <id>` is the available closure CLI.
- Q: "How many orphaned Dispatcher workspaces are acceptable before the workspace list is
  'unusable'?" —
  **Answer (producer, 2026-11-15):** "As recommended." Final: any unbounded growth is
  unacceptable — adoption required; no hard threshold (30/35 is already visible noise).
  Research: live list evidence recorded above; a threshold would only defer the same
  decision.

(Research summary: inspected the live herdr workspace/tab/pane lists, the anchor files
(`~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-dispatch-{anchor,tab-anchors}.json` → w76), the
dispatcher-anchor code family, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` placement/anchor
sections, the parent item's plan/decisions (WL-0MWH50EN4007C6YH), the probe child
(WL-0MWHCUPGQ001FASL), and the pane-triage/auto-close precedents.)

Parent: WL-0MW8G1X3V007CGAE (Full-suite runs in an existing checkout silently use a stale @worklog/shared build).

## Goal

Encode, **before the guard exists**, the regression contracts for a shared-build freshness check that runs once per test invocation: stale build, fresh build, missing build, no discoverable repository root, and linked-worktree resolution. This is the test-first slice of the parent item (parent AC4).

## Scope

One unit suite, `tests/unit/shared-dist-freshness.test.ts`, driven entirely by temp-dir fixtures whose mtimes the test sets explicitly (mirroring `tests/unit/startup-target-freshness.test.ts`). No test may read this checkout's real `packages/shared`.

The suite targets the guard API the next child introduces: an injectable function that returns `null` when the run may proceed, or the actionable diagnostic string otherwise. Red-first evidence is collected by running the suite before the guard module exists.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `tests/unit/shared-dist-freshness.test.ts` exists and builds every fixture in a temp directory with explicit `fs.utimesSync` mtimes, so assertions never depend on the real checkout's build state.
- Regression coverage in unit tests with temporary fixtures whose mtimes the test controls covers stale, fresh (equal mtimes), missing-dist, no-repo-root and worktree-resolution cases; the stale fixture is asserted red-first so the guard cannot pass vacuously (parent AC4).
- The five cases are exercised explicitly: stale (newest shared source mtime newer than the resolved build artefact), fresh (equal mtimes), missing `dist/`, no discoverable repository root, and linked-worktree resolution (the resolved package is the main checkout's, not a worktree-local mirror).
- The stale case asserts the diagnostic names the resolved `packages/shared` directory, the stale artefact mtime versus the newest source mtime, and the exact `npm run build:shared` rebuild command from that repository root.
- The missing-build case asserts the same actionable failure shape and does not expect a raw `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`.
- The no-repository-root case asserts the guard returns `null` (silent, fail-open) and never a false failure.
- The worktree case asserts the guard judges the resolved (main checkout) package rather than a worktree-local `packages/shared`, pinning the mirror-image false positive.
- Red-first evidence is recorded on this work item: the suite run against the absent guard fails, and the stale assertion is shown not to pass vacuously.

**Key Files:**

- `tests/unit/shared-dist-freshness.test.ts` — new suite with controlled-mtime fixtures.
- `tests/unit/startup-target-freshness.test.ts` — fixture and mtime pattern to mirror.
- `./vitest.config.ts` — test discovery context (no change in this item).

## Test-first note

This item must merge before the guard implementation item; the guard item's acceptance requires this suite to turn green.

Parent: WL-0MW8G1X3V007CGAE.

## Goal

Provide the pure, injectable guard that decides whether the `@worklog/shared` build a run actually loads is at least as new as the newest shared source file, returning either `null` (proceed) or one actionable diagnostic naming the resolved directory, the mtimes, and the rebuild command.

## Scope

Implements parent AC1–AC3 at the helper level and turns the red-first suite from the sibling test item green. Resolution must mirror runtime module resolution (`node_modules/@worklog/shared`), not assumptions about the checkout layout. The repository root named in the message is derived from the resolved shared package (its `packages/` parent), so a linked worktree names the main checkout that owns the build.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The guard resolves the `@worklog/shared` build through `node_modules/@worklog/shared` (following symlinks), so freshness is judged on the package the run actually loads and never on a worktree-local `packages/shared` mirror (parent AC2).
- The repository root used in the rebuild command is derived from the resolved shared package location, so a linked-worktree run names the owning checkout's `npm run build:shared`.
- Stale output returns one message naming the resolved `packages/shared` directory, the stale artefact's mtime versus the newest shared source mtime, and the exact rebuild command `npm run build:shared` from that repository root (parent AC1).
- Missing build output (`packages/shared/dist` absent) produces the same actionable failure instead of a raw `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` from the first `@worklog/shared` import; when no repository root can be discovered the guard stays silent (fail-open, never a false failure) (parent AC3).
- An unresolvable package or an unreadable directory also degrades to `null` — silent and fail-open, never a false failure.
- Equal mtimes count as fresh, and generated or declaration files are excluded consistently with `isDistFresh`'s documented exclusion rule, or their irrelevance is justified in a code comment.
- The sibling suite `tests/unit/shared-dist-freshness.test.ts` passes green, and `tests/unit/startup-target-freshness.test.ts` plus `isDistFresh`'s contract remain unchanged.
- A code comment states the mtime heuristic's trade-off (a branch switch or restored file can produce a false positive that costs one `npm run build:shared`) and that content hashing is deliberately out of scope.

**Key Files:**

- `tests/shared-dist-guard.ts` — new guard helper module.
- `bench/wl-startup-perf.ts` — `newestMtimeMs()` / `isDistFresh()` precedent; do not change its contract.
- `src/cli.ts` — `sharedDistPreflight()` resolution-mirroring and diagnostic wording precedent.
- `tests/unit/shared-dist-freshness.test.ts` — the suite this item turns green.

## Depends on

The red-first unit-test sibling must land first.

Wire the shared-build freshness guard into every vitest invocation via `globalSetup`, so a run whose resolved `@worklog/shared` build is stale or missing aborts **before any test file executes**, with the actionable message and no side effects.

## Scope

This is the vertical slice that makes the guard observable end-to-end: configuration + runtime behaviour + verification evidence. It depends on the guard helper. The guard must run exactly once per invocation (`globalSetup`), never per test file (`setupFiles`), so it adds no filesystem walk to the 344 per-file setups.

- The guard performs no writes to the checkout: no implicit rebuild, and the working tree is unchanged after it fires.
- A fresh build proceeds silently, and an unresolvable package or undiscoverable repository root proceeds silently (no false positive) (parent AC3).
- The full project test suite passes with the guard wired in, after a legitimate `npm run build:shared` precondition; the verification run is recorded on this work item (parent AC7).
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (parent AC7).
