# Refactor dispatched pane creation (WL-0MWHUMOHJ006ZMBQ)

## Headline

Technical debt has accumulated across the dispatched-pane creation and management code: multiple parallel paths for discovering, creating and managing panes owned by dispatched processes. Review all paths, catalogue duplication/unification opportunities, and create one child work item per opportunity found, accommodating the naming needs of open in-flight items — stopping at review + child creation (no implementation in this epic).

## Problem statement

Dispatched panes (downtime dispatch, interactive dispatch, scheduled prompts, ship, fetcher, and their lifecycle management) are created and managed through several overlapping code paths that have drifted apart — e.g. two send-to-pi.sh argv builders with divergent option handling, three placement strategies for workspace/tab anchors, and fragmented pane-discovery/close logic. This makes maintenance riskier and each new pane feature touches many files.

## Users

- **ContextHub maintainers** — the primary users. They extend pane behaviour (naming, placement, lifecycle) and pay the cost of duplicated, drifted code.
- **Operators relying on the downtime dispatcher** — indirectly benefit: fewer pane-related regressions and a consistent naming scheme for workspaces, tabs and panes.

Example user stories:

- As a maintainer, I want one canonical send-to-pi.sh / run-in-pane.sh argv builder so a new pane flag (e.g. `--local-preference`) is added once and applied everywhere.
- As a maintainer, I want the pane-discovery and close logic unified so a span of behaviour change (e.g. the hydrator evidence fix) touches one module instead of four.
- As a maintainer, I want the naming scheme of workspaces, tabs and panes coherent with the open work items (e.g. `Ship` tab, `Dispatcher` workspace adopt-or-clean) so no future item needs to re-plumb naming.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — Review covers ALL pane spawn/management paths: downtime dispatcher (`downtime-worker.pane.ts`), interactive dispatch (`index.commands.ts` → `send-to-pi.sh` / `run-in-pane.sh`), scheduled prompts, ship-in-own-pane, fetcher spawns, anchor/placement (`dispatcher-anchor*.ts`), lifecycle/close (`pane-lifecycle.ts`, `pane-close*.ts`), and pane-capture (`index.pane-capture.ts`). Documented in the epic description.
- AC2 — At least one child work item per refactoring opportunity identified (duplication, configuration unification, code reuse, other smells), each under this epic with issue type and priority assigned: `critical` for items with significant maintenance impact, appropriate priority otherwise.
- AC3 — The review explicitly accommodates the naming/placement needs of open in-flight work items (WL-0MWH56SWX004HSKQ, WL-0MWHD0V41007ESWR, WL-0MW6FIZYI0003QEU, WL-0MWHBSTM1004KQ49, WL-0MWAM5N75004ROSW) — recorded in the relevant child descriptions.
- AC4 — Each child work item has a clear goal, testable ACs and predicted key files; children reference the specific code locations duplicated/drifted.
- AC5 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- AC6 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (no behaviour change outside the refactoring).

## Impact

Maintainers can extend pane behaviour through fewer, unified code paths with a consistent workspace/tab/pane naming scheme, instead of patching several drifted implementations.

## Constraints

- Epic stops at review + child creation — no implementation in this epic; children implemented in their own sessions (operator decision).
- No behaviour change: refactoring must be behaviour-preserving; each child must keep the full test suite green.
- "Critical path" means `--priority critical` on high-maintenance-impact items, appropriate priority otherwise (operator decision).
- Scope is all pane spawn/management paths (operator decision).
- Respect repository boundaries: don't edit `.pi/`, `skill/`, `command/` or agent-infrastructure dirs.
- Work must happen in the implement-skill worktree lifecycle (per child).

## Existing state

- `downtime-worker.pane.ts` — downtime pane identity, in-flight resolution, spawn invocation (via `send-to-pi.sh`) and lifecycle monitor. Contains `buildDowntimePaneArgs` and `spawnDowntimePane`.
- `index.commands.ts` — command routing + `buildSendToPiArgs` / `buildRunInPaneArgs` (agent and shell pane argv for `send-to-pi.sh` / `run-in-pane.sh`).
- `dispatcher-anchor*.ts` — three placement strategies (project workspace + item-ID tab; per-prefix tab in Dispatcher workspace; machine-wide Dispatcher fallback) + CLI parsers, persistence, herdr-cli subprocess helpers.
- `pane-lifecycle.ts`, `pane-close.ts`, `pane-close-cli.ts`, `pane-close-herdr.ts`, `pane-close-reaper.ts`, `pane-close-scheduler.ts` — pane lifecycle monitoring and close/reap paths.
- `index.pane-capture.ts` — pane-ID file capture and work-item ↔ pane association.
- `pane-title.ts` — shared pane-title builders (the exemplar of the desired unified pattern).
- `fetcher.cli.ts` — `wl` CLI spawn management with spawn cap (execFile, not send-to-pi.sh).

## Desired change

A documented map of all pane paths plus a set of child work items that, once implemented, converge the duplicated/divergent code onto shared builders/helpers (mirroring the `pane-title.ts` pattern) and a coherent naming scheme — without changing runtime behaviour.

## Key Files:

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.pane.ts` — downtime spawn args/options + lifecycle monitor
- `packages/herdr/src/index.commands.ts` — interactive agent/shell pane argv builders
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor*.ts` — placement strategies, anchors, parsers, persistence
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-lifecycle.ts` — dispatched-pane lifecycle classification
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-close*.ts` — close/reap/CLI paths
- `packages/herdr/src/index.pane-capture.ts` — pane-ID capture
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-title.ts` — canonical title builders (pattern to extend)
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.cli.ts` — wl spawn management (potential unification target)

## Related work

- WL-0MWH56SWX004HSKQ — Hydrator releases a live dispatch claim seconds after spawn (open) — pane evidence workspace scope.
- WL-0MWHD0V41007ESWR — Adopt-or-clean: orphaned Dispatcher workspaces (open) — naming/placement of the Dispatcher workspace.
- WL-0MW6FIZYI0003QEU — Ship opens in own pane (open) — new pane-spawn path + `Ship` tab naming.
- WL-0MWHBSTM1004KQ49 — Test: prep-tier pane-only busy contract (open) — dispatched-pane busy semantics.
- WL-0MWAM5N75004ROSW — Host-wide release barrier (open) — dispatch pause across roots.
- Completed: WL-0MU2EOHK900425VU, WL-0MU7JZE04008VKP0, WL-0MTR01EU7005SYZG, WL-0MTR2CD4X006XI7U, WL-0MTRQT482001SNXC, WL-0MU308WSF0002JWN, WL-0MU4URK4H006OFCE, WL-0MUKXFVMS001BP68, WL-0MUMA5OMH0024PN1, WL-0MUBVKXQJ000L8EO, WL-0MW5JE0SZ0057K30 — prior dispatched-pane evolution.

## Risks & assumptions

- Scope-creep risk: the review may surface many small opportunities; record extra opportunities as additional child work items (or note them in a comment), not as scope of the epic.
- Assumption: refactoring children are behaviour-preserving; each child must keep the full test suite green (implement-skill gate).
- Assumption: "all paths" review may find paths the description did not anticipate (e.g. fetcher execFile spawns); these are in scope per Q1-A.
- Risk: open in-flight items (WL-0MWH56SWX004HSKQ et al.) change the pane landscape while children are being implemented; each child should pin which naming/placement contract it targets so the open items' needs are accommodated rather than re-litigated.
- Risk: a child that unifies argv builders may introduce subtle option-order or env differences; each such child must pin the exact argv/env delta with tests.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Which pane paths are in scope for the review?" — Answer (operator, interactive): "A) All pane spawn/management paths — downtime dispatcher, interactive dispatch, scheduled prompts, fetcher, ship, pane-close/reaper/lifecycle." Source: interactive reply (round 1).
- Q2: "After identifying opportunities and creating child work items, does this epic also implement any children?" — Answer (operator, interactive): "A) Stops at review + child creation; children implemented in their own sessions." Source: interactive reply (round 1).
- Q3: "Does 'critical path' mean `--priority critical`?" — Answer (operator, interactive): "A) Yes — priority=critical for high-maintenance-impact items, appropriate priority for the rest." Source: interactive reply (round 1).


## Review map (AC1 — all pane spawn/management paths reviewed)

Reviewed 2026-11-15 across `packages/herdr/src` and `packages/herdr/{shared,scripts}`. Every path below was read and its duplication/drift catalogued; each opportunity maps to a child work item (AC2).

| Path | Modules | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Downtime dispatcher spawn | `downtime-worker.pane.ts` (`buildDowntimePaneArgs`, `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions`, `spawnDowntimePane`) | Drifted argv builder vs interactive; spawn env owns scrub+knobs alone. → argv child |
| Interactive dispatch | `index.commands.ts` (`buildSendToPiArgs`, `buildRunInPaneArgs`), `index.ts` call sites | Second/third independent argv builders, divergent flag sets. → argv child |
| Scheduled prompts | `scheduled-prompts.ts` + downtime spawn path (via `buildDowntimePaneArgs`) | Shares downtime builder — covered by argv child |
| Ship-in-own-pane | `WL-0MW6FIZYI0003QEU` (in-flight, plan_complete) | New `Ship`-tab spawn path; naming needs recorded in anchor + docs children |
| Anchor/placement | `dispatcher-anchor*.ts`, `downtime-worker.dispatch-placement.ts` (`resolveDispatchPlacement`) | Three strategies with parallel provision-under-lock; live-pane-conditional primary path (traced root cause). → deterministic-placement (WL-0MWHW3PKX0048ZYL) + anchor child |
| Fetcher spawns | `fetcher.cli.ts` (`runWl`), `fetcher.args.ts` | Third subprocess seam (execFile); duplicates binary-probe/error seams. → fetcher child |
| Pane lifecycle/close | `pane-lifecycle.ts` (disabled Mechanism B), `pane-close.ts` (shared classifier), `pane-close-herdr/reaper/cli/scheduler.ts` | Fragmented discovery + two close paths (one disabled, race documented). → discovery child |
| Pane capture | `index.pane-capture.ts`, `parsePaneIdFile` (`index.commands.ts`) | Single implementation — no duplication found (noted, no child) |
| Pane title | `pane-title.ts` | The canonical unified pattern the children should mirror |
| Label parsing | `paneLabelItemId` (×2) + `paneItemIdFromLabel` + `extractWorkItemIdsFromText` | Four graders, three semantics. → label child |

## Plan: children (updates)

- **WL-0MWHWGN23001KMQW** — Test: pin dispatched-pane spawn argv/env/placement behaviour (test-first gate for all unification children).
- **WL-0MWHW3PKX0048ZYL** — Deterministic project-workspace placement without live-pane dependency (folded in from the design-trace session; operator decision: "We want only one. Created in the same work tree." — an explicit placement behaviour change).
- **WL-0MWHWGZI4007D911** — Unify send-to-pi.sh / run-in-pane.sh argv builders (critical — significant maintenance impact).
- **WL-0MWHWH1HV009C46C** — Unify pane-label item-ID and kind parsing.
- **WL-0MWHWH6XL0025YX2** — Unify dispatched-pane discovery and close logic (critical).
- **WL-0MWHWH68L007L7IO** — Unify dispatcher-anchor placement strategies and CLI helpers.
- **WL-0MWHWHB3X004H9VG** — Unify fetch/wl spawn management with pane-close herdr CLI seams.
- **WL-0MWHWHBSW005KG13** — Docs: single pane-creation architecture map and naming contract.

Dependency order (test-first): the pin tests child precedes every unification child; label parsing precedes discovery + fetcher; deterministic placement precedes the anchor strategies child; docs lands last.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-16: AC2 priority gap closed (operator decision, audit finding): WL-0MWHWHB3X004H9VG, WL-0MWHWGZI4007D911 and WL-0MWHWH6XL0025YX2 raised to `--priority critical` — the three children with significant maintenance impact per the plan; every other refactoring child stays `high` and the docs child `medium`. The map table in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md:151-158` was aligned in commit `08eba9812` so the map and the worklog agree.
- 2026-11-16: Audit resume cycle — the in-main-slot child screens for the 15 in-flight children were serviced by the auditing session and each child's own audit persisted (verdicts recorded per child); the parent re-audit collects them through child-verdict reuse (`reused_from`) with no child `pi` calls. Description edited only to record that cycle (audit content fingerprint changes with it).
- 2026-11-16: Idempotent re-dispatch — plan re-verified (tree coverage review: 100% covered, `proceed`; 11 children cover all 6 parent ACs). Stage re-asserted to `plan_complete` after an earlier reset to `intake_complete` had repeatedly re-triggered `/skill:plan` dispatch. No new children created, no questions raised.
- 2026-11-15: Plan skill pass — review map documented (AC1), eight children created/wired (AC2), placement root cause folded in from the design-trace session (herdr-1794749570-1465372-27601 → WL-0MWHW3PKX0048ZYL + epic comment), effort/risk re-estimated.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q4: "Why do some dispatched panes land in the project workspace and others in a separate Dispatcher workspace?" — Answer (operator, interactive, design-trace session herdr-1794749570-1465372-27601): "We want only one. Created in the same work tree." — every dispatched pane must be created in the item's project workspace; the `Dispatcher` fallback becomes a rare, logged last resort. Evidence: traced live 2026-11-15 (ContextHub dispatches 01:18–08:29Z → Dispatcher workspaces while no plugin pane advertised the root; 13:25/13:29Z → project workspace after the w77:p2 plugin pane started 12:41Z). Recorded in WL-0MWHW3PKX0048ZYL. This supersedes the epic's generic "no behaviour change" constraint **for the placement scope only**; all other children remain behaviour-preserving.
- Q5: "How should the review catalogue opportunities without scope-creeping?" — Answer (plan, from epic risks): record every surfaced opportunity as a child under this epic (per AC2), or as a comment when trivial; no implementation in this epic (Q2).

# Deterministic project-workspace pane placement without live-pane dependency

## Headline

Dispatched panes land in the item's project workspace **only while a live herdr
`Work Items` plugin pane advertises the worklog root** via `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD`
(read from `/proc/<shell_pid>/environ`). When that advertisement is absent at
dispatch time, `resolveProjectWorkspace` fails closed (`null`) and the pane falls
back to a per-prefix tab in a `Dispatcher` workspace — producing the two observed
placement behaviours ("created in the same worktree" vs "separate dispatch
worktree"). Unify placement so **every** dispatched pane is created in the item's
project workspace, deterministically, from durable data rather than live-pane
`/proc` scraping.

## Problem statement (traced 2026-11-15, session `herdr-1794749570-1465372-27601`)

The placement precedence in `downtime-worker.dispatch-placement.ts`
(`resolveDispatchPlacement`) already prefers the project workspace:

1. **Primary** — `resolveProjectWorkspace` (`dispatcher-anchor.placement.ts`)
   enumerates machine-wide panes, keeps only `label == 'Work Items'`, reads each
   candidate's `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD` via `herdr pane process-info` →
   `/proc/<pid>/environ`, and matches it to the item's worklog root. On a match,
   `getItemTabAnchor` ensures the item-ID tab in that workspace.
2. **Fallback** — per-prefix tab (`WL`/`AH`/…) in a `Dispatcher` workspace
   (`getDispatcherTabAnchor`).
3. **Retained legacy** — the single persisted `Dispatcher` anchor
   (`downtime-dispatch-anchor.json`).

Step 1 is **conditional on a live plugin pane advertising the root**. It fails
closed to `null` on any of: no `Work Items` pane carrying `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD ==
root` at dispatch time, an unreadable `/proc` env, a missing `shell_pid`, a CLI
failure, a match without a workspace id. Every such failure silently produces
behaviour 2 — a pane in a separate `Dispatcher` workspace whose `cwd` is still the
project root.

**Live evidence (ContextHub worklog, `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`):**

- ContextHub-root dispatches 2026-11-15 **01:18–08:29Z** all landed in
  `Dispatcher` workspaces: `w6C:p3`, `w6D:p3`, `w6V:p3`, `w60:p3`, `w71:p3`,
  `w72:p3`, `w76:p5` — while no ContextHub plugin pane was alive.
- The current ContextHub `Work Items` pane `w77:p2` started **12:41:01Z** with
  `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD=/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub`.
- ContextHub-root dispatches after that (13:25Z → `w77:p6`, 13:29Z → `w77:p8`)
  landed in the ContextHub workspace item-ID tab `w77:t5` — the "same worktree".
- AI Hell items consistently land in AI Hell item tabs (`w50:t44`, `w50:t4H`)
  because that plugin pane (`w50:p8P`) has been up since 2026-11-14 23:29Z.

Root cause of the split: the same root may be advertised or not at any given
dispatch time, and fallback-placed panes stay open — so both behaviours coexist
in one pane grid.

**Registered-root sweep case (structural):** a `downtimeWorklogRoots` swept root
has **no running herdr instance by definition**, so step 1 can never succeed for
it — every swept dispatch is placed in a `Dispatcher` workspace (or fails closed).
A durable mapping fixes this class too.

**Directly affects WL-0MWH56SWX004HSKQ:** the hydrator's demotion-pane evidence is
workspace-scoped, so fallback-placed panes in the `Dispatcher` workspace are
invisible to it (the `w71:p3` implement pane for WL-0MWH56SWX004HSKQ is live
evidence).

## Operator decision (recorded 2026-11-15)

> "We want only one. Created in the same work tree." — every dispatched pane must
> be created in the item's project workspace. This is an **explicit behaviour
> change** for the placement scope and supersedes the epic's generic
> "no behaviour change: refactoring must be behaviour-preserving" constraint for
> this child (the `Dispatcher`-workspace fallback becomes a rare, logged
> last resort, not a routine alternative).

## Naming contract (folded in from WL-0MWHTT2XY005XX3B, producer decision 2026-11-15)

Intake for WL-0MWHTT2XY005XX3B ("Better naming of dispatched items") resolved
with producer answers Q1=(a), Q2=(a), Q3=(a) — the item is covered by this
child and the naming-contract docs child (WL-0MWHWHBSW005KG13) and is closed.
Pinned decisions for this child:

- **"Project ID" = the work-item id prefix** (`WL`, `TCE`, `AH`, `SA`, …) —
  the same value currently used for the `Dispatcher` tabs.
- **One workspace per project** (the project's herdr workspace, identified by
  its project id), **tabs labelled by the full work-item id**, create-or-reuse
  (adopt an existing tab/workspace before creating; never duplicate).
- **Dispatch-created workspaces/tabs only** — existing project workspace labels
  (e.g. `ContextHub`) remain under operator control.
- The machine-wide `Dispatcher` fallback with per-prefix tabs is retired (the
  logged last-resort placement per AC3 remains).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — A dispatched pane for a work item is created in the item's project
  workspace (item-ID tab, existing adopt/reuse semantics) **even when no live
  `Work Items` plugin pane advertises the root at dispatch time** (plugin pane
  down, or a `downtimeWorklogRoots` sweep with no running instance).
- AC2 — root→workspace resolution is derived from a **durable source** (persisted
  per-root workspace map and/or the coordination registry's `worklogRoot`
  entries), not solely from `/proc` env scraping of live panes; the live-pane
  advertisement becomes a fast-path hint, never the only path.
- AC3 — The per-prefix `Dispatcher` fallback is retained only as a last resort
  (documented precedence unchanged) and **every fallback placement is recorded in
  the dispatch log with the reason**, so "separate dispatch worktree" placements
  become observable, rare and attributable.
- AC4 — Deterministic ambiguity: multiple candidate workspaces for one root use
  the existing focused-first then lowest-pane-id rule; adopted/reused item-ID
  tabs behave exactly as today (idempotent, no duplicate tabs).
- AC5 — Full unit + integration suite green; `dispatcher-anchor*.test.ts` and
  `downtime-worker*.test.ts` cover the no-live-pane and swept-root placements.
- AC6 — Naming/placement needs of the open in-flight items are accommodated
  (epic AC3): WL-0MWH56SWX004HSKQ (workspace-scoped demotion evidence),
  WL-0MWHD0V41007ESWR (adopt-or-clean of orphaned `Dispatcher` workspaces),
  WL-0MW6FIZYI0003QEU, WL-0MWHBSTM1004KQ49, WL-0MWAM5N75004ROSW — no expectation
  re-plumbing.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.placement.ts` (`resolveProjectWorkspace`,
  `getItemTabAnchor`)
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.herdr-cli.ts` (`getPaneProcessInfo`,
  `readProcEnvironFile`)
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.contract.ts` (anchor/workspace types)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-placement.ts` (precedence,
  `resolveDispatchPlacement`)
- `packages/herdr/src/machine-coordination.ts` (durable machine-wide state)
- Related: `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.tab-anchors.ts`,
  `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts`

## Related work

- Lineage: WL-0MUR5FUWD00024XN (precedence fix — panes regressed into
  `Dispatcher`), WL-0MU321YK70035AYT (dispatch into project workspace),
  WL-0MUKXFX2M0019E3G, WL-0MWHCV3PR002WSQM (mismatch diagnostic, matching rule
  unchanged), WL-0MWHCUZ5C000I7S6 (anchor-unavailable refusal detail).
- Overlapping open items (not duplicates): WL-0MWHD0V41007ESWR (orphaned
  `Dispatcher` workspace adopt-or-clean — the debris this fallback leaves
  behind), WL-0MWH50EN4007C6YH (stale persisted anchor re-provision),
  WL-0MWH56SWX004HSKQ (hydrator evidence visibility).

## Impact

Operators see exactly one dispatch-pane placement — the item's project workspace —
regardless of which herdr instance is running or when it restarted, with
`Dispatcher`-workspace panes relegated to a rare, logged last resort; the
hydrator's placement evidence (WL-0MWH56SWX004HSKQ) stops losing view of
fallback-placed panes.
data.title: Deterministic project-workspace placement without live-pane dependency

# Test: pin dispatched-pane spawn argv/env/placement behaviour

## Headline

Characterisation tests that pin the **current** behaviour of every dispatched-pane
spawn path — argv builders, spawn env construction, label parsing, discovery
predicates and placement precedence — so each unification child can prove
behaviour preservation by keeping this suite green. Test-first gate for the
epic's refactoring children (WL-0MWHUMOHJ006ZMBQ AC6: full suite green, no
behaviour change outside the refactoring).

## Goal

As a maintainer running a behaviour-preserving refactor of dispatched-pane
creation, I want the exact argv/env/label/placement behaviour pinned by tests
before any unification child changes code, so a subtle option-order, env or
label-parse difference is caught by CI rather than by an operator's pane grid.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — The three argv builders are pinned over their full option matrix with
  byte-exact argv assertions: `buildDowntimePaneArgs`
  (`downtime-worker.pane.ts`), `buildSendToPiArgs` and `buildRunInPaneArgs`
  (`index.commands.ts`) — every optional flag present and absent
  (`--pane-name`, `--focus`/`--no-focus`, `--cwd`, `--model`, `--anchor`,
  `--pane-id-file`, `--request-priority`, `--reservation-ticket`,
  `--local-preference`) and the command/prompt terminal position.
- AC2 — `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions` env is pinned: detached/stdio/cwd,
  `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD`, `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM=1`, priority mapping,
  reservation-ticket and local-preference injection, repository-override env
  scrubbing (`scrubRepositoryOverrides`).
- AC3 — A pivot table documents the *deliberate* divergences between the three
  builders (which flags each supports today and why) so the unification child
  can decide what to converge without guessing intent.
- AC4 — Pane-label parsing is pinned: `paneLabelItemId`
  (`downtime-worker.pane.ts`), `paneItemIdFromLabel` (`pane-close-herdr.ts`),
  the local `paneLabelItemId` (`host-dispatch-budget.repair.ts` — regex-validated
  vs unvalidated suffix parse) and `paneKindFromLabel` — asserting the current
  parse outputs including the regex-validation divergence.
- AC5 — Placement precedence is pinned at the `resolveDispatchPlacement` level:
  project workspace + item-ID tab, per-prefix Dispatcher tab, legacy Dispatcher
  anchor, and the fail-closed `anchor-unavailable` outcome — asserting the
  current behaviour **before** WL-0MWHW3PKX0048ZYL changes it.
- AC6 — Full unit + integration suite green; the pin tests land first (before
  any refactoring child commits).

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.pane.ts` — `buildDowntimePaneArgs`,
  `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions`, `paneLabelItemId`, discovery predicates
- `packages/herdr/src/index.commands.ts` — `buildSendToPiArgs`,
  `buildRunInPaneArgs`
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-close-herdr.ts` — `paneItemIdFromLabel`,
  `paneKindFromLabel`
- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.repair.ts` — local `paneLabelItemId`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-placement.ts` —
  `resolveDispatchPlacement`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.pane-spawn.test.ts`,
  `packages/herdr/src/index.commands.test.ts` (new/extended suites)

## Related work

- Child of WL-0MWHUMOHJ006ZMBQ; prerequisite (dependency) of every unification
  child: WL-0MWHW3PKX0048ZYL (placement), argv-builder unification, label-parse
  unification, discovery/close unification, placement code-reuse.
- Overlap-avoidance: existing `downtime-worker.pane-spawn.test.ts`,
  `downtime-worker.pane.test.ts`, `index.commands.test.ts` already cover pieces

## Impact

Maintainers refactoring dispatched-pane creation now have a green characterisation suite pinning the byte-exact argv, spawn env and label-parse behaviour, so a subtle option-order, env or placement difference is caught by CI instead of arriving in an operator's pane grid.

# Unify send-to-pi.sh / run-in-pane.sh argv builders

## Headline

Collapse the three parallel TS argv builders — `buildDowntimePaneArgs`
(downtime dispatcher), `buildSendToPiArgs` and `buildRunInPaneArgs` (interactive
dispatch / shell panes, `index.commands.ts`) — onto one canonical builder per
script (mirroring the `pane-title.ts` unified pattern), plus one option parser
per shell script (`shared/send-to-pi.sh`, `scripts/run-in-pane.sh`), so a new
pane flag (e.g. `--local-preference`) is added once and applied everywhere.

## Goal

As a ContextHub maintainer, I want one canonical send-to-pi.sh / run-in-pane.sh
argv builder so a new pane flag (`--local-preference`, `--reservation-ticket`,
`--request-priority`, …) is added once and applied to all spawn paths — instead
of the today's drifted option sets (downtime builder carries
reservation-ticket/local-preference; the interactive builder carries
pane-id-file/request-priority; each has a divergent option order).

## Problem statement (drift catalogue, WL-0MWHUMOHJ006ZMBQ)

- `downtime-worker.pane.ts::buildDowntimePaneArgs` — `--pane-name`,
  `--no-focus`, `--anchor`, `--reservation-ticket`, `--local-preference`,
  `--cwd`, `--model`, then prompt.
- `index.commands.ts::buildSendToPiArgs` — `--focus|--no-focus`, `--cwd`,
  `--pane-name`, `--model`, `--pane-id-file`, `--anchor`,
  `--request-priority`, then prompt.
- `index.commands.ts::buildRunInPaneArgs` — `--focus|--no-focus`, `--cwd`,
  `--pane-name`, `--anchor`, `--pane-id-file`, then command.
- Shell-side: `shared/send-to-pi.sh` parses `--pane-name/--focus/--no-focus/
  --resize/--no-resize/--check-cli/--cwd/--anchor/--request-priority/
  --reservation-ticket/--local-preference/--model/--pane-id-file`;
  `scripts/run-in-pane.sh` is an *independent* option parser with a smaller set
  (`--cwd/--focus/--no-focus/--pane-name/--anchor/--pane-id-file`).
  `scripts/send-to-pi.sh` and `scripts/open-pi-agent.sh` are thin wrappers
  (canonical at `shared/`) — the desired pattern.
- Spawn env construction is also split: `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions`
  (`downtime-worker.pane.ts`) owns scrub + knob injection; the interactive path
  has no equivalent builder.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — One canonical argv-builder module (e.g. `pane-argv.ts`, mirroring
  `pane-title.ts`) exports a single builder for `send-to-pi.sh` args and one
  for `run-in-pane.sh` args; `buildDowntimePaneArgs`,
  `buildSendToPiArgs` and `buildRunInPaneArgs` delegate to it (thin
  compatibility wrappers or direct call-site migration — no duplicated option
  assembly left).
- AC2 — The full flag matrix of all three current builders is supported by the
  canonical builders (per the pinned contract, test-first child
  WL-0MWHWGN23001KMQW: option set, order, defaults, env knobs), with a
  documented convergence decision per previously-divergent flag
  (pane-id-file/request-priority/reservation-ticket/local-preference).
- AC3 — `scripts/run-in-pane.sh` shares the canonical option parser (or becomes
  a thin wrapper over a shared `shared/` parser) — no second independent
  option-parsing implementation.
- AC4 — A new pane flag added to `pane-argv.ts` + one shell parser applies to
  every spawn path; the pinned argv/env tests prove byte-identical or
  documented-converged behaviour.
- AC5 — Full unit + integration suite green (split-guard baselines for
  `index.*`/`downtime-worker.*`/`fetcher.*` updated only where the extraction
  legitimately changes the public surface).

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/index.commands.ts` — `buildSendToPiArgs`,
  `buildRunInPaneArgs` (migrate)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.pane.ts` — `buildDowntimePaneArgs`,
  `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions` (migrate)
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-argv.ts` (new canonical module)
- `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh`, `packages/herdr/scripts/run-in-pane.sh`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.pane-spawn.test.ts`,
  `packages/herdr/src/index.commands.test.ts`

## Constraints & assumptions

- Behaviour-preserving refactor: argv/env byte-identical unless a divergence is
  deliberately converged *and* documented (each such change pinned by test).
- Respect `shared/send-to-pi.sh` as canonical; `scripts/*` stay thin wrappers
  where they exist today.


## Convergence decisions (AC2, WL-0MWHWGZI4007D911)

Documented per previously-divergent flag, per the pinned contract
(WL-0MWHWGN23001KMQW AC3 pivot table). Option ORDER is part of the pinned
contract — each builder keeps its byte-exact pre-refactor order.

- **`--pane-id-file`** — interactive send-to-pi.sh (agent commands carrying an
  item id) and run-in-pane.sh (split-confirmation channel) only. Downtime
  dispatch never captures the work-item↔pane association → deliberately absent.
- **`--request-priority`** — send-to-pi.sh only (interactive priority
  threading). Downtime conveys priority via spawn env
  (`HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY`) instead of argv (unchanged); run-in-pane.sh never
  (shell panes schedule no agent work). Deliberately absent from the other
  two builders' vocabulary.
- **`--reservation-ticket` / `--local-preference`** — downtime dispatch only
  (local-capacity reservation / per-turn locality fail-open contracts).
  Interactive panes are never given these → deliberately absent elsewhere.
- **`--model`** — send-to-pi.sh (optional interactive model) and downtime
  (required) only; run-in-pane.sh never (shell panes have no model).
- **focus** — send-to-pi.sh/run-in-pane.sh take `--focus|--no-focus` with
  `--no-focus` the default; downtime always emits `--no-focus` (unattended
  background dispatch is invisible) — unchanged, pinned.
- **Shell-side `--flag=<value>` forms (documented convergence)** — the shared
  option parser (`packages/herdr/shared/pane-options.sh`) accepts BOTH
  `--flag <value>` and `--flag=<value>` in EVERY script. Before this item,
  `run-in-pane.sh` only handled the space-separated form for `--cwd` and
  `--pane-name` (the `=` form fell through into the command); send-to-pi.sh
  already accepted both. The unified parser converges run-in-pane.sh onto the
  canonical forms — pinned by `tests/herdr/run-in-pane-main.test.ts` and
  `packages/herdr/scripts/tests/test_run_in_pane.sh`.
- **Option vocabulary is per-script, never permissive** — the shared parser
  takes an explicit accepts list; a send-to-pi-only flag (e.g. `--model`) is
  NOT parsed by run-in-pane.sh but starts the command (unchanged, pinned).

## Impact

Maintainers add a new pane flag in exactly two places — `pane-argv.ts` (TS argv builders) and `shared/pane-options.sh` (the shell parser) — and every dispatched-pane spawn path (downtime, interactive agent dispatch, shell-output panes) picks it up, instead of patching three drifted builders and two independent option parsers.

# Unify pane-label item-ID and kind parsing

## Headline

Collapse the three parallel pane-label parsers —
`paneLabelItemId` (`downtime-worker.pane.ts`, suffix-only, returns `null`),
`paneItemIdFromLabel` (`pane-close-herdr.ts`, regex-validated, returns `''`) and
the local `paneLabelItemId` (`host-dispatch-budget.repair.ts`, suffix-only) —
onto one canonical label-parsing module so a label-format change (e.g. the
hydrator evidence fix, WL-0MWH56SWX004HSKQ) touches one module instead of four.

## Goal

As a maintainer hardening the dispatched-pane evidence chain, I want one
canonical pane-label parser (item-id extraction + kind classification + label
prefix) so every consumer — downtime worker, reaper, host budget repair,
stalled-work, long-running-panes, ship guard, hydrator — shares identical
parse semantics.

## Problem statement (drift catalogue, WL-0MWHUMOHJ006ZMBQ)

Three item-id-from-label implementations with subtly different semantics:

- `downtime-worker.pane.ts::paneLabelItemId` — token after last ` - `, returns
  `null` when absent/empty; **no** shape validation (accepts any token).
- `pane-close-herdr.ts::paneItemIdFromLabel` — same suffix rule but
  regex-validates `/^[A-Z]{2,}-[A-Z0-9]+$/` and returns `''` when absent.
- `host-dispatch-budget.repair.ts::paneLabelItemId` — local duplication of the
  suffix rule, returns `null`; comments admit "duplicated deliberately".
- Kind parsing: `pane-close-herdr.ts::paneKindFromLabel` (substring match over
  `PANE_KINDS`); `DOWNTIME_PANE_LABEL_PREFIX` matching is repeated at many call
  sites (`dispatch-claims`, `admission`, `stalled-work`, `long-running-panes`).
- ID *sets* in labels: `hydrator.ts::extractWorkItemIdsFromText` (regex over
  full text, used by ship guard) — a fourth parser at different granularity.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — One canonical module (e.g. `pane-label.ts`, mirroring `pane-title.ts`)
  exports: item-id-from-label (single shape/return convention, documented),
  kind-from-label, label-prefix predicate (`isDowntimePaneLabel`) and
  extract-ids-from-text. The three existing implementations delegate to it; the
  local `host-dispatch-budget.repair.ts` copy is removed.
- AC2 — Return-convention divergence (null vs '' vs validated) is settled in
  the canonical API and every consumer updated; the pinned behaviour tests
  (pre-regex-validation on `paneItemIdFromLabel` vs suffix-only on
  `paneLabelItemId`) document which is authoritative and why.
- AC3 — All prefix-matching call sites use the shared predicate — no bare
  `label.startsWith(DOWNTIME_PANE_LABEL_PREFIX)` outside the canonical module.
- AC4 — `extractWorkItemIdsFromText` (hydrator/ship-guard) is either moved into
  the canonical module or documented as intentionally different granularity
  with a shared regex constant.
- AC5 — Full unit + integration suite green; `pane-close-herdr.test.ts`,
  `host-dispatch-budget.repair.test.ts`, hydrator, ship-guard and stalled-work
  suites pin the unified behaviour.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.pane.ts` — `paneLabelItemId`,
  `DOWNTIME_PANE_LABEL_PREFIX`
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-close-herdr.ts` — `paneItemIdFromLabel`,
  `paneKindFromLabel`
- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.repair.ts` — local `paneLabelItemId`
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts` — `extractWorkItemIdsFromText`
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-label.ts` (new canonical module)
- Consumers: `downtime-worker.dispatch-claims.ts`,
  `host-dispatch-budget.admission.ts`, `stalled-work.ts`,
  `long-running-panes.ts`, `ship-guard.ts`

## Constraints & assumptions

- Behaviour-preserving: parse outputs identical (or documented convergence with
  pinned tests). The regex-validation divergence on `paneItemIdFromLabel` is a
  deliberate safety net — decide authoritatively in the canonical API.
- Accommodates WL-0MWH56SWX004HSKQ (hydrator evidence fix must not re-plumb
  label parsing) and WL-0MWHD0V41007ESWR (Dispatcher adopt-or-clean matches
  `Downtime`-labelled panes).

## Impact

Maintainers now change pane-label parsing (work-item id, kind, or prefix matching) in one canonical module instead of chasing four divergent parsers, so a label-format change such as the hydrator evidence fix can no longer drift across the downtime worker, reaper, and budget repair.

# Unify dispatcher-anchor placement strategies and CLI helpers

## Headline

Extract the shared plumbing of the three placement strategies —
project-workspace + item-ID tab (`dispatcher-anchor.placement.ts`), per-prefix
Dispatcher tab and the machine-wide Dispatcher anchor
(`dispatcher-anchor.tab-anchors.ts`) — into a common find-or-provision-under-
coordination-lock helper, and unify the duplicated herdr CLI subprocess/parser
helpers, so naming/placement changes land in one module per concern.

## Goal

As a maintainer, I want the three placement strategies to share one
find-or-create-under-lock helper (and one herdr-CLI seam), so a naming/placement
change (e.g. the Dispatcher adopt-or-clean, WL-0MWHD0V41007ESWR, or the Ship
tab, WL-0MW6FIZYI0003QEU) is implemented once instead of three parallel
provisioning paths.

## Problem statement (drift catalogue, WL-0MWHUMOHJ006ZMBQ)

- `dispatcher-anchor.placement.ts::getItemTabAnchor` and
  `dispatcher-anchor.tab-anchors.ts::getDispatcherTabAnchor` /
  `getDispatcherAnchor` each re-implement the same
  coordination-lock + double-check + create + persist-or-adopt sequence
  (`tryAcquireCoordLock`, `resolveItemTab`/`resolvePrefixTab`,
  stale-pane re-provision) with per-strategy persistence
  (`dispatcher-anchor.persistence.ts`); the find-anchor-in-tab probe
  (`resolveLivePaneInTab`) is shared but the create paths are not.
- Placement precedence lives in `downtime-worker.dispatch-placement.ts`
  (`resolveDispatchPlacement`) and reuses each strategy's result shape — the
  tie-in point for WL-0MWHW3PKX0048ZYL (deterministic placement).
- herdr CLI subprocess wrappers are split across
  `dispatcher-anchor.herdr-cli.ts` and `pane-close-herdr.ts` (both run
  `herdr pane list`/`pane get` with overlapping parse helpers) and
  `downtime-worker.pane.ts::parseHerdrPaneListOutput` (already delegates to
  `pane-close-herdr.ts` — the exemplar pattern).
- Placement-mode post-processing (`applyPlacementMode`,
  `resolveExtensionsTab`) is a fourth drifted corner used by interactive
  dispatch only.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — One shared find-or-provision-under-lock helper (e.g.
  `dispatcher-anchor.provision.ts`) implements the coordination-lock +
  double-check + create + persist sequence once; all three strategies
  (`getItemTabAnchor`, `getDispatcherTabAnchor`, `getDispatcherAnchor`) use it
  with strategy-specific resolvers/persistence — no parallel provisioning
  sequences left.
- AC2 — One shared `herdr pane list` parse/adapter (already the
  `parseHerdrPaneCloseList` contract) is the single pane-list entry point for
  anchor resolution, the reaper and the in-flight guard; `herdr` subprocess
  invocation is consolidated (one deps factory per concern) without a runtime
  import cycle between `dispatcher-anchor.*` and `pane-close-herdr.ts`.
- AC3 — Placement precedence and per-strategy outcomes are unchanged (pinned by
  `dispatcher-anchor.test.ts`, `dispatcher-anchor.probe.test.ts` and the
  split-guard baseline) — this child is structural reuse, not placement
  behaviour change (which is WL-0MWHW3PKX0048ZYL's scope).
- AC4 — Naming/placement needs of open items are accommodated at the shared
  layer: WL-0MWHD0V41007ESWR (Dispatcher workspace adopt-or-clean),
  WL-0MW6FIZYI0003QEU (Ship tab in invoking workspace),
  WL-0MVZ88G51004IYHW (tab placement left-of-extensions) — no per-strategy
  re-plumbing.
- AC5 — Full unit + integration suite green; split-guard baselines for
  `dispatcher-anchor.*` updated only where the extraction legitimately changes
  the public surface.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.placement.ts` — `getItemTabAnchor`,
  `applyPlacementMode`, `resolveExtensionsTab`
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.tab-anchors.ts` — `getDispatcherAnchor`,
  `getDispatcherTabAnchor`, `resolveLivePaneInTab`
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.herdr-cli.ts` —
  `dispatcher-anchor.cli-parsers.ts` — `dispatcher-anchor.persistence.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-placement.ts` —
  `resolveDispatchPlacement`
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.provision.ts` (new canonical helper)

## Constraints & assumptions

- Structural refactor: no placement-behaviour change (deterministic placement is
  WL-0MWHW3PKX0048ZYL); coordination-lock semantics, ambiguity rules and
  fail-closed outcomes preserved exactly.
- Layering: sibling modules must not import the `dispatcher-anchor.js` barrel
  (existing split-guard constraint).

# Unify dispatched-pane discovery and close logic

## Headline

Consolidate the fragmented pane-discovery and close paths — in-flight
resolution (`resolveInFlightPanes` / `runningDowntimePaneItemIds` /
`countRunningDowntimePanes` / `isSafeDowntimePaneToClose`), the reaper family
(`pane-close.ts`, `pane-close-herdr.ts`, `pane-close-reaper.ts`,
`pane-close-cli.ts`, `pane-close-scheduler.ts`), the disabled lifecycle monitor
(`pane-lifecycle.ts`), ship-guard blocking-pane discovery and the
long-running-panes classification — onto shared discovery/classify helpers, so
a span of behaviour change (e.g. the hydrator evidence fix) touches one module
instead of four.

## Goal

As a maintainer, I want the pane-discovery and close logic unified so a span of
behaviour change (e.g. the hydrator evidence fix, WL-0MWH56SWX004HSKQ) touches
one module instead of four — matching the epic's second user story verbatim.

## Problem statement (drift catalogue, WL-0MWHUMOHJ006ZMBQ)

- Discovery: `downtime-worker.pane.ts` owns `parseHerdrPaneListOutput`,
  `countRunningDowntimePanes`, `runningDowntimePaneItemIds` and
  `isSafeDowntimePaneToClose`; `pane-close-herdr.ts` owns an overlapping
  `parseHerdrPaneCloseList` + `ParsedHerdrPane` mapping; `ship-guard.ts` builds
  its own blocking-pane filter over `parseHerdrPaneListOutput` +
  `extractWorkItemIdsFromText`; `long-running-panes.ts` re-implements
  `paneLabelItemId`-based discovery. Same "list panes → filter label → classify
  agent status" pipeline, four partial copies.
- Close: `pane-close.ts` is the shared pure classifier (good exemplar, reused by
  reaper + pane-triage CLI); the **disabled** `pane-lifecycle.ts` monitor is a
  second, retired decision path (WL-0MUMEKDK0008LKH8) with a documented
  double-close race — retained code that must be reconciled (delete, or fold
  into the reaper as the documented single auto-close path).
- Liveness probe: `isPaneAlive` / agent-status checks repeated across anchor
  resolution (`resolveLivePaneInTab`), reaper (`classifySession` agentDone)
  and the in-flight guard.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — One shared discovery module (e.g. `pane-discovery.ts`) owns: parse pane
  list → per-pane record, live/working predicates, item-scoped in-flight set,
  safe-close predicate and blocking-pane filter; consumers
  (`downtime-worker.pane.ts`, `pane-close-herdr.ts`, `ship-guard.ts`,
  `long-running-panes.ts`) delegate — no duplicated list→filter→classify
  pipelines left.
- AC2 — One documented auto-close decision path: the reaper classifer
  (`pane-close.ts::classifySession`) is the single source of truth; the
  disabled `pane-lifecycle.ts` classifier (Mechanism B) is either deleted or
  documented as intentionally retained-for-redesign with the double-close race
  resolved at the wiring level (no two mechanisms both closing).
- AC3 — The in-flight resolution and the reaper share liveness semantics
  (agent-status classification and/or `isPaneAlive` probe) via one helper —
  no silently divergent "live" definitions.
- AC4 — The hydrator evidence fix (WL-0MWH56SWX004HSKQ) and prep-tier busy
  contract (WL-0MWHBSTM1004KQ49) land against the unified discovery module with
  no label-parse or discovery duplication; their tests pin the shared helpers.
- AC5 — Full unit + integration suite green; `pane-close*.test.ts`,
  `pane-lifecycle.test.ts`, `ship-guard.test.ts`, `long-running-panes.test.ts`
  and the downtime dispatch suites cover the consolidated paths.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.pane.ts` — discovery predicates +
  lifecycle monitor wiring
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-close.ts` — shared classification (exemplar)
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-close-herdr.ts`, `pane-close-reaper.ts`,
  `pane-close-cli.ts`, `pane-close-scheduler.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-lifecycle.ts` — disabled Mechanism B
- `packages/herdr/src/ship-guard.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/long-running-panes.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-discovery.ts` (new canonical module)

## Constraints & assumptions

- Behaviour-preserving: discovery and close outcomes unchanged; the reaper
  remains the only active auto-close path (Mechanism B stays disabled unless
  the race is reworked — see WL-0MUMEKDK0008LKH8).
- The pane-close CLI is a cross-language bridge for the `pane-triage` skill —
  its output contract is stable (fixture tests pin it).


## Impact

Maintainers now change pane discovery or close behaviour (e.g. the hydrator evidence fix) in one shared `pane-discovery.ts` module instead of patching four drifted copies, and the reaper is the documented single auto-close decision path — so a span-wide pane change touches one module and the double-close race stays resolved at the wiring level.

# Unify fetch/wl spawn management with pane-close herdr CLI seams

## Headline

Reconcile the fourth spawn/CLI seam — `fetcher.cli.ts` (`wl` CLI spawn with a
spawn cap, timeout, retry and in-flight memo) and the duplicated `herdr` binary
invocation helpers — with the canonical pane-discovery/herdr-CLI seams, so all
herdr/wl subprocess handling converges on shared deps factories and parse
helpers (or is documented as intentionally out of scope).

## Goal

As a maintainer, I want every herdr/wl subprocess boundary (pane discovery,
close, budget repair, fetch) to share one CLI-resolution + spawn + parse
convention, so a change to the `herdr`/`wl` binary probe order or output shape
touches one module instead of scattered execFile/execFileAsync call sites.

## Problem statement (drift catalogue, WL-0MWHUMOHJ006ZMBQ)

- `fetcher.cli.ts` owns `runWl` (execFileAsync, binary probe `wl`→`worklog`,
  bounded timeout, spawn-cap slots, in-flight memo) while
  `dispatcher-anchor.herdr-cli.ts` and `pane-close-herdr.ts` each own their own
  `herdr` exec helpers — three subprocess seams with duplicated binary-probe
  and error-normalisation logic.
- `host-dispatch-budget.repair.ts` re-implements label parsing locally and
  shells out to `herdr pane list` through yet another path.
- The pane-close CLI bridges to the Python `pane-triage` skill via its own
  executable — the CLI seam is the cross-language contract that must stay
  stable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — A shared CLI-resolution + spawn helper (binary probe order, bounded
  timeout, exec seam, error normalisation) is used by `fetcher.cli.ts` and the
  herdr invoke sites; the `wl`/`worklog` probe and the `herdr` probe each have
  one canonical declaration (constants shared, not re-declared).
- AC2 — Every `herdr pane list` invocation across the codebase goes through the
  single parse contract (`parseHerdrPaneCloseList` family); the
  `host-dispatch-budget.repair.ts` local label parse is removed in favour of the
  canonical label module (see pane-label child).
- AC3 — The pane-close CLI output contract (pane-triage skill bridge) is
  unchanged and pinned by its fixture tests.
- AC4 — Where fetch/wl spawn management is deliberately different (execFile for
  data reads vs pane spawns via send-to-pi.sh), the difference is documented in
  the shared module header — no accidental convergence of unrelated seams.
- AC5 — Full unit + integration suite green; `fetcher.split-guard.test.ts` and
  the fetcher suites pin the refactor.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.cli.ts` — `runWl`, `CLI_BINARIES`, spawn-cap,
  memo
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.args.ts` — `buildWlArgs`, `getExecFileAsync`,
  `getWorklogDir`
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.herdr-cli.ts` — herdr subprocess seams
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-close-herdr.ts` — reaper deps factory,
  `createHerdrReaperDeps`
- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.repair.ts` — local herdr/label path

## Constraints & assumptions

- Behaviour-preserving; the `wl` CLI spawn-cap/timeout/memo semantics
  (F5/F8, WL-0MSGAEZRB0016GCX lineage) are load-bearing and unchanged.
- Pane spawns (send-to-pi.sh) and `wl` data reads (execFile) are different
  seams by design — this child unifies their *plumbing* (probe/exec/error
  convention), not their purpose.

## Impact

Maintainers can change the `herdr`/`wl` binary probe order or spawn-error
handling in one shared module (`cli-spawn.ts`) instead of patching three
parallel subprocess seams.

# Docs: single pane-creation architecture map and naming contract

## Headline

Docs child: consolidate the dispatched-pane architecture documentation —
`docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` placement/lifecycle sections, README, and the
module-header doc comments — into one map of the unified pane-creation paths
and one workspace/tab/pane naming contract, so the refactoring children land
against a single documented target and open in-flight items keep their naming
needs pinned.

## Goal

As a maintainer, I want the pane-creation architecture documented once — one
map of which path creates which pane, one naming contract for workspaces, tabs
and panes (after the unification children land) — so future pane features and
the open in-flight items (Ship tab, Dispatcher adopt-or-clean, hydrator
evidence) have one reference instead of the current scattered section headers.

## Problem statement

- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` documents the three-strategy placement
  precedence and lifecycle mechanisms (Mechanism A reaper / disabled Mechanism B
  monitor) — references that will change as WL-0MWHW3PKX0048ZYL and the
  unification children land.
- README and module headers repeat partial path maps
  (`downtime-worker.pane.ts`, `index.commands.ts`, `dispatcher-anchor*`,
  `pane-close*` headers each describe their own slice).
- Naming: `Dispatcher` workspace, `Downtime` root tab, per-prefix tabs, item-ID
  tabs, `Work Items` plugin pane, planned `Ship` tab (WL-0MW6FIZYI0003QEU) —
  no single contract page.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` gains a single "Pane creation
  architecture" section: one map of spawn paths → argv builder → shell script →
  placement strategy → lifecycle/close path, reflecting the post-refactor
  structure (shared argv builder, unified discovery module, deterministic
  placement).

  project workspaces), tab labels (item-ID, per-prefix, `Downtime`, `Ship`,
  `Worklog`), pane title formats (`Downtime triggered …`, `Manually
  triggered …`, `Shell: …`) and the truncation/suffix rules — cross-referenced

  (`downtime-worker.pane.ts`), interactive dispatch (`index.commands.ts` →
  `send-to-pi.sh` / `run-in-pane.sh`), scheduled prompts, ship-in-own-pane,
  fetcher spawns, anchor/placement (`dispatcher-anchor*.ts`),
  lifecycle/close (`pane-lifecycle.ts`, `pane-close*.ts`), and pane-capture
  (`index.pane-capture.ts`) — and this docs child keeps that map accurate.

  reuse, other smells) to its child work item, each under this epic with

- AC8 — Child quality bar (epic AC4) and suite gate (epic AC6): this docs

## Key Files

**Parent:** WL-0MVYZ458V004GRF8 (Create a podcast for standups). Q3=A: the trigger is a standup-skill post-step (SorraAgents-owned, tracked as the SorraAgents follow-up child); this item covers the **ContentCreator-side contract** the hook invokes.

As an operator, I want a single, well-defined per-project invocation of the ContentCreator pipeline (stable script path, args, exit codes, logging) that the standup-skill post-step can call right after a standup report is written, so podcast publication is automatic and observable.

# Blocker: Concurrent main-checkout mutation blocks full-suite gate

## Headline

Stray uncommitted edits in the main checkout (`docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `tests/herdr/run-in-pane-main.test.ts`) left by the WL-0MWHWGZI4007D911 session blocked WL-0MWHBSY6Q00760H9's finish gate (`full_suite_red`, infrastructure) — the mutated paths must be committed/pushed by the owning item (or reverted), the root cause confirmed, and the blocked finish re-run green.

## Problem statement

A sibling implementation session (WL-0MWHWGZI4007D911, "Unify send-to-pi.sh / run-in-pane.sh argv builders") left uncommitted changes in the **main checkout** instead of its linked worktree: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (docs table row for the new `pane-argv.ts` canonical builder) and `tests/herdr/run-in-pane-main.test.ts` (pins for the converged `--cwd=`/`--pane-name=` forms). Those live-repo mutations were detected by the pre-lock full-suite run of WL-0MWHBSY6Q00760H9's `implement.py finish`, failing the gate with `full_suite_red (failure_kind: infrastructure)` and blocking that session. The systemic gate-verdict fix for this failure class is already scoped separately (WL-0MWFKDFFA009N3OC); this item covers the immediate unblock and the instance-level root-cause confirmation.

## Users

- **Hydrator release-diagnostics session (WL-0MWHBSY6Q00760H9)** — blocked mid-finish; needs a clean main checkout to re-run the full-suite gate.
- **Operator / herdr downtime worker** — needs the main checkout restored to clean so concurrent work is not blocked by another session's stray writes.
- **WL-0MWHWGZI4007D911 session** — owns the mutated content; needs to land it through its own worktree, not the main checkout.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Main checkout restored to clean.** The two mutated paths (`docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `tests/herdr/run-in-pane-main.test.ts`) are either (a) committed and pushed to `dev` by WL-0MWHWGZI4007D911 through its worktree, or (b) reverted to HEAD if they do not belong there; `git status` in the main checkout is clean afterwards.
2. **Blocked session unblocked.** WL-0MWHBSY6Q00760H9 re-runs `implement.py finish` and the full-suite gate passes (no `full_suite_red` / `live_repo_mutation`) — the finish reaches its normal terminal outcome.
3. **Instance root cause confirmed and recorded.** Determine whether the stray writes came from WL-0MWHWGZI4007D911's main session writing to the main checkout instead of its worktree, or from an unfinished pre-worktree phase; record the finding and the supporting evidence (e.g. session logs, file mtimes, `.implement_state.json`) as a comment on this item.
4. **No duplication with the systemic fix.** The gate's verdict behaviour (concurrent-session writes misattributed to the suite) is *not* re-implemented here — that is WL-0MWFKDFFA009N3OC's scope; this item links it as related work and only performs the operational unblock.
5. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes** (any commit made as part of this item, and the re-run gate of step 2).

## Constraints

- Do not weaken the main-checkout wipe protection that the 2026-10-26 incident motivated (WL-0MVPE2BY9001CR9O) — reverting or committing the stray files must not disable or narrow the live-repo mutation guard.
- The mutated content is legitimate WL-0MWHWGZI4007D911 work; prefer committing it over reverting it. Revert only if the item's owner determines the content is stale or wrong.
- All changes land through the owning item's worktree, never by committing directly in the main checkout.

## Existing state

- Main checkout (`/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub`): two modified files with no corresponding entries in the owning worktree's `git status` — `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `tests/herdr/run-in-pane-main.test.ts`.
- Owning worktree `wl-WL-0MWHWGZI4007D911-unify-send-to-pi-sh-run-in-pane-sh-argv`: has its own modified/new files (pane-argv.ts, pane-options.sh, etc.) but does **not** contain the two mutated paths; item still `in-progress`.
- WL-0MWHBSY6Q00760H9: `status=blocked`, `stage=intake_complete`, finish gate red with `failure_kind: infrastructure`.
- Systemic fix WL-0MWFKDFFA009N3OC is `intake_complete` + `needsProducerReview` (mechanism A/B/C/D open, A recommended, C folded into WL-0MW4W15U500009D2).

## Desired change

1. Move the two stray files into WL-0MWHWGZI4007D911's worktree, commit and push them to `dev` (or revert them to HEAD).
2. Restore the main checkout to clean; verify with `git status`.
3. Re-run WL-0MWHBSY6Q00760H9's finish gate to green.
4. Record the confirmed root cause on this item and cross-link WL-0MWFKDFFA009N3OC for the gate fix.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — stray doc edit (belongs to WL-0MWHWGZI4007D911)
- `tests/herdr/run-in-pane-main.test.ts` — stray test pins (belongs to WL-0MWHWGZI4007D911)
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-argv.ts` — the canonical builder the strays document/pin
- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` — worktree rules the stray write violated (reference)

## Related work

- **WL-0MWFKDFFA009N3OC** — "Pre-push live-repo mutation gate blocks driven finishes when a concurrent session writes the main checkout" (`intake_complete`, needs producer review): the systemic gate-verdict fix for this failure class; **not** re-implemented here.
- **WL-0MWHWGZI4007D911** — "Unify send-to-pi.sh / run-in-pane.sh argv builders": the owning sibling session that left the stray mutations.
- **WL-0MWHBSY6Q00760H9** — "Impl: release diagnostics evidence": the session blocked by the dirty checkout.
- **WL-0MW4W15U500009D2** (blocked) / **WL-0MW4W0WDF005Y0TQ** (open) — isolated-worktree verification runs; the architectural alternative (mechanism C).
- **WL-0MVPE2BY9001CR9O** (completed) — the main-checkout guard whose false positive this class triggers.
- Docs: `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`, `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` §8.5.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep:** keep this item to the operational unblock and instance diagnosis; the gate-verdict change and the isolated-worktree migration are separately tracked (WL-0MWFKDFFA009N3OC / WL-0MW4W15U500009D2). If more systemic work is discovered, record it as new linked work items.
- **Assumption:** the two mutated files are legitimate WL-0MWHWGZI4007D911 work and should be committed (option a of AC1), not reverted.
- **Assumption:** the owning session is still active (worktree present, item `in-progress`); if it is not, this item may need to commit the strays directly or revert them — verify ownership before choosing.
- **Risk:** if the root cause is a driven child or pre-worktree phase that never asserted worktree isolation, a one-off cleanup does not prevent recurrence; the durable prevention is WL-0MWFKDFFA009N3OC's gate verdict plus the existing `implement.py finish` outside-worktree check.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Should the stray changes be committed by WL-0MWHWGZI4007D911 or reverted?" — Answer: **Committed** (preferred), since the diff content matches the sibling item's documented scope (pane-argv.ts docs table row; converged `--cwd=`/`--pane-name=` run-in-pane.sh test pins). Revert only if ownership review finds the content stale. Source: diff analysis of `git diff docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` and `tests/herdr/run-in-pane-main.test.ts` (2026-11-15).
- Q: "Which phase wrote to the main checkout?" — OPEN: needs inspection of the WL-0MWHWGZI4007D911 session logs / `.implement_state.json` / file mtimes to distinguish a main-session write outside its worktree from an unfinished pre-worktree edit. Recorded as AC3.
- Q: "Does this item duplicate WL-0MWFKDFFA009N3OC?" — Answer: **Partial overlap only.** WL-0MWFKDFFA009N3OC owns the gate's verdict (concurrent main-checkout writes must not fail a driven finish); this item owns the immediate cleanup, the blocked-finish re-run, and the instance root-cause record. Linked as related work per the duplicate-work detection procedure.

data.description:
# Make the startup-budget regression gate load-independent

## Headline

The measured regression gate in `tests/cli/startup-import-budget.test.ts` is not load-independent in two of its three metrics, so it fails the dev-push full suite whenever the host is busy — blocking unrelated work items and spawning duplicate triage items. Isolate the measured suite from the parallel full-suite run and replace the `p95`-over-4-samples statistic with a robust one, **without blunting regression sensitivity**.

## Goal

As a maintainer, I want the startup-import-budget regression gate to give the same verdict on the same code whether the host is idle or saturated, so a red dev-push gate always means "this tree regressed" and never "the machine was busy".

## Problem statement

`evaluateStartupBudget` (`bench/startup-budget.ts`) checks three metrics against recorded baselines in `bench/startup-import-budget.json`:

| Metric | Headroom (current budget) | Load correction today |
|---|---|---|
| p95 CPU time | `cpuHeadroomPct: 100` (2x) | none (treated as the "load-independent" metric in the budget note) |
| p95 wall time | `wallHeadroomPct: 200` (3x) + `wallFloorMs: 250` | divided by the run's `bareNode` control via `hostLoadFactor()`, clamped at `maxHostLoadFactor: 8` |
| p95 peak RSS | `rssHeadroomPct: 25` | **none by design** — the budget note states RSS "keeps a tighter 25 % headroom so memory regressions still fail promptly" |

Two flakes were observed in one epic session (WL-0MWHUMOHJ006ZMBQ, host load 4.7-6.3 with ~20 concurrent sessions):

1. **Wall-clock flake** — triaged as WL-0MWI7A1N7009NLIM; mitigated by raising `bareNodeRuns` 2 -> 5 (commit `78062d7c6`). The `hostLoadFactor` clamp of 8 means wall is in practice barely gated on a busy host (3x headroom, then up to 8x normalisation).
2. **RSS flake** — triaged as WL-0MWIF616V008380O: `version: p95RssMb 131 exceeds limit 130.8 (recorded p95 104.6 MiB + 25 % RSS headroom)`, while the same suite measures 99.8-106 MiB standalone. Hypothesis: in-suite parallel vitest workers (fork pool, `maxForks ~6`) inflate tsx child RSS by ~25 % — starved V8 collects less often, so the heap grows before exit. Not yet proven.

**Secondary defect:** `regression.runs: 4`, so the "p95" is effectively the maximum of four samples — a very jumpy statistic that amplifies the flake.

### Why this is not "just add headroom"

RSS is the only metric tight enough to catch a real memory regression promptly. Loosening it (or normalising it by the wall-time control, which is dimensionally wrong) trades a flake for a blind spot. Similarly, skipping the assertion when load is high converts a perf gate into a sometimes-gate: a genuine regression that lands during a busy period passes. Both are explicitly rejected below.

## Users

- **Implementation agents** — every dev-push runs the full suite; a load-flaky gate costs a ~5-minute suite per retry, resets otherwise-good worktrees, and spawns duplicate triage items.
- **Producers/operators** — need an auditable, trustworthy red/green signal for the startup-cost budget (the AC1 goal: warm p95 wall <= 700 ms and peak RSS <= 68 MB was accepted at the measured floor by the producer decision of 2026-10-21).
- **Downstream epics** — WL-0MWHUMOHJ006ZMBQ's remaining children (WL-0MWHWH6XL0025YX2, WL-0MWHW3PKX0048ZYL, WL-0MWHWHB3X004H9VG, WL-0MWHWH68L007L7IO, WL-0MWHWHBSW005KG13) each need this gate to pass.

## Design options considered

| # | Option | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Normalise RSS/CPU by the existing `bareNode` wall factor | **Rejected as a standalone fix** — scaling a memory budget by a time ratio is dimensionally unsound and would mask a real memory regression |
| 2 | Isolate the measured suite (own vitest project / quiet pool / serialised) | **Adopted (primary)** — attacks the cause, keeps thresholds honest |
| 3 | Replace `p95`-over-4 with a documented robust statistic | **Adopted (secondary)** — the second-order defect; reduces variance without loosening limits |
| 4 | Gate on structure only (AST import-graph ratchet, module sizes) | Rejected as a replacement — loses end-to-end runtime signal. The existing ratchet test stays as-is and is already deterministic |
| 5 | Per-host-class recorded baselines / dedicated runner | **Deferred** — correct long-term home for the AC1 numbers, but needs infra this repo does not own |
| 6 | Skip or soft-fail the measured assertions when load is high | **Rejected** — hides real regressions; converts the gate into a sometimes-gate |
| 7 | Memory-aware control (spawn a fixed allocation workload to derive a memory factor) | **Fallback only** — acceptable *if and only if* AC4 (a synthetic regression still fails) is proven for it |

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Isolation.** The measured regression test executes without contention from the parallel full-suite run, using **repo-side** configuration only (e.g. a separate vitest project with a serialised/quiet fork pool, or equivalent). It must work when the harness runs plain `vitest run` with no extra flags — the agent-side test runner is not modifiable from this repo.
- **AC2 — Robust statistic.** The measured assertions no longer derive a `p95` from a 4-sample set. Choose and document one of: median-of-N with a stated margin, max-of-N with an explicit N, or another justified estimator. Record the choice and rationale in the `regression` block's `note` in `bench/startup-import-budget.json` so a later reader knows why it is not `p95`.
- **AC3 — Determinism under load.** With the isolation in place, the suite's verdict is stable across repeated runs on a contended host. Evidence: N >= 5 consecutive runs of the measured suite at host load >= 4 (or an equivalent synthetic contention harness) all agree, recorded on this item.
- **AC4 — Sensitivity preserved (anti-blunting).** A synthetic regression still fails. Add a test exercising `evaluateStartupBudget` against a measurement where RSS (and separately wall) exceed their limits, asserting a violation is reported. If option 7 (memory factor) is used, it must be proven that a genuine +30 % RSS regression still reds under a large derived factor.
- **AC5 — No threshold loosening without justification.** `rssHeadroomPct` and `cpuHeadroomPct` are not raised (or any change is justified with measurement evidence on this item and recorded in the budget `note`); `maxHostLoadFactor` is not raised.
- **AC6 — Deterministic tests untouched.** The AST ratchet and the entry-point split allowlist tests keep their current behaviour and pass unchanged.
- **AC7 — Docs.** Update the budget file's `note`, the header comment of `bench/startup-budget.ts`, and any test-suite documentation (e.g. `tests/README.md` if it describes the perf gates) to state: the measured suite runs isolated, the statistic used, and why normalisation is limited to wall.
- **AC8 — Full suite green.** The full project test suite passes, and the full suite passes repeatedly on a loaded host (evidence on this item).

## Key Files

- `tests/cli/startup-import-budget.test.ts` — the measured regression test + ratchet + allowlist suites
- `bench/startup-budget.ts` — `evaluateStartupBudget`, `hostLoadFactor`, `MAX_HOST_LOAD_FACTOR`, headroom policy types
- `bench/startup-import-budget.json` — recorded baselines + `regression` policy (`runs`, headrooms, `maxHostLoadFactor`, `note`)
- `bench/wl-startup-perf.ts` — `runStartupBenchmark`, `bareNodeRuns` / `runs` sample collection
- `bench/startup-import-graph.ts` — AST import-graph walker (deterministic ratchet; unchanged)
- `vitest.config.ts` — fork pool config; the natural place for a repo-side isolation project
- `tests/unit/maxworkers-config-guard.test.ts` — existing declared-config guard; extended to pin the measured project's single worker, its group order, and its exclusion from `suite`
- `docs/dev/wl-startup-import-budget.md` — the budget document that must state the isolation, the statistic and why normalisation is limited to wall (AC7)
- `README.md` (Vitest Configuration section) — secondary AC7 surface; `tests/README.md` does not describe the perf gate and stays unchanged

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** isolating the suite slows the full run. Accepted: the measured file is ~13 s standalone.
- **Risk:** a vitest config change could silently stop covering the file. AC3/AC8 evidence must show it still *runs* (not merely passes).
- **Risk:** the RSS-inflation mechanism is a hypothesis. If isolation alone does not stabilise RSS, option 7 becomes viable provided AC4 holds.
- **Assumption:** the agent-side test runner invokes `vitest run` in the repo and honours repo-side project configuration.
- **Assumption:** baselines remain recorded on a quiet reference host; this item does not re-record them (that belongs with option 5).

## Out of scope

- Re-recording baselines per host class (option 5) — separate item if pursued.
- The AC1 target enforcement flip (`ac1Targets.enforced`).
- Any change to the agent-side test skill/runner (`skill/`, `.pi/`) — repository boundaries.

## Related work

- **WL-0MWIF616V008380O** — the RSS flake instance that surfaced this (duplicate root cause of the item below). This item is the durable fix.
- **WL-0MWI7A1N7009NLIM** — the wall-clock flake instance; its mitigation (`bareNodeRuns` 2 -> 5, commit `78062d7c6`) is partial and superseded by AC2/AC3.
- **WL-0MWHUMOHJ006ZMBQ** — epic whose remaining children are blocked in practice by this gate.
- **WL-0MVS9Z965006MC4R** — the prior wall-flake precedent recorded in the budget note.

## Impact

A red dev-push gate means the tree regressed and never that the machine was busy, so maintainers stop paying repeated ~5-minute suite retries and stop mistrusting the startup-cost guard.

## Discovered from

`discovered-from:WL-0MWIF616V008380O` (and `discovered-from:WL-0MWHUMOHJ006ZMBQ`) — found while driving the pane-refactor epic, where this gate blocked every remaining child's dev push on a contended host.

## Plan

A single cohesive slice — **no child work items**. The design decision is already
recorded in *Design options considered* (option 2 primary, option 3 secondary; 1, 4 and
6 rejected; 5 deferred; 7 fallback), so the eight ACs *are* the deliverable increment and
decomposing them further would only add handoffs. Effort M / risk Medium, and the
plan-approval gate did not request producer confirmation (approval is requested only for
Extra Large effort **and** High/Severe risk).

### Implementation order (test-first, vertical slices)

Each step cuts through every layer it touches (code + tests + docs) and leaves the tree
shippable; AC3/AC8 evidence is deliberately last because it needs the final tree.

1. **Isolation slice (AC1, AC6, AC7).** Declare the `suite` and
   `startup-budget-measured` projects in `vitest.config.ts` (measured file only,
   `maxWorkers: 1`, `sequence.groupOrder: 1`, excluded from `suite`); extend
   `tests/unit/maxworkers-config-guard.test.ts` to pin single worker + group order +
   exclusion; document it in `README.md` and `docs/dev/wl-startup-import-budget.md`.
   Verify: the guard test fails when the project or the exclusion is removed, and the
   measured file still *executes* under plain `vitest run` (the stated risk: a config
   change could silently stop covering it — a green run that ran nothing must not pass).
2. **Statistic slice (AC2, AC4, AC5).** Record `p50CpuMs` / `p50RssMb` beside the
   existing p95 samples in `bench/wl-startup-perf.ts`; select the declared
   `regression.statistic` in `evaluateStartupBudget`, falling back to p95 when a
   measurement carries no median, so an older measurement is still gated rather than
   skipped; set `runs: 7` and `statistic: "p50"` and record the rationale in
   `regression.note`. Verify with the AC4 anti-blunting tests: one spiked sample passes
   under the median and fails under p95 (the estimator changed, not the threshold);
   uniform +30 % RSS, over-budget wall and over-budget CPU all still fail; a legacy
   p95-only measurement still fails. AC5 is pinned by asserting the unchanged
   `cpuHeadroomPct` / `rssHeadroomPct` / `maxHostLoadFactor`.
3. **Evidence slice (AC3, AC8).** Run the full suite repeatedly on a contended host
   (host load >= 4, or an equivalent synthetic contention harness), confirm the measured
   suite genuinely ran in its own group — not merely that the run went green — and record
   the run table (timestamp, load average, verdict, measured p50/p95 numbers) on this
   item. AC3 needs N >= 5 consecutive agreeing runs of the measured suite.

### Non-goals repeated for the implementer

- Do not raise `cpuHeadroomPct`, `rssHeadroomPct` or `maxHostLoadFactor` (AC5).
- Do not re-record baselines — per-host-class baselines are option 5, out of scope.
- Do not touch `bench/startup-import-graph.ts` or the entry-point split allowlist (AC6).
- Do not change the agent-side test runner (`skill/`, `.pi/`) — repository boundaries;
  the isolation must work under plain `vitest run` (AC1).

### Verified planning facts (constraints that shaped this plan)

- `package.json`'s `test` script is exactly `vitest run`, and the skill runner runs
  `npm --silent test -- <path>` verbatim (`.pi/test-config.json`), so repo-side project
  configuration is the only reachable lever — AC1's premise holds.
- vitest ^4.0.18 supports `test.projects` with `extends: true` and
  `sequence.groupOrder`, so a sequenced single-worker project is expressible with no
  extra CLI flags.
- The skill test runner injects `VITEST_MAX_WORKERS` (default 4) into the child
  environment and vitest applies it *after* config resolution
  (`vitest/dist/chunks/coverage.*.js`: `if (process.env.VITEST_MAX_WORKERS)
  resolved.maxWorkers = ...`). The declared `maxWorkers: 1` is therefore a lower bound
  under the runner (effective cap 4). Isolation is still intact because that project
  includes exactly one file, so one worker runs in practice — but the docs should state
  that the declared value is what the guard pins, and AC3 evidence must show genuine
  serialisation against `suite` (the groups do not overlap), not merely low fan-out.
- `tests/README.md` does not describe the perf gate (verified by grep), so AC7's docs
  obligation lands on `README.md` and `docs/dev/wl-startup-import-budget.md`.

### Deliverables checklist (maps 1:1 to the ACs)

Isolated vitest project + config guard (AC1), declared statistic with a recorded
rationale (AC2), determinism evidence (AC3), anti-blunting tests (AC4), unchanged
thresholds pinned by a test (AC5), untouched deterministic suites (AC6), three
documentation surfaces updated (AC7), repeated green full-suite evidence (AC8).

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-15 — `/skill:plan WL-0MWIGCK0E009GGLG`. Effort/risk pre-check: `plan`
  (effort M, risk Medium). Approval gate: not requested (only XL effort **and**
  High/Severe risk pauses for producer confirmation). AC coverage review: `proceed`.
  Duplicate check: no overlapping completed item — WL-0MWI7A1N7009NLIM (wall flake) and
  WL-0MWIF616V008380O (RSS flake) are the two *instances* this item durably fixes, and
  WL-0MVS9Z965006MC4R is prior precedent already recorded in the budget note.
  - No child work items created: single cohesive slice, one implementation session.
  - Added the `## Plan` section (test-first order, non-goals, verified constraints) and
    the Appendix below.
  - Completeness review: added the three changed-but-unlisted files to **Key Files**
    (`tests/unit/maxworkers-config-guard.test.ts`,
    `docs/dev/wl-startup-import-budget.md`, `README.md`). **Key Files** passes
    `validate_key_files_format()`.
  - No wording changes to the ACs, the design verdicts or the thresholds; nothing removed.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No producer questions were required: the intake brief already records the design decision
and every AC was verifiable from the repository. The questions considered, and the
evidence that resolved them:

- **Q: Is there a reachable isolation lever that does not touch the agent-side test
  runner (AC1)?** Answer (evidence): yes — `package.json` runs `vitest run` and the skill
  runner passes the command through verbatim (`.pi/test-config.json`,
  `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`); vitest ^4 `test.projects` +
  `sequence.groupOrder` is plain repo configuration. No producer decision needed.
- **Q: Does switching the estimator force a baseline re-record?** Answer (evidence): no —
  the recorded baselines stay p95 values and the measured spread puts the median and the
  p95 within a few percent, so the unchanged headroom percentages remain the effective
  margin (recorded in `regression.note`); re-recording belongs with option 5, out of
  scope.
- **Q: Does an existing completed item already satisfy these ACs?** Answer (evidence):
  no — WL-0MWI7A1N7009NLIM and WL-0MWIF616V008380O are single-instance triage items
  (`completed` / `blocked`); neither isolates the suite nor changes the statistic, so
  nothing was closed as a duplicate and no description was rewritten.
- **Q: Does AC7's "`tests/README.md` if it describes the perf gates" apply?** Answer
  (evidence): no — grep finds no mention of the startup budget or the perf gates there,
  so AC7 lands on `README.md` and `docs/dev/wl-startup-import-budget.md`.
- **Q: How does the declared `maxWorkers: 1` interact with the runner's
  `VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=4`?** Answer (evidence): vitest applies the env var after config
  resolution, so the effective cap under the runner is 4; the project includes a single
  file, so one worker runs in practice. Recorded as a constraint in **Verified planning
  facts** and as an AC3 evidence requirement. No intent change, so no OPEN QUESTION —
  flagged to the implement session.

**Assumptions:** the measured suite remains a real measured run (never skipped) under
isolation; baselines stay recorded on a quiet reference host; the residual
host-saturation risk is absorbed by the wall host-load factor plus the robust estimator.
