# Add startOn (earliest start date/time) to work items

## Goal

Give every work item a first-class **`startOn`** field — the earliest date/time at which the item may proceed — and make every CLI and Herdr-plugin **search surface filter out not-yet-started items by default**. Today scheduling is unenforceable: the only signal is a `[run-not-before 2026-11-19T10:25:00Z]` prefix baked into the title, which nothing filters on, which agents must parse by hand, and which pollutes titles permanently.

## Problem statement

Worklog has no structural scheduling dimension for temporal gates. Downtime-ordered work items encode their earliest-start date in the title text, and nothing enforces or filters on it. This means dispatchers can fire agents before measurement windows are valid, and restarts can silently void mid-flight windows.

## Users

- **Downtime dispatcher agents** — need a reliable `startOn` signal to know when an item is eligible for dispatch.
- **Human operators** — need `wl list`/`wl search`/`wl next` to respect temporal scheduling without manual date parsing.
- **Herdr worklist users** — need to see not-yet-started items read-only with a "not started until" marker.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Data model.** `startOn` is stored per work item as an ISO-8601 UTC timestamp, exposed in every JSON surface (`show`, `list`, `search`, `next`, `recent`, `in_progress`, dependency listings). **Default = the item's `createdAt`** when omitted, including on import of legacy JSONL/Git data that has no field (back-compat is the default, never "blocked").
- **AC2 — CLI authoring.** `wl create --start-on <ISO-8601>` and `wl update <id> --start-on <ISO-8601>` (offset accepted, normalised to UTC); `--start-on ""` clears it back to `createdAt`. Invalid values fail with an actionable message. `wl show <id>` is **never** filtered — an item is always retrievable by id.
- **AC3 — Default filtering in searches.** `wl list`, `wl search`, `wl next`, `wl in_progress`, `wl recent` and the equivalent JSON paths **exclude** items whose `startOn` is in the future. An explicit opt-in (`--include-not-started`, and/or `--starts-before <ISO>`) shows them, marked as not yet started in both text and JSON output. `in_progress` items are never filtered out (a started item has already started).
- **AC4 — Herdr plugin parity.** Worklist, dispatcher and audit-pickup queries apply the same default filter, so a future item is never dispatched or claimed by any Herdr worker. Surface not-yet-started items **read-only** in the worklist with a "not started until <date>" marker, following the existing held-items banner convention (WL-0MVR8FN1D002SCIR), and never clear or alter their state.
- **AC5 — Claim guard (defence in depth).** Setting an item to `in_progress` (or any claim path) on a future `startOn` is refused with a machine-readable reason (`start_on_not_reached`) unless an explicit, auditable override is passed; the override writes a comment naming the actor and the reason. The guard must not fire for `createdAt`-defaulted items.
- **AC6 — Migration and sync.** A documented, idempotent migration sets `startOn = createdAt` for existing items (`docs/migrations/`); `doctor` reports a mismatch; JSONL export/import and Git sync round-trip the field; cross-project edges (foreign ids) are unaffected; two-way sync never resurrects a stale value.
- **AC7 — Tests.** Unit and integration coverage for: default = `createdAt`; future-filtered out of every search surface listed in AC3; opt-in shows them marked; `--start-on` set/clear; claim refused and overridden; legacy JSONL import back-fill; sync round-trip; a frozen-clock test (no wall-clock flakiness).
- **AC8 — Docs and help.** `CLI.md`, `DATA_FORMAT.md`, `API.md`, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` and the relevant skill docs updated; `wl create --help` / `wl update --help` describe the field and its default.
- **AC9 — Performance.** An index on `startOn` (or an equivalent query plan) so `list`/`search`/`next` stay within the existing benchmarks on the current store size; record the before/after figures.

## Impact

Users can now schedule work items to become available at a specific future time, ensuring that time-gated measurements and scheduled tasks are not dispatched before their measurement windows are valid.

## Constraints and non-goals

- **Non-goals:** a scheduler or queueing engine, recurrence, timezone UI, automatic re-anchoring of dates, calendar integration.
- Do not repurpose the existing `assignee` hold, `dependencies` or `blocked` status: `startOn` is temporal, dependencies are causal, the assignee hold is an operator claim. All three must compose (an item can be dependency-ready, unheld and still not-yet-started).
- UK English throughout; schema changes ship with migration + docs in the same change; no breaking change to existing JSON consumers (additive field, defaulted).
- Test discipline: the full suite through the project's test skill, and no direct test invocations outside it.

## Key Files

- `packages/shared/src/types.ts` — Add `startOn` to `WorkItem`, `CreateWorkItemInput`, `UpdateWorkItemInput`
- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` — Add `startOn` column to the `workitems` table DDL and bump `SCHEMA_VERSION`; include the field in every JSONL export/import row projection
- `src/migrations/index.ts` — Add the idempotent back-fill migration (`startOn = createdAt` for existing rows) and bump `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION`
- `src/commands/create.ts` — Add the `--start-on <ISO-8601>` option, offset-accepted + normalised to UTC, defaults to `createdAt`
- `src/commands/update.ts` — Add `--start-on <ISO-8601>` (`""` clears back to `createdAt`); host the claim guard on the `--status in_progress` transition
- `src/commands/list.ts` — Default `startOn` exclusion plus `--include-not-started` / `--starts-before <ISO>` opt-in with a not-yet-started marker in text and JSON
- `src/commands/search.ts` — Same default exclusion + opt-in as `list`
- `src/commands/next.ts` — Default `startOn` exclusion (with opt-in) in the browse-feed selection
- `src/commands/in-progress.ts` — Default `startOn` exclusion, but never filter items already `in-progress`
- `src/commands/recent.ts` — Default `startOn` exclusion + opt-in
- `src/commands/worklist.ts` — Consolidated read (`db.list()` + shared browse feed) must apply the same default filter for every subset
- `src/worklist-selection.ts` — Shared browse-feed selection: carry the filter so `next`/`worklist`/Herdr agree
- `src/claim-hold.ts` / `src/claim-hold-read.ts` — Claim-path surfaces the guard sits behind; add the `start_on_not_reached` refusal and the audited override comment
- `packages/shared/src/fields.ts` — Add `startOn` to `VALID_FIELDS`
- `packages/shared/src/predicates.ts` — Add the shared `isNotStarted(item, now)` predicate (clock injectable for tests)
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — Surface not-yet-started items read-only with a "not started until <date>" marker, following `dispatch-window-hold.ts`'s banner convention
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatch-window-hold.ts` — Reference implementation for the read-only banner; extend or mirror for not-yet-started items
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-filter.ts` — Filter out not-yet-started items from the Herdr list-head dispatch pipeline
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.gates.ts` — Add the `startOnNotReached` gate (never dispatch a future item)
- `src/commands/export.ts` / `src/commands/import.ts` — Round-trip `startOn`; legacy rows without it import as `createdAt`
- `src/doctor/` — Add a mismatch check (`startOn` missing ≠ `createdAt`) to `wl doctor`
- `docs/CLI.md` — Document `--start-on`, `--include-not-started`, `--starts-before`
- `docs/DATA_FORMAT.md` — Document the `startOn` field and its `createdAt` default
- `docs/API.md` — Document `startOn` in every JSON surface
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — Document `startOn` scheduling and the claim guard
- `docs/migrations/` — Add the migration note

## Existing state

- No `startOn` field exists anywhere in the codebase.
- Current practice: `[run-not-before YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ]` prefix in item titles, parsed manually by agents.
- Items created 2026-11-18 from the `llm` abort-class remediation chain (`LP-0MWM0B7IQ008W2FP`) encode scheduling in titles.

## Definition of done

A `llm`-style dated work item created with `--start-on 2026-11-19T10:25:00Z` is invisible to `wl next`, `wl search`, `wl list` and the Herdr worklist until that instant, visible with `--include-not-started`, retrievable by id, claimable only after the instant (or by explicit audited override), and survives export/import and a restart unchanged.

## Related work

- LP-0MWM0B7IQ008W2FP — `llm` abort-class remediation chain (explicitly scheduled by title dates; blocked on this feature)
- WL-0MVR8FN1D002SCIR — Held-items banner convention (reference for Herdr worklist UI marker)

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk (scope creep):** `startOn` invites adjacent scheduling features (recurrence, calendar, timezone UI, auto re-anchoring). Mitigation: non-goals are explicit above; extra opportunities become linked work items, not scope.
- **Risk (silent behaviour change):** filtering by default could hide items an operator expects to see. Mitigation: the default is `createdAt`, so every existing item is already "started" and stays visible — the filter only bites on newly authored dates; `--include-not-started` is the escape hatch and not-yet-started items are surfaced read-only in the worklist rather than hidden.
- **Risk (clock flakiness):** future/past comparisons against wall-clock make tests non-deterministic. Mitigation: inject the clock through the shared predicate; AC7 requires a frozen-clock test.
- **Risk (sync resurrection):** a two-way sync could resurrect a stale `startOn` from the remote. Mitigation: AC6 requires two-way sync to never resurrect a stale value, covered by a sync round-trip test.
- **Risk (performance regression):** a non-indexed `startOn` predicate on every search surface could slow `list`/`search`/`next`. Mitigation: AC9 requires an index (or an equivalent query plan) with recorded before/after benchmarks.
- **Assumption:** `createdAt` is always present and non-empty on every existing row, so "default = `createdAt`" needs no fallback beyond the migration back-fill.
- **Assumption:** `startOn` composes with existing gates (dependency readiness, assignee hold, `needsProducerReview`) rather than replacing any of them — the new filter is an additional sequential filter.
- **Assumption:** the downtime dispatcher and `llm`-style dated items are the first consumers; no other project relies on title-embedded dates programmatically.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- No clarifying questions — the seed context (work item description) provides sufficient detail for a clear brief. The description was authored by the downtime dispatcher and contains a complete spec with 9 acceptance criteria, constraints, and definition of done.

## Review stages (automated, completed)

## Decisions taken (reversible)

- **D1 — `startOn` is always stored populated** as the effective instant
  (`startOn ?? createdAt`); a `NULL` on a legacy row reads as `createdAt`. This
  keeps the default-filter query a single-column comparison so the `startOn`
  index (AC9) is actually used, instead of a `COALESCE(startOn, createdAt)`
  expression that defeats a plain index.
- **D2 — unparseable `startOn` is treated as *started* (fail-open).** AC1 pins
  the back-compat default as "never blocked"; `startOn` is a scheduling gate,
  not a security control, so an unreadable value must not hide an item. AC2's
  authoring validation means this should be unreachable.
- **D3 — a bare date (`2026-11-19`) is rejected.** Its timezone would be
  ambiguous and AC2 requires invalid values to fail actionably.
- **D4 — the refusal token is `start_on_not_reached`** (AC5). The override flag
  is proposed as `--force-start-on <reason>`; the implementer may rename it if
  the CLI's flag conventions demand, provided it stays auditable.
- **D5 — the boundary is inclusive:** `startOn == now` counts as *started*.
- **D6 — both opt-ins ship:** `--include-not-started` **and** `--starts-before
  <ISO>` (AC3 allows "and/or"), composing as "not started AND starting before
  `<ISO>`". `--starts-before` is what a scheduler-facing caller actually wants.
- **D7 — child priorities:** `high` for the six functional slices, `medium` for
  the docs/perf slice. The parent stays `critical`.
- **D8 — no standalone horizontal "tests" children.** Each slice owns its own
  tests; slice 1 owns the shared frozen-clock harness so the test-first
  requirement is met structurally.

## Open questions (non-blocking — producer may override)

- **OPEN QUESTION (for the Producer).** Should the claim-guard override be
  restricted to named actors (e.g. the producer sentinel `Map`) or open to any
  agent? *Proposed default:* open to any actor, with the override comment
  recording the actor and reason as the audit trail (AC5). Not blocking —
  slice 5 can ship the permissive form and tighten later.
- **OPEN QUESTION (for the Producer).** Does `startOn` need to appear in the TUI
  worklist (`packages/tui`) as well as Herdr? AC4 scopes Herdr only, so the TUI
  is out of scope by omission. *Proposed default:* out of scope; raise a
  separate work item if wanted. Not blocking.
- **OPEN QUESTION (for the Producer).** Should existing `[run-not-before …]`
  title prefixes be rewritten once `startOn` exists? *Proposed default:* no —
  automatic re-anchoring is an explicit non-goal; the `llm` abort-class chain
  (`LP-0MWM0B7IQ008W2FP`) re-authors its own titles when it unblocks. Not
  blocking.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

it carries nine acceptance criteria, explicit non-goals, constraints, risks,

recorded here with explicit preferred options so a producer can confirm or

  non-blocking.**
- **Q2 (plan → producer).** "Is the TUI worklist in scope for the
  not-yet-started marker, or is Herdr parity sufficient?"
  **Answer:** not answered by a producer. *Plan agent's proposed default:*
  Herdr only. Evidence: AC4 names "Worklist, dispatcher and audit-pickup
  queries" in the Herdr plugin and does not mention `packages/tui`. Status:
  **proposed, non-blocking.**
- **Q3 (plan → producer).** "Should existing `[run-not-before …]` title prefixes
  be rewritten as part of this work?" **Answer:** not answered by a producer.
  *Plan agent's proposed default:* no rewrite. Evidence: the parent's non-goals
  exclude "automatic re-anchoring of dates", and
  `LP-0MWM0B7IQ008W2FP` is the consumer that owns its own titles. Status:
  **proposed, non-blocking.**

Research performed (no questions raised, recorded for traceability):

- **Duplicate-work detection** — `wl search startOn`, `wl search run-not-before`
  and `wl list startOn` each return only this parent item. No overlapping
  completed or in-flight item exists, so nothing was closed or rewritten as a

  is the shared browse-feed path used by `wl next`, `wl worklist` and the Herdr
  fetchers; the intake comment on this item flags it as the single place AC4

- **Reference convention** — `packages/herdr/src/dispatch-window-hold.ts`
  (WL-0MVR8FN1D002SCIR) supplies the read-only header-count + banner pattern

- **Gate-token pattern** — `ClassifyGateToken` in

  `startOnNotReached` gate extends it rather than introducing a parallel
  mechanism.
- **Schema state** — `SCHEMA_VERSION = 9` in
  `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` and `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION = '9'`
  in `src/migrations/index.ts` must be bumped together in slice 2.

## Plan: changelog

# `isNotStarted` predicate, frozen-clock harness and perf baseline

## Goal

Deliver the shared "is this item not yet started?" predicate that every later
`startOn` slice consumes, together with the deterministic test harness that
keeps its comparisons off the wall clock, and the performance baseline recorded
*before* any filtering or index lands.

This is the test-first foundation slice: it ships code, tests and a recorded
baseline, and changes no CLI or Herdr behaviour.

## Context

`startOn` does not exist yet. Everything else in this epic (schema, authoring,
default filtering, the claim guard, Herdr parity) reads the predicate defined
here, so it lands first and is depended on by all siblings.

## Impact

Work items scheduled for a future date now have one deterministic, test-verified definition of "not yet started", so they become available exactly at their start instant on every surface and no clock-dependent flakiness can make a future item appear early or hide a started one.

## Acceptance Criteria

### Predicate and harness

- [ ] `isNotStarted(item, now)` is exported from
  `packages/shared/src/predicates.ts` and published via the existing
  `@worklog/shared/predicates` subpath (the root `@worklog/shared` entry is a
  frozen surface — never add an export there).
- [ ] Effective start instant resolution is `startOn ?? createdAt`, so the
  default is `createdAt` and every pre-existing item is already "started"
  (back-compat is the default, never "blocked").
- [ ] `now` is an explicit parameter (milliseconds) — no `Date.now()` call
  inside the predicate, so tests are deterministic.
- [ ] A shared frozen-clock test helper is added (e.g.
  `tests/helpers/frozen-clock.ts`) and used by every new `startOn`
  test in this epic.
- [ ] Unit tests cover: `startOn` in the future → not started; `startOn` in the
  past → started; `startOn` exactly equal to `now` → started (boundary is
  inclusive); `startOn` absent with past `createdAt` → started; `startOn`
  absent with future `createdAt` → not started; `startOn` absent and
  `createdAt` absent → started; unparseable `startOn` → started (fail-open:
  an unreadable value must never hide an item).
- [ ] The predicate handles ISO-8601 with a UTC offset (`+01:00`) and a `Z`
  suffix identically.

### Performance baseline

- [ ] Baseline `list` / `search` / `next` latency is measured on the existing
  large-db harness (`packages/herdr/test/perf/large-db-harness.ts`) and the
  figures are recorded in `docs/benchmarks/start_on_filter_baseline.md` with
  the store size and the measurement method.

### Non-goals

- No schema change, no CLI flag, no Herdr change in this slice.


### Parent acceptance criteria satisfied (restated verbatim)

These restate the covering parent acceptance criteria word for word so
the parent/child AC-coverage check is exact.

- [ ] **AC7 — Tests.** Unit and integration coverage for: default = `createdAt`; future-filtered out of every search surface listed in AC3; opt-in shows them marked; `--start-on` set/clear; claim refused and overridden; legacy JSONL import back-fill; sync round-trip; a frozen-clock test (no wall-clock flakiness).
- [ ] **AC9 — Performance.** An index on `startOn` (or an equivalent query plan) so `list`/`search`/`next` stay within the existing benchmarks on the current store size; record the before/after figures.

## Key Files

- `packages/shared/src/predicates.ts` — add the `isNotStarted` export
- `packages/shared/src/database/work-items.ts` — existing predicate home for reference
- `tests/helpers/frozen-clock.ts` — new frozen-clock helper
- `packages/shared/src/predicates.test.ts` — new unit tests
- `packages/herdr/test/perf/large-db-harness.ts` — baseline harness
- `docs/benchmarks/start_on_filter_baseline.md` — recorded baseline

## Dependencies

None — this is the first slice.

## Deliverables

- `isNotStarted` predicate with injectable clock, exported via the predicates subpath.
- Frozen-clock test helper used by all later `startOn` tests.
- Recorded pre-filter performance baseline.

# `startOn` data model, schema migration and sync round-trip

## Goal

Add `startOn` as a first-class stored field: a SQLite column, the type and
field-registry entries, an idempotent back-fill migration for existing rows, a
`doctor` mismatch check, and a JSONL export/import + Git sync round-trip that
never resurrects a stale value.

This is the vertical data slice — schema through to persisted bytes and back.

## Context

`startOn` does not exist anywhere in the codebase today. `SCHEMA_VERSION` is
`9` (`packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts`) and
`CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION` is `'9'` (`src/migrations/index.ts`); both must be
bumped by exactly one step, reconciled in the same change. Scheduling is
currently encoded as a `[run-not-before …]` title prefix that nothing enforces.

Depends on the `isNotStarted` predicate slice for the shared clock-injectable
predicate and the frozen-clock test harness.

## Impact

Scheduled work is now a stored, indexed field that defaults to when the item was created, so an item can carry a real future start time that survives export, import and Git sync and that `wl doctor` can verify — instead of a date hidden in the title that nothing enforces.

## Acceptance Criteria

### Data model

- [ ] `startOn` is added to `WorkItem`, `CreateWorkItemInput` and
  `UpdateWorkItemInput` as an optional ISO-8601 UTC string in
  `packages/shared/src/types.ts`.
- [ ] `startOn` is added to `VALID_FIELDS` in `packages/shared/src/fields.ts`
  so generic field reads/writes see it.
- [ ] A `startOn TEXT` column is added to the `workitems` table DDL in
  `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts`, with `SCHEMA_VERSION` bumped.
- [ ] An index on `startOn` (or a documented equivalent query plan) is created
  so the default-filter query keeps using an index rather than a table scan.
- [ ] **`startOn` is always populated on write** — it is stored as the
  effective instant (`startOn ?? createdAt`), so queries compare a single
  non-null column and never need `COALESCE` over two columns. A `NULL`
  `startOn` is read as `createdAt` for back-compat.
- [ ] **Default = the item's `createdAt`** when omitted, including on import of
  legacy JSONL/Git data that has no field (back-compat is the default, never
  "blocked").

### Migration and doctor

- [ ] An idempotent migration is added to `src/migrations/index.ts` setting
  `startOn = createdAt` for existing rows whose `startOn` is `NULL`, and
  `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION` is bumped to match `SCHEMA_VERSION`.
- [ ] The migration is documented in `docs/migrations/start_on.md` and
  registered so `wl doctor upgrade` lists it.
- [ ] `wl doctor` reports a mismatch where `startOn` is missing/null and
  differs from `createdAt`, with a remediation hint.
- [ ] Re-running the migration is a no-op (idempotence) and is covered by a
  test.

### Sync and export/import

- [ ] JSONL export/import round-trips `startOn`; legacy rows without the field
  import as `createdAt`.
- [ ] Two-way sync never resurrects a stale `startOn` (newest-write-wins on the
  same semantics as the other mutable fields), covered by a sync round-trip
  test.
- [ ] Cross-project dependency edges (foreign ids) are unaffected.
- [ ] `startOn` appears in every JSON surface: `show`, `list`, `search`,
  `next`, `recent`, `in_progress` and the dependency listings.

### Tests

- [ ] Unit/integration tests: default = `createdAt`; legacy JSONL import
  back-fill; sync round-trip; migration idempotence; `doctor` mismatch
  detection; all use the frozen-clock harness.


### Parent acceptance criteria satisfied (restated verbatim)

These restate the covering parent acceptance criteria word for word so
the parent/child AC-coverage check is exact.

- [ ] **AC1 — Data model.** `startOn` is stored per work item as an ISO-8601 UTC timestamp, exposed in every JSON surface (`show`, `list`, `search`, `next`, `recent`, `in_progress`, dependency listings). **Default = the item's `createdAt`** when omitted, including on import of legacy JSONL/Git data that has no field (back-compat is the default, never "blocked").
- [ ] **AC6 — Migration and sync.** A documented, idempotent migration sets `startOn = createdAt` for existing items (`docs/migrations/`); `doctor` reports a mismatch; JSONL export/import and Git sync round-trip the field; cross-project edges (foreign ids) are unaffected; two-way sync never resurrects a stale value.

## Key Files

- `packages/shared/src/types.ts` — `WorkItem`, `CreateWorkItemInput`, `UpdateWorkItemInput`
- `packages/shared/src/fields.ts` — `VALID_FIELDS`
- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` — table DDL, `SCHEMA_VERSION`, JSONL projections, index
- `packages/shared/src/database/work-items.ts` — row mapping / read path
- `src/migrations/index.ts` — back-fill migration, `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION`
- `src/commands/export.ts` — export projection
- `src/commands/import.ts` — legacy back-fill on import
- `src/commands/doctor.ts` — mismatch check
- `src/doctor/` — check implementation
- `docs/migrations/start_on.md` — migration note

## Dependencies

- Depends on: `isNotStarted` predicate, frozen-clock harness and perf baseline (sibling slice 1).

## Deliverables

- Stored, indexed, always-populated `startOn` column with `createdAt` default.
- Idempotent back-fill migration + `doctor` mismatch report.
- Lossless export/import and sync round-trip.

# CLI authoring: `--start-on` on `wl create` and `wl update`

## Goal

Let operators and agents set, change and clear `startOn` from the CLI with
strict validation — the authoring half of the feature, end to end through
option parsing, normalisation, storage and `wl show` output.

## Context

The field is stored and round-tripped by the data-model slice, but nothing can
write a non-default value yet. AC2 also pins the guarantee that `wl show <id>`
is never filtered, so an item is always retrievable by id no matter its
`startOn`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `wl create --start-on <ISO-8601>` accepts a full ISO-8601 timestamp,
  **accepts a UTC offset** (`+01:00`) and normalises it to UTC `Z` form before
  storage.
- [x] `wl update <id> --start-on <ISO-8601>` behaves identically.
- [x] `--start-on ""` clears the value back to the item's `createdAt`.
- [x] An invalid value fails with an actionable message that names the flag,
  the received value and an accepted example, and the command exits non-zero
  without writing.
- [x] A bare date (`2026-11-19`) is **rejected** with the same actionable
  message (a bare date is not a date/time, and its timezone would be
  ambiguous), covered by a test. Rationale: AC2 requires invalid values to
  fail with an actionable message, and silently assuming midnight UTC would
  make a scheduling gate fire 24h early or late in some timezone.
- [x] `wl show <id>` is **never** filtered — an item is always retrievable by
  id, and the output includes `startOn`.
- [x] `wl create --help` and `wl update --help` describe the field, its
  ISO-8601 offset acceptance, the `createdAt` default and the `""` clear form.
- [x] Tests: set / clear / offset normalisation / invalid rejection / bare-date
  behaviour / `show` retrieval of a future item, all on the frozen clock.

## Impact

Operators and agents can now schedule a work item for a future instant from the CLI (`--start-on`), see it in `wl show`, and clear it back to the creation time, with ambiguous values rejected before anything is written.

### Parent acceptance criteria satisfied (restated verbatim)

These restate the covering parent acceptance criteria word for word so
the parent/child AC-coverage check is exact.

- [ ] **AC2 — CLI authoring.** `wl create --start-on <ISO-8601>` and `wl update <id> --start-on <ISO-8601>` (offset accepted, normalised to UTC); `--start-on ""` clears it back to `createdAt`. Invalid values fail with an actionable message. `wl show <id>` is **never** filtered — an item is always retrievable by id.

## Key Files

- `src/commands/create.ts` — `--start-on` option, normalisation, `createdAt` default
- `src/commands/update.ts` — `--start-on` option, `""` clear form
- `src/argv-normalize.ts` — shared option parsing helpers (if applicable)
- `src/commands/show.ts` — confirm `startOn` in output and no filtering
- `tests/cli/create-start-on.test.ts` — option tests
- `tests/cli/update-start-on.test.ts` — option tests
- `docs/CLI.md` — flag documentation

## Dependencies

- Depends on: `startOn` data model, schema migration and sync round-trip (sibling slice 2).

## Deliverables

- Working `--start-on` on `create` and `update`, offset-normalised, validated, clearable.
- Help text and `CLI.md` coverage for the new flag.

# Default filtering across the CLI search surfaces

## Goal

Make every CLI search surface hide not-yet-started items by default, with an
explicit opt-in that still shows them — marked — in both text and JSON output.
One shared filter, applied once, so `next`, `worklist` and Herdr cannot diverge.

## Context

The choke point is `src/worklist-selection.ts` (`selectBrowseFeed`), which
`wl next`, `wl worklist` and the Herdr fetchers all go through. The filter
belongs there plus the per-command read paths, never forked per command
(intake note on the parent item). `in_progress` items are never filtered out —
a started item has already started.

## Acceptance Criteria

### Default exclusion

- [ ] `wl list`, `wl search`, `wl next`, `wl in_progress`, `wl recent` and the
  equivalent JSON paths **exclude** items whose `startOn` is in the future.
- [ ] `wl worklist` (the consolidated `db.list()` + shared browse-feed read)
  applies the same default filter to every subset.
- [ ] The shared browse-feed selection (`src/worklist-selection.ts`) carries
  the filter so `next`, `worklist` and the Herdr fetchers agree by construction.
- [ ] `in_progress` items are never filtered out, even if their `startOn` is in
  the future (`wl in_progress` and the `in_progress` subset of `worklist`).
- [ ] `wl show <id>` remains unfiltered.

### Opt-in

- [ ] An explicit opt-in (`--include-not-started`, and/or `--starts-before
  <ISO>`) shows not-yet-started items on every surface listed above.
- [ ] Opted-in items are marked as not yet started in **both** text and JSON
  output. Text carries a trailing marker in the same bracketed style the
  worklist already uses for `[held: N by Map]`:
  `[not started until 2026-11-19T10:25:00Z]` (effective `startOn`, UTC `Z`
  form). JSON carries `notStarted: true` alongside the effective `startOn`.
- [ ] `--include-not-started` and `--starts-before <ISO>` compose: with both,
  the window is "not started AND starting before `<ISO>`".
- [ ] The filter is clock-injectable through the shared predicate so tests use
  a frozen clock.

### Tests

- [ ] Tests prove a future item is excluded from each surface in the list
  above, included with the opt-in, and correctly marked in text and JSON.
- [ ] A test proves an `in_progress` item with a future `startOn` still appears.


### Parent acceptance criteria satisfied (restated verbatim)

These restate the covering parent acceptance criteria word for word so
the parent/child AC-coverage check is exact.

- [ ] **AC3 — Default filtering in searches.** `wl list`, `wl search`, `wl next`, `wl in_progress`, `wl recent` and the equivalent JSON paths **exclude** items whose `startOn` is in the future. An explicit opt-in (`--include-not-started`, and/or `--starts-before <ISO>`) shows them, marked as not yet started in both text and JSON output. `in_progress` items are never filtered out (a started item has already started).

## Key Files

- `src/commands/list.ts` — default exclusion + opt-in flags
- `src/commands/search.ts` — same default exclusion + opt-in
- `src/commands/next.ts` — browse-feed selection
- `src/commands/in-progress.ts` — exclusion, never filtering in-progress items
- `src/commands/recent.ts` — exclusion + opt-in
- `src/commands/worklist.ts` — consolidated read, same filter for every subset
- `src/worklist-selection.ts` — shared browse-feed filter (single choke point)
- `packages/shared/src/database/next-pipeline.ts` — selection query
- `src/cli-output.ts` — the not-yet-started marker in text/JSON output
- `docs/CLI.md` — `--include-not-started` / `--starts-before`

## Dependencies

- Depends on: `isNotStarted` predicate slice (1).
- Depends on: `startOn` data model slice (2).
- Depends on: CLI authoring slice (3) — integration tests author future items with `--start-on`.

## Deliverables

- Default exclusion of not-yet-started items on all six CLI search surfaces.
- `--include-not-started` / `--starts-before` opt-in with a text and JSON marker.
- Shared browse-feed filter that Herdr inherits.
data.title: Filter not-yet-started items by default across CLI search surfaces

# Claim guard: refuse a future claim with an audited override

## Goal

Make it structurally impossible to claim work that has not started yet —
while keeping a deliberate, audited escape hatch for an operator who needs to
start early.

## Context

Defence in depth: the default filter (slice 4) hides future items, but a direct
`wl update <id> --status in_progress` or an explicit id-targeted claim must
still be refused. The refusal must be machine-readable so Herdr and skill
scripts can branch on it rather than parse prose. `src/claim-hold.ts` and
`src/claim-hold-read.ts` host the existing claim-path surfaces; the Herdr claim
path is `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.claim.ts` / `index.claim.ts`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Setting an item to `in_progress` (or any claim path, including the Herdr
  claim and the `StatusLifecycle` claim helper) on a future `startOn` is
  **refused** with the machine-readable reason `start_on_not_reached` in JSON
  output, and a non-zero exit.
- [ ] The refusal message names the item's effective `startOn` and how long
  until it is reached.
- [ ] An explicit, auditable override is available (proposed flag:
  `--force-start-on <reason>`; the implementer may rename it if the CLI
  convention demands) — when passed, the claim proceeds **and** a comment is
  written naming the actor, the reason and the `startOn` that was overridden.
- [ ] The override comment is visible in `wl show <id>` comments and survives
  export/import.
- [ ] The guard must **not** fire for `createdAt`-defaulted items, nor for any
  item whose effective `startOn` is at or before `now`.
- [ ] The guard composes with the existing gates — it never replaces the
  `assignee` hold, dependency readiness or `needsProducerReview`, and is an
  additional sequential refusal.
- [ ] Tests: claim refused; claim allowed after the instant (frozen clock);
  override succeeds and writes the audited comment; `createdAt`-defaulted items
  never refused.


### Parent acceptance criteria satisfied (restated verbatim)

These restate the covering parent acceptance criteria word for word so
the parent/child AC-coverage check is exact.

- [ ] **AC5 — Claim guard (defence in depth).** Setting an item to `in_progress` (or any claim path) on a future `startOn` is refused with a machine-readable reason (`start_on_not_reached`) unless an explicit, auditable override is passed; the override writes a comment naming the actor and the reason. The guard must not fire for `createdAt`-defaulted items.

## Key Files

- `src/commands/update.ts` — the `--status in_progress` transition and the override flag
- `src/claim-hold.ts` — claim-path policy surface
- `src/claim-hold-read.ts` — claim-path read surface
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.claim.ts` — Herdr claim path
- `packages/herdr/src/index.claim.ts` — Herdr claim wiring
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.gates.ts` — dispatch-side refusal token
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.offer-attribution.ts` — `ClassifyGateToken` union
- `docs/CLI.md` — refusal reason and override flag

## Dependencies

- Depends on: `isNotStarted` predicate slice (1).
- Depends on: `startOn` data model slice (2).
- Depends on: CLI authoring slice (3) — tests author future items with `--start-on`.

## Deliverables

- `start_on_not_reached` refusal across every claim path.
- Audited override that records actor, reason and the overridden instant.

# Herdr parity: dispatch gate and read-only worklist marker

## Goal

Guarantee a not-yet-started item is never dispatched or claimed by any Herdr
worker, while the operator can still *see* it in the worklist with a
"not started until <date>" marker — read-only, never altered.

## Context

Herdr has two distinct paths: the *queries* it issues through `wl` (and the
`fetcher*` family), and its own local dispatch pipeline
(`downtime-worker.dispatch-filter.ts` → `classifyItemForDispatchDetail` in
`downtime-worker.gates.ts`). Parity requires both. The read-only banner
convention is `packages/herdr/src/dispatch-window-hold.ts`
(WL-0MVR8FN1D002SCIR): derived from items the worklist has *already* fetched,
no extra `wl` spawn, no mutation, no second ranking path. Mirror it.

## Acceptance Criteria

### Never dispatch a future item

- [ ] Worklist, dispatcher and audit-pickup queries apply the same default
  filter as the CLI, so a future item is never dispatched or claimed by any
  Herdr worker.
- [ ] A dedicated `startOnNotReached` gate is added to
  `classifyItemForDispatchDetail` (as a new `ClassifyGateToken` member) and
  refuses at **every** tier (intake, plan, risk-effort, implement, audit).
- [ ] The Herdr list-head dispatch pipeline
  (`downtime-worker.dispatch-filter.ts`) filters not-yet-started items out of
  its candidate set.
- [ ] The gate is clock-injectable and covered by a frozen-clock test proving
  no tier can select a future item.

### Read-only visibility

- [ ] Not-yet-started items are surfaced **read-only** in the worklist with a
  "not started until <date>" marker.
- [ ] The marker follows the existing held-items banner convention
  (WL-0MVR8FN1D002SCIR): a header count plus a banner, derived from the
  already-fetched window, with no additional `wl` subprocess and no second
  ranking path. Concretely, mirroring `assigneeHoldStatusText` /
  `assigneeHoldBannerText`:
  - header indicator `[not started: N]`, `null` when N is 0 (no chrome for the
    common case);
  - banner `Not started — all N of M dispatch-window item(s) start after
    <earliest startOn>; no downtime dispatch possible`, rendered only when the
    whole window is not-yet-started.
- [ ] A per-row marker `[not started until <date>]` distinguishes individual
  not-yet-started rows from already-started ones.
- [ ] The surface never clears or alters the item's state — no claim, no
  status/stage write, no `startOn` change (strictly read-only, mirroring
  `dispatch-window-hold.ts` AC4).
- [ ] Existing held-items semantics are unchanged: a held item is still
  reported by the hold banner, and an item that is both held and not started
  does not double-count in a way that misreports either bucket.
- [ ] Tests: the marker renders for a future item; the banner appears when the
  whole window is not-yet-started; no mutation is performed.


### Parent acceptance criteria satisfied (restated verbatim)

These restate the covering parent acceptance criteria word for word so
the parent/child AC-coverage check is exact.

- [ ] **AC4 — Herdr plugin parity.** Worklist, dispatcher and audit-pickup queries apply the same default filter, so a future item is never dispatched or claimed by any Herdr worker. Surface not-yet-started items **read-only** in the worklist with a "not started until <date>" marker, following the existing held-items banner convention (WL-0MVR8FN1D002SCIR), and never clear or alter their state.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — surface the marker
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatch-window-hold.ts` — reference banner implementation
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.detail.ts` — detail rendering
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.meta.ts` — header counts
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-filter.ts` — list-head dispatch pipeline
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.gates.ts` — `startOnNotReached` gate
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.offer-attribution.ts` — `ClassifyGateToken`
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — CLI-backed query path
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.api.ts` — in-process query path

# Placement gate false-positive blocks epic driving on a busy machine

## Problem statement

`implement.py parent <epic>` refuses to proceed for an epic child whose
worktree exists but holds no changes whenever **any** other registered
worktree of the repository is dirty:

```
ERROR: Child WL-... produced changes in the sibling worktree
.../worktrees/wl-WL-0MVOA0XVC... instead of its worktree ...
Offending paths: ...
```

`_child_main_checkout_violation` (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`)
treats "child worktree clean + sibling worktree dirty" as evidence that the
child wrote outside its tree. Condition 3 of its documented precision rule
says pre-existing/unrelated dirt must not block a legitimate child, but the
code only earns that exemption when the child's own worktree already holds
changes — which a **freshly started child never does**. The result: on a
machine running several concurrent dispatches (the normal steady state),
`parent` and `drive` fail closed before the first child session is ever
spawned.

## Evidence (captured 2026-11-18, parent epic WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9)

1. `implement.py parent WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9` started child
   WL-0MWKY141H002LULI and created its (empty) worktree.
2. `implement.py drive WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9` then failed in `phase_parent`
   with one message per dirty sibling worktree:
   - `wl-WL-0MVOA0XVC0002PBG-...` (item soft-deleted, 3 dirty paths)
   - `wl-WL-0MVOBP8MC0093Y7T-...` (blocked item, 22 dirty paths)
   - `wl-WL-0MWKQ51G0006F3KV-...` (live concurrent dispatch, 15 dirty paths)
   - `wl-WL-0MWMGEL5R003IH71-...` (6 dirty paths)
   - `/tmp/wl-base-check`, `/tmp/wl-clean-check`, ... (1 dirty path each)
   `sessions_spawned: 0` — no child session ran, so no child work existed.
3. Removing the empty worktree (`implement.py abort`) and re-running `drive`
   let the chain start normally: `phase_start` recreated the tree and the
   session was spawned, precisely because no clean worktree existed at the
   moment the placement check ran.

## Desired change

A freshly started child (worktree created, no session spawned against it yet)
must never be reported as a placement violation because of dirt in a
*different* work item's worktree. Candidate treatments, in order of
preference:

- Exempt a child whose worktree was created by this run's `phase_start` and
  has never had a session spawned against it (the same shape as the existing
  `read_spawn_failure` exemption).
- Restrict the sibling scan to worktrees whose dirt this child's session could
  have produced (age ordering vs the child worktree creation time).
- At minimum, fail-open (WARNING) when the offending sibling belongs to an
  independently live, non-terminal item (a concurrent dispatch), keeping the
  hard failure only for siblings whose item is terminal (deleted/completed),
  where the dirt genuinely is orphaned.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A unit test drives `phase_parent`/`_child_main_checkout_violation` with a
  clean child worktree and at least one dirty sibling worktree owned by a
  distinct non-terminal item and asserts the child is reported startable, not
  failed.
- A second test pins the genuine case that must stay fail-closed: dirt in a
  sibling worktree attributable to this child's own session still fails
  placement.
- `implement.py drive <epic>` completes its first `parent` step and spawns the
  first child session on a repository where other items' worktrees are dirty.
- No existing placement/attribution test regresses.

## Impact

An epic can be driven on a machine that is also running other dispatches,
instead of the driver dead-ending before the first child session.

# implement.py abort leaves the item branch behind, so the next start cannot create a worktree

## Problem statement

`implement.py abort <id>` resets the item to `open`, removes the worktree and
deletes the state file — but it leaves the item's branch
(`wl-<id>-<slug>`) in the repository. A subsequent `implement.py start <id>`
(or `parent`/`drive` re-starting the same child) then fails:

```
{
  "phase": "start",
  "success": false,
  "worktree_path": "",
  "message": "Failed to create worktree at
    /home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug> from dev"
}
```

`git worktree add -b <branch> <path> dev` refuses because the branch already
exists. Recovery is an undocumented manual step: `git branch -D <branch>`.

## Evidence (2026-11-18, epic WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9, child WL-0MWKY141H002LULI)

1. `implement.py parent WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9` created the child worktree and
   branch `wl-WL-0MWKY141H002LULI-record-per-project-fairness-metric-on-di`
   at `39b10762d` (= `dev`), no commits.
2. `implement.py abort WL-0MWKY141H002LULI` reported success and removed the
   worktree; `git branch` still listed the branch.
3. `implement.py drive WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9` failed immediately with
   `"Failed to start child WL-0MWKY141H002LULI"` →
   `"Failed to create worktree ... from dev"`.
4. `git branch -D wl-WL-0MWKY141H002LULI-...` followed by a re-run of `drive`
   started the child successfully.

## Desired change

`phase_start` should be idempotent with respect to a leftover branch created
by a previous `start`/`abort` cycle for the **same** work item:

- when the branch exists and is contained in the parent branch (no commits
  ahead: `git rev-list --count dev..<branch> == 0`), re-use it
  (`git worktree add <path> <branch>`) instead of failing;
- when the branch exists with commits ahead, either continue that work (the
  existing-work semantics) or refuse with an actionable message naming the
  exact recovery command — never a bare "Failed to create worktree".

Alternatively (or additionally), `phase_abort` deletes the branch it created
when it holds no commits ahead of the parent branch, so an aborted item is
genuinely re-startable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A test creates a worktree via `start`, aborts it, then calls `start` again
  and asserts the second call succeeds with a worktree at the same path.
- A test pins the pre-existing-branch-with-work case: a branch holding
  commits ahead of the parent is never silently discarded, and the refusal
  message names the recovery command.
- If abort is chosen as the fix point: a test asserts `abort` removes a
  branch that has no commits ahead of the parent branch, and leaves a
  branch with commits alone.
- No existing worktree/abort/cleanup test regresses.

## Impact

An interrupted or aborted implementation can be restarted with one command
instead of failing and requiring a manual `git branch -D`.

Discovered from WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9 (deps: discovered-from:WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9).

# Intake Brief — Priority-first section ordering for the sprint view

## Problem statement

In the herdr sprint view (`f-s-s` → `/wl`) and the core `wl next --groups` output, sections are bucketed by **stage**, not priority, so a medium-priority `plan_complete` item renders above a high-priority `idea` item. Priority is only ever a *within-section* sort key.

## Users

- **Producers browsing the sprint view** (`f-s-s`).
  - *As a producer, I want high-priority work shown above medium-priority work regardless of its stage, so the top of my sprint view is genuinely the most urgent work.*
- **CLI users running `wl next --groups`** — the same ordering contract applies, so the fix must land in both copies.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` → `assignItemGroups` buckets by stage: `Critical Group N` → `Group N` (in-progress / `plan_complete` / `intake_complete`) → `Idea` → `Other` → `In Review`.
- `src/commands/grouping.ts` → `assignItemGroups` is the core duplicate used by `wl next --groups`; both module headers state the copies must be kept in sync.
- `compareGroupableItems` already sorts priority-first *within* a section (WL-0MVVLBTTP003Y4XO), but the section boundaries themselves are stage-derived.
- `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts` → `selectWorkItems` slices the non-mandatory `others` in raw `wl next` score order before truncating to `othersLimit`. Because `computeScore` (`packages/shared/src/database/sort.ts`) awards +3500 to a fresh audit-not-ready item, a medium (2000 + 3500 = 5500) outranks a plain high (3000) — so a medium can be *selected* while a high is cut from the sprint window entirely.
- Precedent: `Bubble up critical items (WL-0MR1COW20005IO1C)` introduced the priority-band-first mechanism for `critical` only. This item generalises it to every non-critical band.

## Desired change

Order sections by priority band first; use stage/state only as the intra-band tie-breaker and for selection tie-breaking.

1. **Bucket order** — priority band first: `critical` → `high` → `medium` → `low`. Within a band the stage sub-order is the tie-breaker: `status === 'in-progress'` → `plan_complete` → `intake_complete` → `idea` → other.
2. **`In Review` stays pinned last** — a single global section rendered after every band; it never moves into its own priority band (explicit exception — the review queue is mandatory and always shown).
3. **File-path conflict grouping preserved within each band** — greedy first-fit, max 3 file-path groups per band-section; items with no Key Files remain singleton groups. "Two items sharing a Key File never share a file-path group" continues to hold *within* a band.
4. **Selection** — the non-mandatory `others` slice is ordered priority-first, with the existing `wl next` score as the tie-break, *before* the `othersLimit` truncation. Highs can therefore never be displaced by mediums when more highs exist than the window allows.
5. **Labels** — extend the existing `Critical Group N` scheme to `High Group N` / `Medium Group N` / `Low Group N` with each band's stage sub-sections, and `In Review` last. The core `wl next --groups` output changes with herdr (deliberate; both copies in lockstep).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A mixed set of `high@idea` and `medium@plan_complete` items is regrouped so every high item's group number is lower than every medium item's — the inversion is gone.
- Section order is `critical` → `high` → `medium` → `low` → `In Review`, independent of stage.
- Within a priority band the stage sub-order is `status='in-progress'` → `plan_complete` → `intake_complete` → `idea` → other; stage never reorders across priorities.
- `In Review` is rendered as the final single section regardless of the priority of its members.
- Two items in the same priority band sharing a Key File never share a file-path group; the 3-file-path-group cap applies per band-section; items with no Key Files remain singleton groups.
- With 5 high and 2 medium non-mandatory items and `othersLimit = 3`, all 3 selected `others` are high-priority — no medium displaces a high.
- The always-show mandatory guarantee is unchanged: every `critical`, `in-progress`, `blocked` and `completed`/`in_review` item is still selected regardless of the window.
- Grouping remains a pure function of item content — no dependence on `updatedAt`, arrival order, or pin-map insertion order.
- Section labels follow the band scheme: `Critical Group N`, `High Group N`, `Medium Group N`, `Low Group N`; no non-critical section is labelled plain `Group N`.
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` and `src/commands/grouping.ts` implement the identical order and stay in sync; `wl next --groups` reflects the new section order.
- Existing grouping/selection tests are updated and new tests cover: the high@idea vs medium@plan_complete inversion (both copies), the `In Review` pin, per-band file-path grouping, and the selection-truncation case.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Producers see the most urgent work at the top of the sprint view regardless of what stage each item is in, instead of medium-priority in-progress-stage work pushing high-priority ideas out of sight.

## Constraints

- `packages/shared/src/database/sort.ts` (`computeScore`) is **not** changed — only its consumers (grouping and selection).
- Blocker pinning (WL-0MW7YJYS5009H7WC) must keep working: a pinned blocker still shares the blocked item's group and sorts immediately after it.
- Expand/`childCount` reachability, root substitution and the mandatory always-show set are untouched.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Copy drift** — `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` and `src/commands/grouping.ts` are hand-synchronised; a partial change leaves `wl next --groups` disagreeing with the sprint view. Mitigation: change both in one commit and assert the same contract in both suites.
- **Blocker-pinning regression** — the pinned-blocker group override interacts with band partitioning; a pinned blocker must stay in its blocked item's group *and* inherit that item's band. Mitigation: keep the existing pinning tests green and add a cross-band case.
- **Test churn** — roughly 2,300 lines of existing grouping/selection tests encode the old stage-first order and must be rewritten rather than extended; a careless rewrite can bake in the new bug. Mitigation: derive expectations from this brief's contract, not from current output.
- **Scope creep** — consolidating the two grouping copies into one shared module, or changing `computeScore`, is out of scope here; file as separate work items.
- **Assumption** — `others` arrive from `wl next` already score-ordered, so the change is a stable priority-first re-sort with score as tie-break, not a full re-score.

## **Key Files:**

- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` — `assignItemGroups` band-first bucketing; `compareGroupableItems` intra-band tie-break.
- `src/commands/grouping.ts` — the core `wl next --groups` duplicate; must match herdr exactly.
- `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts` — `selectWorkItems` priority-first ordering of the `others` slice before truncation.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.root-substitution.ts` — selection tail; verify pin/substitution interaction.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — sprint-view render path (verification only).

## Related work

- `Bubble up critical items (WL-0MR1COW20005IO1C)` — the completed precedent that added the `Critical Group N` band; this item generalises the mechanism to all bands.
- WL-0MVVLBTTP003Y4XO — made priority the primary *within-group* sort key.
- WL-0MW7YJYS5009H7WC — blocker pinning (group override that must be preserved).
- WL-0MV6JGVPH009YDXB / WL-0MV6KV22S004NYIU / WL-0MV71WBHB007D8ZE — the mandatory always-show guarantees.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

1. **Canonical bucket order?** Priority band first (`critical` → `high` → `medium` → `low`), stage as the intra-band tie-breaker. — agreed.
2. **Does `In Review` move into its priority band?** No — it stays pinned last.
3. **Is file-path conflict grouping preserved?** Yes, within each priority band.
4. **Should selection also be priority-first before truncation?** Yes.
5. **Do labels and the core `wl next --groups` output change too?** Yes — expect `High Group N` / `Medium Group N` / `Low Group N`, with the shared copy updated in lockstep.

data.description:
## Goal

Encode the new priority-band ordering contract as executable tests **before** any production code changes, so the two implementation items work against a red specification rather than a guess.

## Scope

Tests only — **no production source is edited in this item**. `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts`, `src/commands/grouping.ts` and `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts` must be untouched (the diff for this item is test files only).

Tests are added to:

- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.test.ts` — herdr `assignItemGroups` / `compareGroupableItems`
- `tests/grouping-utility.test.ts` — the core mirror used by `wl next --groups`
- `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.test.ts` — selection truncation

## Contract under test

- **Band order:** `critical` → `high` → `medium` → `low` → `In Review` (single global section, pinned last).
- **Intra-band stage sub-order:** `status='in-progress'` → `plan_complete` → `intake_complete` → `idea` → other. Stage never reorders across bands.
- **The inversion case:** a `high@idea` item's group number is lower than every `medium@plan_complete` item's group number (today the stage bucket wins and the medium renders above the high).
- **Per-band file-path grouping:** greedy first-fit inside each band, at most 3 file-path groups per band-section, two same-band items sharing a Key File never share a group, items with no Key Files stay singleton groups.
- **`In Review` pin:** rendered as the final section regardless of the priority of its members.
- **Selection truncation:** with 5 high and 2 medium non-mandatory items and `othersLimit = 3`, all three selected `others` are high — no medium displaces a high.
- **Mandatory guarantee unchanged:** every `critical`, `status='in-progress'`, `status='blocked'` and `in_review`+`completed` item is selected regardless of the window.
- **Purity:** the same item set in any arrival order / `updatedAt` order groups identically.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each contract bullet above has at least one named test in the files listed under Scope, with an assertion message that identifies the specific inversion or ordering rule being violated.
- The new tests fail against current `main` sources for the expected reason (red for the inversion/selection cases, not for compile or fixture errors) when run through the test skill (`/skill:test`).
- Tests that encode ordering unchanged by this work (in_review bucket sort, expand reachability, mandatory always-show) remain green and are left semantically untouched.
- At least one test exercises the **core** copy (`src/commands/grouping.ts`) for the band order, not only the herdr copy, so the mirror is specified too.
- The selection test asserts both the selected set **and** that the incoming score order is preserved within a priority band (the score tie-break must come from `wl next` order, not a re-sort).
- No ad-hoc test command is used; the red/green evidence comes from the test skill.

- New tests cover the high@idea vs medium@plan_complete inversion (both copies), the `In Review` pin, per-band file-path grouping, and the selection-truncation case; existing grouping/selection tests are updated rather than deleted.

**Key Files:**

- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.test.ts`
- `tests/grouping-utility.test.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.test.ts`

## Notes

Test-first ordering: this item must land before the two grouping implementation items and before the selection item. Fixtures should be shared helpers inside each test file (no new production helper) to keep the diff test-only.

data.description:
## Goal

Rewrite `assignItemGroups` in the herdr plugin so sections are bucketed by **priority band first**, with stage used only as the intra-band sub-order — a `high@idea` item can then never render below a `medium@plan_complete` item.

## Implementation

1. Replace the stage-derived bucket assembly (`Critical Group N` → `Group N` → `Idea` → `Other` → `In Review`) with a band loop over `['critical', 'high', 'medium', 'low']`.
2. Inside each band:
   - `critical` keeps today's file-path partitioning (`Critical Group N`, per-category label counter).
   - Non-critical bands partition the band's actively-worked / `plan_complete` / `intake_complete` items by file-path conflicts (`<Band> Group N`), then emit a single `<Band> Idea` group and a single `<Band> Other` group for the band.
   - `maxFilePathGroups` (default 3) applies **per band-section**; the label counter restarts at 1 per band.
3. Extend `WITHIN_GROUP_STAGE_ORDER` with `idea: 3` and raise `REMAINING_STAGE_ORDER` to 4, so `compareGroupableItems` and `compareGroupingContentKey` express `in-progress → plan_complete → intake_complete → idea → other`.
4. Keep `compareGroupableItems` (priority-first), `canonicalizeForGrouping`, `groupItemsByFilePaths`, `buildLabelCounter`, `remapToSequential` and the `in_review` bucket sort semantically unchanged — only bucket assembly and the stage-order table change.
5. Emit `In Review` last as one global section, never inside a band.
6. Update the module header group-order documentation and keep the "mirrors `src/commands/grouping.ts`" note accurate.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `high@idea` sits in a lower-numbered group than every `medium@plan_complete` item for a mixed fixture; the inversion test from the contract-tests item passes.
- Section order is `critical` → `high` → `medium` → `low` → `In Review` independent of stage; a low-priority `plan_complete` item never outranks a high-priority `idea` item.
- Intra-band stage sub-order is `in-progress` → `plan_complete` → `intake_complete` → `idea` → other, and stage never reorders across bands.
- `In Review` is a single final section regardless of the priority of its members.
- Labels are `Critical Group N`, `High Group N`, `Medium Group N`, `Low Group N`, `<Band> Idea`, `<Band> Other`, `In Review`; label counters restart per band.
- Per-band file-path grouping holds: two same-band items sharing a Key File never share a group, at most 3 file-path groups per band-section, no-Key-Files items are singleton groups.
- Grouping stays a pure function of item content — no dependence on `updatedAt`, arrival order or pin-map insertion order (permutation test).
- The herdr grouping test suite is green through the test skill; no other production module is modified.

- A mixed set of `high@idea` and `medium@plan_complete` items is regrouped so every high item's group number is lower than every medium item's — the inversion is gone.
- Section labels follow the band scheme: `Critical Group N`, `High Group N`, `Medium Group N`, `Low Group N`; no non-critical section is labelled plain `Group N`.

**Key Files:**

- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.test.ts`

## Notes

`packages/shared/src/database/sort.ts` (`computeScore`) is explicitly out of scope. The core `wl next --groups` copy is a separate item; this item changes herdr only, and the module header must still state the two copies are kept in sync.

## Goal

Order the non-mandatory `others` slice priority-first **before** the `othersLimit` truncation so a medium-priority item can never displace a high-priority one from the sprint window.

## Implementation

1. In `selectWorkItems` (`packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts`), sort the `others` slice with a **stable** comparator on priority band (`high` → `medium` → `low`; unknown → `medium`) immediately before `.slice(0, othersLimit)`.
2. The incoming `wl next` score order is the intra-band tie-break: a stable priority sort preserves it. Do **not** re-score — `packages/shared/src/database/sort.ts` (`computeScore`) is untouched by this item and by the parent.
3. Keep mandatory-set assembly unchanged (criticals, `in_review`+`completed`, `status='blocked'`, `status='in-progress'`), including the root-only filter and the `done` exclusion.
4. Document the ordering and the stable-sort/sub-score relationship in the module header.

## Acceptance Criteria

- With 5 high and 2 medium non-mandatory items and `othersLimit = 3`, all three selected `others` are high-priority — no medium displaces a high.
- With `othersLimit` larger than the high count, the remaining slots are filled with mediums in their incoming score order (stable sort, rank order preserved within a band).
- The mandatory always-show guarantee is unchanged: every `critical`, `status='in-progress'`, `status='blocked'` and `in_review`+`completed` item is still selected regardless of the window, and mandatory items never consume a slice they previously did not.
- `selectWorkItems` remains pure and deterministic: no input mutation, same input → same output.
- Existing smart-selection tests are updated to the new contract and all pass through the test skill.
- A test asserts the reproduced anomaly is gone: a fresh audit-not-ready medium (score 5500) no longer out-selects a plain high (score 3000).

**Key Files:**

- `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.test.ts`

## Notes

Whether `others` already arrive score-ordered from `wl next` is asserted by a test (incoming order within a band must be preserved) rather than assumed; if the fetcher does not guarantee score order, document that in the module header and keep the stable sort as the guarantee boundary.

## Goal

data.author: plan
data.comment:
Planning Complete. Decomposed `src/commands/doctor.ts` (1,732 lines) into 14 serial child tasks behind a thin registrar.

## Plan summary

The epic is now a 14-child serial chain, each a `task` at `stage: intake_complete`,
wired so every intermediate state builds and passes the suite:

`notices` → `cache` → `audit-gaps` → `prefix` → `dangling-parents` → `priority`
→ `prune` → `file-paths` → `migrate` → `foreign-items` → `stage-sync` → `upgrade`
→ `root validation/--fix` → `guard test + docs`.

After the split, the largest module is `validate.ts` (~408 lines) and the
registrar is ~60-120 lines — both well under the 1,000-line ceiling.

## Effort & risk

- Effort: **Medium** — PERT O=22h / M=35h / P=55h; expected 36.17h; recommended
  (with overheads) **54.17h**; range 40-73h.
- Risk: **Medium** (score 9/25). Top drivers: root validation/`--fix`
  extraction, `foreign-items`, `upgrade`.

## Six review stages

- **Requirements & AC alignment review:** each extraction child's ACs trace to
  parent ACs 1-5; the guard/docs child carries parent ACs 1, 6, 7, 8. Added
  explicit AC6 (module-level doc comment) and AC7 (no cycle / narrow context) to
  every extraction child, plus verbatim parent-AC traceability lines where the
  similarity gate required them. No invented requirements.
- **Completeness review:** all 14 children have a description and an AC section;
  no `**Key Files:**` section exists on any child (none required — the parent
  carries the file map).
- **Sequencing & dependencies review:** dependencies form a single acyclic serial
  chain. The guard test intentionally lands last (it asserts the post-split
  ceiling and would be red mid-refactor); the 18 existing doctor suites are the
  test-first regression gate that runs at every step.
- **Scope sizing review:** one module per child; 39-408 lines each, all
  deliverable increments that leave the tree green.
- **Acceptance & testability review:** every AC is objectively checkable via
  `wc -l`, `grep`, named test files, or the full suite; no vague criteria.
- **Polish & handoff review:** descriptions are copy-pasteable; each names its
  source line range, target module, and the tests that must stay green.

AC coverage review: **proceed** — 100% of parent ACs covered.

## Appendix: questions and decisions

No producer questions were raised; every open point was resolved by repository
inspection, consistent with parent Assumption A3.

- **Decision D1 — `prefix` subcommand is in scope.** The file grew from 1,658 to
  1,732 lines since intake and gained a `wl doctor prefix` subcommand (lines
  848-890, ~43 lines) added by WL-0MVM8V79C003XH2J. It is extracted as its own
  child (WL-0MW0845IS003VCTK). Evidence: `.command('prefix')` at line 848;
  `tests/cli/doctor-prefix.test.ts` exists.
- **Decision D2 — notices module lands first, not alongside the registrar.** Both
  `doctor cache` (`DAY_MS`, `formatCacheBytes`) and the root `doctor` action (all
  pending-upgrade/pending-cache helpers) depend on the shared helpers. Extracting
  notices first satisfies parent AC5 (no extracted module imports from
  `src/commands/doctor.ts`); the original order would have forced `cache.ts` to
  import from the monolith. Evidence: helper usage scan across the 12 command
  bodies (only `cache` and root use them).
- **Decision D3 — guard test remains last.** The additive ≤1,000-line guard
  asserts a post-split invariant and would fail if landed before the split,
  violating the "serial, tree-green landing" constraint. The pre-existing suites
  are the test-first gate. Recorded as an explicit, reasoned exception to the
  generic test-first ordering rule.
- **Open question O1 (non-blocking, for implementers):** no test was found that
  pins the order subcommands appear in `wl doctor --help`; the plan mitigates
  this by preserving registrar call order and relying on the existing CLI suites,
  but reviewers should diff `--help` output manually.
- **Housekeeping:** an erroneous duplicate child WL-0MW05O2FG002LWFG (corrupted
  77,647-char description from an unescaped shell substitution) was closed; the
  valid audit-gaps child is WL-0MW08084M000ZQW7.

Decomposed `src/github-sync.ts` (1,339 lines, 6 type + 4 value exports) into an
8-child serial, test-first plan. Layout mirrors the shipped `src/sync/` and
`src/github/` splits: `src/github-sync.ts` becomes a thin barrel over
`src/github-sync/{types,util,progress,labels,comments,push,import,import-hierarchy,import-close-check,import-comments}.ts`.

### Children (dependency order)

| # | ID | Title |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | WL-0MW0JF51F009HNWN | Add github-sync split guard (test-first) |
| 2 | WL-0MW0JF5YE008LV1R | Extract github-sync types |
| 3 | WL-0MW0JF6TH00749I2 | Extract github-sync shared helpers and progress |
| 4 | WL-0MW0JF7QN007E1JU | Extract github-sync label resolution |
| 5 | WL-0MW0JF8R6006HUA6 | Extract github-sync comment sync |
| 6 | WL-0MW0JF9QG008E791 | Extract github-sync push flow |
| 7 | WL-0MW0JFANE006VCGO | Extract github-sync import flow |
| 8 | WL-0MW0JFBIK007E6VZ | Barrel, docs and guard close-out |

Each child depends on the previous one (`wl dep add` chain), so implementation
is one session per child in order.

### Six automated review stages

1. Finished Requirements & AC alignment review: all five parent ACs trace to at
   least one child AC; AC2 (public surface) and AC4 (cycles/docs) were restated
   verbatim in child 1 and child 8 after the coverage gate flagged a weak
   textual match; the stale "draft — refine during intake" AC label was removed.

   Criteria, Minimal implementation, Key Files, Dependencies, Constraints and
   Deliverables; all Key Files paths are syntactically valid.
3. Finished Sequencing & dependencies review: guard (test/verification) lands
   before any production move; types → helpers → labels → comments → push →
   import → close-out is a coherent serial chain with real prerequisites as
   ancestors.
4. Finished Scope sizing review: each child is a deliverable increment that ends
   with the unchanged suite green; the largest surfaces (push ~400 lines;
   import ~615 lines across four modules) stay well under the 1,000-line ceiling.
5. Finished Acceptance & testability review: every AC is pass/fail-checkable via
   guard gates, named test files, module line counts or recorded `wc -l` output;
   the approximate barrel target was tightened to ≤ 150 lines.
6. Finished Polish & handoff review: descriptions are copy-pasteable, move-only
   constraints and the "no barrel imports" rule are explicit, and each child
   requires the commit hash to be recorded.

`apply_coverage_review` initially reported two weak textual matches and then
auto-closed four generic "Close coverage gap" children. Those children

duplicates (WL-0MW0JGHHX0032S72, WL-0MW0JGIEZ004QVY1, WL-0MW0JGJ8C0051WIY,

pre-check first returned `skip` because effort/risk were unset; with the

## Decomposition landed (move-only)

`packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts` was **1,512 lines** at `dev` @ 810d6ec9 (the description's 1,067 and the plan's 1,438 were both stale). It is now a **thin barrel** (137 lines) over six single-responsibility siblings:

| `downtime-log-budget.ts` | 77 | Host-budget refusal vocabulary + evidence shape (pure leaf) |
| `downtime-log-coordination.ts` | 313 | Coordination/decision entries, append, readers, per-hour reason tally |
| `downtime-log-entries.ts` | 234 | Dispatch-log entry shapes, pane-close lifecycle entries, appends, reader, marker predicate |
| `downtime-log-markers.ts` | 414 | Dispatched-marker readers, staleness/stage guards, attempt budget, pane-close cooldown |
| `downtime-log-recent.ts` | 294 | Recent-dispatches projection + 4-hour UTC time blocks |

### AC evidence

- **AC1 (no file > 1,000 lines):** largest family module is 414 lines. Enforced by `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.split-guard.test.ts`.
- **AC2 (public exports unchanged):** barrel exports **54** names; the pre-split module exported the same 54 — verified set-equal (no additions, no removals) by scripted comparison and pinned by the committed baseline `downtime-log.split-baseline.json`.

I stopped **before writing any code** because AC1 and AC2 are arithmetically incompatible, and AC6 inherits the conflict. The exact shipped threshold values materially change what alarms on every host, so this is a producer decision rather than an implementer guess.

### Evidence (reproducing `classify_metric` from `scripts/metrics.py`)

- AC1 fixes `process_count`: warn `cores * 32`, crit `cores * 48`, and gives `thread_count` "the same shape".
- On the **16-core** host named in the brief: warn = `16 * 32 = 512`, crit = `16 * 48 = 768`.
- AC2 requires a simulated **16-core** profile with **560 processes / 2250 threads** to classify **low**.
- Applying AC1's own thresholds: `560 >= 512` → **warning**; `2250 >= 768` → **critical**. AC2 therefore cannot pass while AC1 holds.
- AC6 ("the report headline for the multi-agent host profile carries no spurious critical rows") also fails: `thread_count = 2250` is **critical** under AC1's thread block.
- This is not a rounding slip: 560 processes is ~9 % above the 512 warning bound, and 2250 threads is ~2.9× the 768 critical bound. Even the producer's own 527-process observation is **above** 512 (→ warning, not low).

### Options (please pick one)

- **Option A (recommended) — recalibrate from measured data.** Keep AC1's design (dedicated, independently-overridable, core-derived blocks) but set:
  - `process_count`: warn `cores * 48`, crit `cores * 96` (16-core host: **768 / 1536**)
  - `thread_count`: warn `cores * 160`, crit `cores * 320` (16-core host: **2560 / 5120**)

  This makes the brief's profile (560 / 2250) and this host's measured values (521 processes / 1674 threads) **low**, while a genuine explosion (>1536 processes or >5120 threads on 16 cores) stays **critical**. AC1's AC text would need the example multipliers updated; AC2, AC5 and AC6 then pass.
- **Option B — keep AC1's literal 32/48 for both blocks.** Then AC2's "low" must become "not critical" and AC6 must drop its "no spurious critical rows" claim, because `thread_count` stays **critical** on the target host. This keeps the P0 thread alarm the item exists to remove — not recommended.
- **Option C — keep AC1's 32/48 for `process_count` only and calibrate `thread_count` separately** (the Appendix OPEN QUESTION). With 16 cores, 560 processes still classify **warning** (not low), and `thread_count` still needs its own high pair; AC2's "both low" still needs rewording for processes.

**Recommendation: Option A.** It is the only option that satisfies the brief's observable goal (profile is green) without disabling genuine alarms, and it stays fully overridable in `config.yaml` (AC3), so a producer can retune per host without a code change.

### Current state

No code was written; no worktree change was kept. The item is released (`status: open`) with `needsProducerReview: true`. Everything except the numeric multipliers is unambiguous — AC4 (stale-lock validation), AC5 (swap/memory cross-check), AC7 (suite) and AC8 (docs) can be implemented as soon as a ruling is recorded.
