# Plan draft — WL-0MVR8GDJ3008WY3Y (Downtime leader cannot see a worklog root with no running herdr instance)

Seed context: feature | stage intake_complete | effort Medium | risk High | assignee Map (producer hold).
Decisions already producer-confirmed at intake: **D1 = O1 registered roots** (`downtimeWorklogRoots` config + round-robin sweep via `getHerdrListHead` under the existing sequential gates, reusing the retired `downtime-round-robin-by-root` cursor); **D2 = liveness-aware `hasPeerOffer`** (entries older than `DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_MARKER_STALE_WINDOW_MS` count as absent peers; `pruneStaleEntries` stays a no-op).

## Decomposition — 7 features (3 test-first verification + 4 implementation)

| # | Title | Type | Parent ACs |
|---|-------|------|-----------|
| T1 | Test: downtimeWorklogRoots settings validation | test | AC6, AC11 |
| T2 | Test: hasPeerOffer liveness | test | AC7, AC9, AC11 |
| T3 | Test: registered-root sweep — fairness, fail-open, gates | test | AC1–AC5, AC9 |
| I1 | Implement: downtimeWorklogRoots setting + validation | feature | AC6 |
| I2 | Implement: hasPeerOffer liveness-aware predicate | feature | AC7 |
| I3 | Implement: registered-root sweep in the leader | feature | AC1–AC5, AC3 (ranking) |
| I4 | Implement: docs — root-discovery model + README | docs | AC8, AC10 |

Dependencies (test-first; implementation depends on its test contract):
- I1 ← T1; I2 ← T2; I3 ← T3 and I1; I4 ← I2 and I3.

Vertical-slice phasing: each pair (test + implementation) cuts the relevant layer end-to-end (config surface / coordination predicate / leader dispatch loop with root seam + cursor reuse + dispatch claims), and each features tests + code comments; docs slice I4 lands last so it records the final model.

## Key design notes (grounded in code)

- `computeMostImportantItem(deps, cwd, ...)` is already cwd-parameterised — a registered-root head is the same call with `cwd = registeredRoot`.
- The leader's dispatch-time gates are already root-parameterised (`cooldownEntriesForRoot`, `inFlightForRoot`, `reviewGateForRoot`; `dispatchClaimedTier{cwd: root}`) — the sweep reuses them, satisfying "no gate bypass" (AC2) without new gate logic.
- `selectLeastRecentlyServed` (retired-but-functional cursor in `downtime-round-robin-by-root.ts`) is reused for root-level round-robin (AC4).
- `getHerdrListHead(cwd, limit)` currently IGNORES its `cwd` argument (index.ts:527 calls `fetchNextItems` without a root override) — the sweep slice must make the seam root-aware (resolve `--worklog-dir` per registered root, as `getNextItem` already does via `buildWlArgs`).
- `hasPeerOffer(entries, instanceId)` has exactly two callers (orchestrator-dispatch.ts:908, orchestrator-tick.ts:267); the liveness change is additive optional `nowMs`/`staleMs` params defaulting to `DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_MARKER_STALE_WINDOW_MS` (24 h).
- Settings: new `downtimeWorklogRoots: string[]` on `PluginSettings` follows the existing clamp/validation pattern in `downtime-worker.clamps.ts` and `loadSettings`/`saveSettings`; empty/absent must leave today's behaviour byte-for-byte (AC6).

## Assumptions (recorded, non-blocking — grounded in codebase convention)

- **A1 (config shape):** `downtimeWorklogRoots` entries are **worklog ROOTS** (parents of `.worklog/`), matching the coordinator's `worklogRoot` field semantics used across `coordination.ts`, `computeMostImportantItem` and `CoordinationEntry`. The brief's phrase "paths to `.worklog` directories" is treated as loose wording; the sweep validates `<root>/.worklog/worklog.db` presence at load time and normalises symlinks via realpath. (Effort/risk unknown #1.)
- **A2 (verification):** AC1's ContextHub live check is performed at I3 completion (read-only sweep observation); unit-level reachability is proven in tmp-root fixtures under `HERDR_COORDINATION_DIR` isolation, the established cross-root test pattern, so running instances are never disturbed. (Effort/risk unknown #2.)
- **A3:** Sweep runs only when the leader has idle capacity and no offer dispatched — same placement as the own-backlog fallback; it is an additional candidate source, never a second ranking.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q: (none asked — the plan run found no blocking questions.) Decisions D1 (O1) and D2 (liveness-aware hasPeerOffer) were producer-confirmed at intake (comments WL-C0MW4WJ7DW006UVJ3, WL-C0MW4WJ9G9009WZKU, 2026-11-06); effort/risk (Medium / High) recorded at intake. OPEN QUESTION (for implementer): whether AC1's ContextHub verification should also add a temporary registry entry for ContextHub itself — resolved conservatively as "read-only observation only; no persistent config mutation" (A2).

data.comment:
## Implementation notes — grouping stability (WL-0MVVLBTTP003Y4XO)

### What changed

**1. Content-deterministic packing (AC1, AC2).** `groupItemsByFilePaths` now
canonicalises its input before the greedy first-fit loop in **both** mirrors
(`src/commands/grouping.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts`). The new exported
`compareGroupingContentKey(a, b)` orders by `priority` (high → medium → low) →
stage sub-order → `id`, and **nothing else**: `updatedAt` and the audit fields
are deliberately excluded. Greedy first-fit itself is unchanged, `maxGroups`
(default 3) is unchanged, and restricted singleton groups behave exactly as
before — only the packing order is now a pure function of the item set.

**2. Priority-first within-group ordering (AC3).** `compareGroupableItems` now
sorts **priority first**, then the stage sub-order, then `id`. The `in_review`
6-bucket comparator was already priority-first and is untouched. Applied in
both mirrors.

**3. Tests (AC2, AC3, AC4).** Both grouping suites gained a stability block that
perturbs only non-material inputs and asserts nothing changes:
- every permutation of a set whose packing genuinely depends on order
  (`A→x`, `B→x+y`, `C→y`) yields the same `group`/`groupLabel`;
- varying `updatedAt`/`auditedAt`/`auditResult` never moves an item;
- `regroupWorkItems` (the herdr merged-list entry point) renders the same ids,
  group numbers and labels for every input order + timestamp permutation;
- a material change (key files, priority) *does* move the item, so the
  assertions cannot pass vacuously;
- `compareGroupingContentKey` returns 0 for two items differing only in
  `updatedAt`.
Both mirrors assert the same contract (mirror stays a self-contained pure
duplication — no core import from the plugin, per WL-0MS8W5LTW006YZ4B Q2c).

### Intentional, observable behaviour changes (deliberate, not incidental)

- Within a group, a **high-priority** `intake_complete`/remaining item now
  outranks a **medium-priority** `plan_complete` item. Previously the stage
  sub-order was primary.
- In the herdr mirror the **actively-worked** sub-order (`status='in-progress'`)
  is now *secondary*: an actively-worked **low**-priority item no longer
  outranks a **high**-priority `plan_complete` item. It still sorts first within
  its own priority band (WL-0MUY1CSQG007TCYX behaviour preserved where it does
  not conflict with AC3).
Existing order assertions in `tests/grouping-utility.test.ts` and
`packages/herdr/src/grouping.test.ts` were updated explicitly for both points,
with the new contract stated in the test names and comments. Canonical group
section order (Critical Group N → Group N → Idea → Other → In Review) and the
`selectWorkItems` always-show-mandatory guarantee are unchanged (no filtering).

### Docs (AC6)

`CLI.md` (parallel-safe grouping + new *Stability* paragraph), 
`docs/FILE_PATH_CONVENTION.md` (group order + a material/non-material table),
`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (content-deterministic grouping + priority-first), 
`packages/herdr/README.md` (new *Grouping stability* subsection, corrected the
"actively-worked items first" wording), plus code comments in both mirrors.
`CHANGELOG.md` deliberately untouched (ship skill owns it).

### Test evidence

- Root suite (`npm --silent test -- tests`, the dev-push gate command):
  **PASS** — 344 files / 4818 tests.
- Herdr group (`npm --silent test -- packages/herdr/src`): **PASS** —
  151 files / 4707 tests.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; `npm run build` clean.

### Pre-existing failure found (not caused by this item)

With the test skill's default disk-backed `TMPDIR` (`/var/tmp/pi-test-<uid>`),
two **pre-existing** tests in `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` fail because
the Pi session-dir encoding (every `/` → `-`) cannot round-trip a hyphenated
path: `worklogRootFromPiSessionPath …` and `defaultStalledPaneRootResolver …`.
Reproduced on `dev` @ 4d105bf8 with no local changes (main checkout and
worktree alike); green with a hyphen-free `PI_TEST_TMPDIR`. Because
`packages/herdr/**` is a declared changed-scope group, those two failures would
otherwise make this item's changed-scope gate red, so the runs above were
executed with `PI_TEST_TMPDIR=/tmp/pitestwork`. Filed as
**WL-0MW5C6XS00071DWN** (`discovered-from` this item) — the durable fix belongs
there, not here (scope-creep guard).

### Assumptions

- "Material" = the `**Key Files:**` section, `priority`, `stage`/`status`, or the
  item set. Description prose outside Key Files and all audit fields stay
  non-material (consistent with `extractFilePaths`).
- Canonical pre-pack order and within-group display order share the same
  priority → stage → id key, so the first item packed is also the first item
  displayed within its group.

data.comment:
## Implementation summary — github split guard + frozen baseline

Delivered the deterministic, read-only structural gate **before** any production
code moves. No `src/` file was modified.

### Artefacts

- `tests/github/github-split-guard-scan.ts` — scanners and pure gate predicates
  for the github family (`src/github.ts` barrel + `src/github/**`), plus the
  `--write-baseline` CLI.
- `tests/github/github-split-guard.test.ts` — the guard suite (38 tests): live
  gates, committed-baseline tests, and negative "fails on broken input" proofs.
- `tests/github/github.split-baseline.json` — frozen 58-symbol surface
  (52 value + 6 type), generated from the live barrel at plan time.

### Reuse decision (plan step 2, preferred — not the local fallback)

Added small **additive, backward-compatible optional parameters** to the shared
sync scanner `tests/sync/split-guard-scan.ts` instead of copying its 942-line
scanner:

- `splitFamilyModules(index, isFamily = isSyncFamilyFile)`
- `GraphOptions.family` / `.barrel` / `.allowlist` on `buildImportGraph`
- `findStaticCycles` / `findUnexplainedStaticCycles` / `findRuntimeCycles` gain
  `options: GraphOptions`
- `findBarrelImports(index, runtimeOnly, isFamily, barrel)`
- `dynamicImportNames` derives its cheap pre-filter token from the `barrel`
  argument (`sync` → `github`), so a differently-named barrel is never skipped.

Defaults preserve the sync guard byte-for-byte; `tests/sync/split-guard.test.ts`
is **unmodified** and stays green (verified by a full-suite run).

### Documented assumption (resolves two ACs that pull in opposite directions)

The item requires (a) the JSDoc-header gate to fail on **any** github-family
production module without a header, and (b) **no production file under `src/`**
to be modified by this item. At plan time `src/github.ts` has no header, so the
two cannot both hold literally.

Resolution: the JSDoc gate covers **every module under `src/github/` always**,
and the in-flight monolith `src/github.ts` is exempt **only while it remains the
oversized allowlisted barrel** (mirroring the shrink-only size allowlist). Once
child 7 reduces the barrel to a façade and removes its allowlist entry,
`findStaleAllowlistEntries` forces the entry away and the JSDoc gate covers the
barrel — so the façade must then carry a header. This keeps `src/` untouched
while guaranteeing the final state enforces headers everywhere.

### Gates and parent-AC mapping (also in the suite header JSDoc)

- AC1 (no file > 1,000 lines) — size gate + shrink-only `['github.ts']`
  allowlist (ceiling `['github.ts']`); a stale entry also fails.
- AC2 (public exports importable) — frozen 58-symbol baseline (52 value + 6
  type), value-resolution and type-declaration gates, consumer scan.
- AC3 (existing tests unmodified) — no test import/assertion changed; full
  suite green.
- AC4 (no cycles; responsibilities documented) — barrel-import ban, static +
  runtime cycle gates, JSDoc-header gate.
- AC5 (docs) — the guard documents the contract it enforces in its own header.

### Verification

- Build: `npm run build` — success.
- Full suite: **310 files passed, 1 skipped; 4445 tests passed, 5 skipped**.

Error JSON follows the CLI convention (stdout when present, otherwise stderr).
- `wl project add <PREFIX> --git-url <url> [--path <path>]` -> success JSON `{ success: true, prefix, path, gitUrl, cloned }`; clones into the projects root by default; records `projects: { <PREFIX>: { path, gitUrl } }` in the consumer `.worklog/config.yaml`; validates the cloned `config.yaml` prefix.
- Idempotent second run: exit 0, `cloned: false`, untracked marker inside the clone survives, mapping unchanged.
- Prefix mismatch -> non-zero, `error_code: "prefix_mismatch"`, message names both prefixes, no mapping.
- Clone failure -> non-zero, `error_code: "clone_failed"`, no mapping.
- No `--git-url` (stdin closed) -> deterministic non-zero, `error_code: "missing_git_url"` naming `--git-url`; never prompts without `--interactive`.

Note: the spec spawns the CLI with the real git binary on PATH because the suite's mock `git clone` only copies a local directory and cannot clone a `file://` URL. No production code changed (spec-only child); docs are F9.

data.author: implement
data.comment:
Implementation notes and verification (commit eb044ae0).

Delivered:
- `wl project add <PREFIX> --git-url <url> [--path <dir>] [--projects-root <path>] [--interactive]` — clones only when the target is absent, validates the checkout's declared prefix, records `projects.<PREFIX>.{path,gitUrl}` in the consumer `.worklog/config.yaml` (all other keys preserved) and is idempotent (`cloned: false`, clone untouched, mapping unchanged). Failures: `invalid_prefix`, `missing_git_url`, `invalid_project`, `prefix_mismatch`, `clone_failed`, `config_error` — none leave a mapping behind. No stdin read unless `--interactive` is passed.
- `unknown_project` payload (`prefix`, `projects_root`, `remediation`) from `wl dep add` and `wl dep list` for a foreign prefix no discovered project declares; same-project missing ids keep the plain not-found payload.
- `wl next --json` attaches the same `error_code`/`prefix`/`projects_root`/`remediation` to a `foreign_dependencies` entry whose prefix is undiscoverable (still a non-blocking coordination note).
- `CLI.md` (project add + dep unknown-project remediation) and `CONFIG.md` (`projects` map now written by `project add`).
- F7's 6 RED pins flipped to `it(`; added pins for `dep list`, `--path`, `--interactive`, and the `wl next` remediation view.

Verification:
- Changed-scope gate (implement.py finish): green — tests/config, cross-repo-gating, cross-repo-project-add (13 + 13 + 23).
- Full suite via the test skill (`run_tests.py --scope full`): green, 0 failures (207 s), cached for HEAD (audit evidence available).

Assumptions (documented):
1. Default clone target is `<projectsRoot>/<prefix-lowercased>`; `--path` overrides it (relative paths resolve against cwd).
2. A prefix mismatch on a freshly made clone removes that clone so discovery is not polluted under the wrong prefix; no mapping is written.
3. The recorded mapping is durable, but discovery still requires a genuine store (`initialized` or `worklog.db`); a freshly cloned repo becomes discoverable once its store exists (e.g. after `wl sync` inside the clone). Documented in CLI.md.
4. Config write-through re-serialises `.worklog/config.yaml` with js-yaml, so YAML comments are not preserved (values are).
5. The `wl next` remediation enrichment lives in the CLI output layer: `@worklog/shared` is a data layer that must not run filesystem discovery, and the remediation wording is CLI-owned.

data.author: implement
data.comment:
Implementation summary (AC5 isolation).

**New module:** `tests/cross-repo-isolation.test.ts` (2 tests, both green via the test skill's changed scope).

1. **No foreign mutation lock.** Runs the real CLI (`dep add`, `dep list`, `next --include-blocked`) with `WL_DEBUG=1`, parses every `[wl:lock] Lock acquired at …` line and asserts (a) the local store's lock IS acquired (non-vacuous instrumentation), (b) no lock path inside the sibling `.worklog/` is ever touched, (c) the sibling `.worklog/` holds no `*.lock` file, and (d) the sibling DB hash, file mtime, directory mtime and entry set are byte-identical (no `-wal`/`-shm`). The foreign read remains a snapshot copy, so `src/mutation-lock.ts` is never engaged for a foreign path.
2. **No foreign item in the local edge cache.** Records one foreign edge and one local edge, builds the `wl next` `EdgeCache` from the persisted local store, and asserts the foreign id is absent from `itemsById` while the local edge target is present (non-vacuity control); `outbound`/`inbound` still carry the foreign edge; and passing that exact cache to `hasActiveBlockers` / `getForeignDependencyViews` still gates on the foreign target (resolved from its own store, never from the cache). The foreign row is also absent from the local `workitems` table.

**Constraints honoured:** `tests/sync-prefix-filter.test.ts`, `tests/sync-regression-guard.test.ts` and `tests/sync-worktree.test.ts` are unchanged; `src/mutation-lock.ts` and `src/cross-repo/foreign-store.ts` are unchanged (test-only diff).

**Doctor evidence (repo store):** `wl doctor --json` reports 48 pre-existing findings (33 incompatible-status-stage, 11 missing-parent, 3 invalid-stage, 1 invalid-priority) — none cross-repo/dependency related and unaffected by a test-only change.

**Assumption:** the isolation proof relies on the existing snapshot-copy read path in `src/cross-repo/foreign-store.ts`; a future switch to a direct read-only open of the sibling would reintroduce `-wal`/`-shm` sidecars and be caught by these assertions.

## Implementation complete — schema + config startup fast paths

### What landed

1. **Schema/migration fast path** (`packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts`)
   - `SqlitePersistentStore` now takes one cheap bootstrap-state query on open: it reads `metadata.schemaVersion`, the new `metadata.requiredColumnsVersion` marker and `worklog_fts` presence in a single statement. When `schemaVersion` **and** the repair marker both equal the code's `SCHEMA_VERSION`, `initializeSchema()` (all `CREATE TABLE`/index DDL + the additive required-column repair) is skipped entirely, and FTS availability comes from the same query instead of a write probe.
   - `initializeSchema()` writes `requiredColumnsVersion` at the end of every successful bootstrap, so a store created before the marker existed pays one slow (repairing) open and is fast after.
   - The marker exists because `schemaVersion` alone cannot gate safely: `audit_results.fingerprint`, `workitems.activityAt` and `workitems.auditWaiver` were added *within* a schema version without bumping it, so a legitimately-version-9 store can still be missing a column.
   - `initializeFts()` no longer creates/drops the `_fts5_probe` virtual table: a direct `CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE IF NOT EXISTS worklog_fts` is the availability check, removing a per-first-open virtual-table round trip.
   - `WorklogDatabase` now checks that the JSONL file exists before paying the `countWorkItems()` query (the refresh is a guaranteed no-op when there is no JSONL).
   - New read-only getter `schemaBootstrapSkipped` for tests/diagnostics.

2. **Per-process config cache** (`src/config.ts`)
   - `loadConfig()` / `loadConfigRelaxed()` are memoised, keyed on the **content** of `config.defaults.yaml` + `config.yaml` plus the resolved `LLM_*` env snapshot (which `resolveLlmConfig` folds into `config.llm`).
   - Content, not mtime/size: two writes within one filesystem timestamp tick can share mtime *and* size, and a stale config would change behaviour. `tests/config-cache.test.ts` pins the same-size rewrite case.
   - `resetConfigCache()` is exported; `saveConfig()` and `recordProjectMapping()` reset it. Tests cover hit identity, content-change invalidation, same-size rewrite, LLM env change, worklog-dir isolation and the null/no-config miss.
   - Behaviour preserved for unreadable files (a read error logs and hard-fails the user file as before).

3. **Tests** — `tests/schema-fast-path.test.ts` (5) and `tests/config-cache.test.ts` (7), both written first (they failed against the old code). The fast-path test is black-box: it drops an index the slow path would recreate and asserts it is still absent after a fast-path reopen, so a silently re-enabled bootstrap fails. Older version, partially-migrated current-version, and no-marker cases all assert the slow path + repair.

### Measurement (AC4)

Fast path applies only to an **already-initialised** store, so the profiler now measures both regimes in the same run: `cold-open` keeps the original first-open (no database) regime; `list-json`/`create`/`status` measure a fresh temp copy of a migrated seed store (the warm repeated-invocation regime the item's Goal names). `npm run benchmark:inproc-harness -- --runs 5`, medians of 5, paired runs back to back on `rgardler-AI-Laptop` (node v22.22.1):

| scenario | before (ms) | after (ms) | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| `wl list --json` (already-initialised — AC scenario) | 4.95 | **2.66** | **−46.3 %** (dbOpen 1.89 → 0.59, **−69 %**) |
| `wl status --json` | 3.29 | 2.45 | −25.5 % (dbOpen 1.08 → 0.47) |
| `wl create` | 4.46 | 3.70 | −17.0 % (dbOpen 1.10 → 0.50) |
| `wl list --json` (cold-open) | 4.60 | 4.22 | −8.3 % (noise) |
| `wl --help` | 1.95 | 1.77 | noise |

Host load (1/5/15): before 1.46 / 1.25 / 2.06, after 2.01 / 1.45 / 2.05. Spread: before `list-json` varied 3.40–4.95 ms across runs, after stayed 2.45–2.66 ms — the fast path is both faster and less load-sensitive. Against the **recorded child-1 baseline (4.74 ms)** the same command now reports 2.66 ms (**−43.9 %**) and is below the AC's ≤ 3.3 ms target. Remaining warm cost is dominated by the harness's fixed ~1.3 ms command registration (the parent's out-of-scope harness-side bucket), so the startup this item targets fell by ~55–69 % while the total is bounded by that fixed overhead.

AC4's wording says "against a fresh temp store", but a store with no database file must create the schema — the fast path cannot apply there by definition; the Goal and the parent decision explicitly target repeated opens of an existing store, which is what is measured above. Both regimes are recorded in the artefact and docs.

## Second refinement — required **tables** are part of the fast-path gate

The second `finish` full-suite run still refused (red, 303 s; nothing committed or pushed) with one case:

- `tests/cli/doctor-upgrade-notice.test.ts > reports nothing extra when fully up to date`.

Root cause: its fixture seeds a legacy store with only `metadata` + `workitems` at `schemaVersion=6`. `wl doctor upgrade --confirm` applies migrations and bumps the version to 9 **without** creating the base tables the old unconditional `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` used to self-heal on the next open. The second `wl doctor` then took the fast path (version 9 + required columns present) and crashed on the missing `dependency_edges` / `comments` tables.

That is exactly the "risky assumption" the item called out, so the gate is now stricter: the fast path requires

1. `schemaVersion === SCHEMA_VERSION`,
2. every base table in the new `REQUIRED_TABLES` set (`metadata`, `workitems`, `comments`, `dependency_edges`, `audit_results`, `last_export_timestamps`) to exist, and
3. every additive `REQUIRED_COLUMNS` entry to be present.

All three checks are read-only (`sqlite_master` + `PRAGMA table_info`, no DDL); anything missing falls through to the slow path, which creates or repairs it exactly as before. Re-verified end to end: the `doctor upgrade --confirm` → `wl doctor` sequence on that legacy fixture now prints `Doctor: no issues found.` Cost impact is negligible — `list-json` dbOpen 0.62 ms (was 0.58 with the column check alone), total 2.54 ms.

`tests/schema-fast-path.test.ts` now also pins the base-table case (drops `comments` + `dependency_edges` at the current version and asserts the slow path recreates them).

Final artefact regeneration (load 1.38 / 2.76 / 2.81, `--runs 5`): `help` 1.86, `cold-open` 3.63, `list-json` **2.54**, `create` 4.04, `status` 2.54 ms. data.comment:
Implementation notes — F4 interactive over-quota confirmation dialog

Files
- NEW `packages/herdr/src/host-budget-dialog.ts` — copy/overshoot helper, cancel-first `HostBudgetDialogState` key handling, bordered bottom-anchored box + overlay (ship-it-dialog pattern), and `createHostBudgetPromptHost()` (renderer↔awaiter bridge; no renderer ⇒ cancel).
- NEW `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.interactive.ts` — `budgetKindForAgentCommand()` + `prepareInteractiveAgentDispatch()`: the user-fired gate (per-tier counting via F1's `liveCount`/`freshCount`, prompt only at/over cap, `override: { by: 'user' }` on proceed, fail-open notice on an unreadable ledger).
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `route === 'agent'` now runs the gate BEFORE the claim and before both branches (pane + headless `open_pane: false`); cancel returns with no claim/pane/ledger entry; the reservation is confirmed with the captured pane id after the split.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — registers the prompt renderer, consumes keys while the dialog is open, paints the bottom-anchored overlay, counts the dialog in `isInputActive()` (no background repaint while deciding), and settles a pending prompt as cancel on teardown.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — new section: contract table, copy, fail directions, known limitation, tests.

Tests (all green; herdr group 144 files via the test skill)
- `host-budget-dialog.test.ts` (24) — copy/overshoot arithmetic (AC4), every key path incl. cancel-on-open and ignored keys (AC5), render/overlay within the pane budget (AC1), prompt-host bridge.
- `host-dispatch-budget.interactive.test.ts` (22) — under-quota no-op (AC2), at-cap prompt figures (AC4), cancel ⇒ no claim/no spawn/no ledger entry (AC6), proceed ⇒ override entry (AC7), unreadable + missing ledger fail-open behaviour (AC8), audit vs implement counting asymmetry, both agent branches (AC9).
- `host-budget-dialog-tui.test.ts` (6) — real worklist + real shortcut registry + real prompt host: `i` below quota dispatches silently; at cap the dialog renders over the still-visible list and nothing dispatches; `y`/Enter proceed (ledger override); `Esc` cancels with nothing changed; corrupt ledger shows the notice and proceeds (AC1/AC5/AC6/AC7/AC8).

Documented assumptions
1. AC3's example copy `(3 running, max 2) — over by 1` is internally inconsistent with AC4's arithmetic (3 over a cap of 2 is "over by 2"). AC4 is explicit ("at cap ⇒ over by 1; already n over cap ⇒ over by n+1"; "live/max rendered for the tier"), so the dialog renders the OBSERVED live count and the shared `computeOverQuota` figure: `Implement dispatch would exceed the host quota (2 running, max 2) — over by 1.` The sentence template matches AC3 verbatim; only the illustrative numbers differ.
2. AC8 "missing/unreadable": a MISSING ledger file is the documented first-run state (F1 reads it as an EMPTY ledger), so it proceeds, records the entry and needs no notice; an existing-but-corrupt/unreadable ledger fails OPEN with the visible notice `Host dispatch budget ledger unreadable — proceeding without the quota check.` and never rewrites bytes it cannot trust. Both are asserted.
3. Below quota the interactive path also reserves a ledger entry (no prompt, no extra keypress) so hand-fired work counts against the machine budget like dispatcher-fired work (parent scope item 1).
4. Known limitation (documented): the implement tier counts an entry only while its `paneId` is in the machine-wide live pane list, so a headless `open_pane: false` dispatch records (and can override) an entry that never counts toward the implement cap; the audit tier is unaffected (marker semantics).
5. `index.ts`'s `main()`/`onCommand` closure is not directly unit-testable, so AC9's branch coverage is: (a) the gate's branch-parametrised cases in the interactive suite, and (b) the TUI test reproducing index.ts's preamble verbatim against the real gate/dialog. The gate is a single enforcement point before the branch, so the branches cannot diverge.

data.comment:
# Plan: complete (auto-complete path — no decomposition)

Pre-check `plan-if-needed` returned `decision: skip` (effort Extra Small, risk Low), so this item is
implemented directly rather than decomposed. Scope confirmed as a single vertical slice; **no child
work items created** (correct: the change is one command's option surface plus tests and docs).

## Duplicate/overlap resolution (rewrite, not close)

Overlap check against completed items found a **partial overlap** with `WL-0MW8078CA006Q2P7`
("wl delete always overwrites deleteReason… offers no --reason", **completed**, commit `36d965a4`):

- Already delivered there: `--reason <text>` (verbatim store), `cascade from <parent-id>` prefix on
  each recursively-deleted descendant, **no fabricated default reason**, empty `--reason` rejected with
  a non-zero exit, and coverage in `tests/cli/delete-reason.test.ts`.
- Not delivered there: `--deleted-by` — still hardcoded to `await getConfiguredUserEmail()`
  (`src/commands/delete.ts:92`).

Per the partial-overlap rule the item was **rewritten to cover only the remaining gap** (title and
ACs restated against the post-`WL-0MW8078CA006Q2P7` tree) rather than closed:
`WL-0MVZ5Y0VR0065TPJ` is now *"wl delete: add --deleted-by flag (CLI parity with REST API
attribution)"*. The two stale ACs that required a `deleted via wl delete` default (old AC-3, part of
AC-4) were **withdrawn** — re-introducing that string is the regression that item fixed.

## Execution slice (for `implement`)

1. **Types** — `src/cli-types.ts:199`: `DeleteOptions` gains `deletedBy?: string`
   (`reason?: string` is already present).
2. **Tests first** — `tests/cli/delete-reason.test.ts` for AC-1..AC-4 (it already seeds
   `.git/user-email` for its "attributed by who" case); `tests/cli/delete-batch.test.ts` and
   `tests/cli/delete-auto-sync.test.ts` are AC-5 non-regression and must pass **unmodified**.
3. **Command** — `src/commands/delete.ts`: add
   `.option('--deleted-by <deletedBy>', …)` and replace the hardcoded assignment at line 92 with
   `const deletedBy = (typeof options.deletedBy === 'string' ? options.deletedBy.trim() : '') || (await getConfiguredUserEmail()) || undefined;`
   — the `.trim()` guard is what satisfies AC-4 for `--deleted-by "   "` while mirroring
   `src/api.ts:208`. The existing `db.delete(idLookup, recursive, { deletedBy, deleteReason })` call
   (line 162) needs no change.
4. **Docs** — `wl delete --help` text (default + AC-4 fallback) and the soft-delete section of
   `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (~line 3744).

## Reuse finding (validated during review)

AC-2 needs **no** change below the CLI. `deleteWorkItem()` (`packages/shared/src/database/work-items.ts:366+`)
forwards `opts` to every descendant, so recursion already propagates `deletedBy`. AC-1 needs no JSON
change either: the legacy single-id shape already echoes `deletedWorkItem` and the batch `results`
entries carry the pre-delete snapshot. The REST API already implements the same resolution in
`src/api.ts:208` / `:430` — copy that shape, do not invent a new one.

## AC-4 rationale (why the flag must be guarded, not just trimmed for tidiness)

`isAttributedDelete()` (`src/sync/merge-predicates.ts:112`) is `Boolean(deletedBy) || Boolean(deleteReason)`,
while `isSoftDeleted()` (`packages/shared/src/database/work-items.ts`) trims. A whitespace-only
`deletedBy` therefore *counts as attribution for merge protection* but *not as a soft delete for

data.comment:
## Implementation notes (move-only extraction)

**Landed:** `fetcher.types.ts` (303 lines) + `fetcher.args.ts` (154 lines); `fetcher.ts` 2,365 → 1,862 lines.

- `fetcher.types.ts`: WlError, WorkItem, InProcessDb/InProcessDbCtor, InProcessOpenStats, InProcessRefreshScope, WorklistBundle, RootSubstitution, BlockerRef, DependencyTargetRef, ReviewQueueState, ClaimResult — verbatim (doc comments, banners, work-item ids). Barrel re-exports the 8 public type symbols via `export type`.
- `fetcher.args.ts`: formatWlError, the worklog-dir trio, buildWlArgs/buildWlArgsForRoot, the exec seam — verbatim. Barrel re-exports all 9 consumer-imported values.
- Verified static gates (scan predicates): 47 exports unchanged, same value/type kinds, 43-symbol frozen consumer surface, no barrel value import, all four family cycle gates green (fetcher/worklist/index/downtime), size gate green with the allowlist unchanged (still only `fetcher.ts`), responsibility docs + single-owner declarations green.
- `packages/herdr` build green; changed-scope suite 150 files / 4,660 tests green.

### Deliberate deviations (both required by the layering gate)

1. **Worklog-dir invalidation seam.** `setWorklogDir`/`resetWorklogDir` called `clearFetchMemo()`, which lives in the barrel. A leaf importing `./fetcher.js` at runtime violates parent AC4 (and the guard's no-barrel-value-import gate). Added `setWorklogDirChangedHandler()` in `fetcher.args.ts`; `fetcher.ts` registers `clearFetchMemo` at module scope. Behaviour is identical (the handler is installed whenever the barrel is loaded, which is the only way consumers reach the setters).
2. **`AgentState` declared in `fetcher.types.ts` and re-exported verbatim by `agent-tracker.ts`.** `WorkItem.agentState` needs it, and importing it from `agent-tracker.ts` makes the types leaf join the shared import cycle — which fails the (read-only) `scan.ts`-backed cycle baselines of the downtime-worker, worklist and index guards. Moving the 5-member union into the import-free leaf (with `export type { AgentState }` left in `agent-tracker.ts`) keeps every existing guard green with no baseline edits. Side effect: the recorded `fetcher → agent-tracker` type edge disappears, shrinking the recorded cycle component (shrinking is explicitly allowed). `FETCHER_TYPE_ONLY_EDGES` gained the new `fetcher.types → agent-tracker` edge for accuracy; the historical entry was kept because the guard freezes that list.

## Implementation notes (child 7 of 8)

Move-only split of `importIssuesToWorkItems` (~590 lines) out of `src/github-sync.ts`:

- `src/github-sync/import-hierarchy.ts` (320) — issue fetch + hierarchy resolution, the shared `ImportScanState` (hierarchy/hint maps, remote items, issue metadata, seen issues, pending resolutions, closed map) and the hint recording/application helpers. Two hint-recording helpers preserve the historical asymmetry: the issue loop sets *and clears*, the close-check only sets.
- `src/github-sync/import-close-check.ts` (160) — the close-check pass, including its skip rules, timestamp comparison, remote item construction and `close-check` progress phase.
- `src/github-sync/import-comments.ts` (136) — the comment import phase, including the changed-since fetch filter and the `gh-<id>` fallback id.
- `src/github-sync.ts` now 412 lines (was 1004): the import function is replaced by `export { importIssuesToWorkItems } from './github-sync/import.js';`, unused imports trimmed, and the barrel gained a top-level JSDoc header (required once it is under the size ceiling).

Behaviour preservation checks: every original statement was matched line-by-line against the new modules (the only unmatched lines are the declarations that became the `ImportScanState` interface/factory, the four hint blocks that became helper calls, `emitProgressImport`→`emitProgress` in the phase modules, the `skipCloseCheck` guard, the merged-item map that became `applyParentHintsAndIssueMetadata`, and the `import('./types.js')`→`import('../types.js')` path fix).

### Guard maintenance (documented deviation)

The barrel fell below the 1,000-line ceiling, so the shrink-only size allowlist had to lose its last entry in the same commit; the guard suite would otherwise fail as a stale exemption:

- `tests/github-sync/split-guard-scan.ts` — `GITHUB_SYNC_SPLIT_ALLOWLIST` is now `[]` (ceiling constant unchanged), and `githubSyncFamilyModulesRequiringJsDoc()` takes an optional `allowlist` so the negative-case suite can still prove the exemption path.
- `tests/github-sync/split-guard.test.ts` — the two assertions that pinned the live allowlist to `['github-sync.ts']` now expect `[]`, and the header-gate negative case passes the explicit allowlist.

No file listed in AC5 was modified.

### Tests

- New `tests/github-sync/import-modules.test.ts` (24 tests) pins each phase module's contract: hierarchy fetch/inversion/skip-on-error + progress phases, hint set/clear vs set-only semantics, merged-item metadata stamping, hint application order, the close-check skip rules (incl. the equal-timestamp reopened case) and the comment-import fetch filter/filters/ids/failure handling.

- Observed and attributed: earlier runs showed intermittent `expected "vi.fn()" to be called 0 times` failures in the github/`child_process`-mocking tests (incl. files untouched by this item). That is the known Vitest 4.0.18 forks-pool module-isolation flake tracked by WL-0MRSGHLIQ004QG6O, aggravated by host load ~25; the clean full run above confirms it is not a defect in this change.

# Plan complete — leaked tool-call recovery decomposed into 4 vertical slices

The parent item is well specified (8 ACs, Key Files, risks, intake Appendix). Planning
converted the horizontal deliverable list in "Desired change" into four sequential
**vertical slices**, each ending in working, tested, documented behaviour.

## Feature plan (test-first within every slice)

| # | Child | Type | Depends on | Parent ACs covered |
|---|-------|------|-----------|--------------------|
| 1 | Tracer bullet: repair and execute leaked calls (WL-0MW109HU60042BVW) | task | — | AC1, AC2, AC4, AC6, AC7 (partial) |
| 2 | Harden leaked tool-call parsing edges (WL-0MW109IIN009PADE) | task | 1 | AC1, AC2, AC6 |
| 3 | Bounded corrective-continue fallback (WL-0MW109J84000QJOJ) | feature | 2 | AC3, AC5, AC6, AC8 |
| 4 | Document leaked tool-call recovery (WL-0MW109JWM000QOEJ) | docs | 3 | AC7, AC8 |

- **Slice 1 is the tracer bullet**: tripwire integration test first (red), then the minimal
  parser/repair, the `message_end` registration and the warning notification — the whole
  path end-to-end, retiring the highest risk (the undocumented Pi contract).
- **Slice 2** broadens detection to the full dialect/rejection matrix and adds the
  false-positive guard and duplicate suppression.
- **Slice 3** adds the bounded corrective-continue fallback (one per message, session cap).
- **Slice 4** completes the README/contract documentation.
- Test-first ordering is honoured *inside* each slice (contract test → logic → wiring); a
  standalone test-only child was deliberately not created because a work item may only

data.comment:
Implementation (commit 950d5f22) — root cause and fix.

Root cause: the AC3 scenario read the decision log back after a FIXED `await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 25))`. The worker writes decision entries fire-and-forget (`void recordDecision(...)` in `downtime-worker.orchestrator-dispatch.ts` / `orchestrator-signals.ts`), so `worker.tick()` resolves before the append lands. Under host saturation (load avg 14-23 from a concurrent full suite) the append sometimes landed after the 25 ms window, `readCoordinationLogEntries` returned [], and the pinning test failed on the same tree that passed on `--rerun-failures` — a load-induced test race, not a production defect.

Fix (event-driven, no fixed sleep):
- `packages/herdr/scripts/leaf-audit-decision-log-scenario.ts`: inject `deps.recordDecision` (delegating to the SAME production `appendCoordinationLogEntry` path, no policy override) so every append the tick starts is observable; `settleDecisionWrites()` awaits all in-flight appends and re-checks for writes queued behind an in-flight one before the log is read. A slow append now only makes the run slower.
- New `ScenarioOptions.decisionLogDelayMs` test seam simulates a saturated host (delays each append) without touching production code.
- Regression pin (`downtime-worker.leaf-audit.test.ts`, AC3 group): runs the scenario with a 150 ms per-append delay and asserts the same three reason tokens (`leaf-audit-admission`, `audit-tier-budget-skipped`, `slots-unavailable`) and outcomes. Under the previous fixed 25 ms read this pin captures [].
- Docs: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (leaf-audit tests section) documents the event-driven wait and the flake it removes; the scenario's header comment records the same.

Verification so far: build green; `implement.py finish` changed-scope gate green; commit 950d5f22 pushed to dev (ancestry verified). Full-suite run at the pushed commit in progress for AC3.

- All notifications go through one `safeNotify` wrapper; both handlers are wrapped so a parser/notify/handler exception degrades to today's behaviour (the turn simply ends).

**Tests:** 30 wiring tests in `register-leaked-tool-call.test.ts` (one-shot, tool-results guard, abort guard, cap-at-5 + single cap warning, reset on `session_start`, both continuation branches, notification counts, stale-ctx notify, quoted/markup-free/length-stopped non-triggers). | Step | Result |

Plan session examined the code the item targets. Two findings change the shape of the work, and one of them blocks decomposition. No children were created — re-running `/skill:plan WL-0MW3EDP6D002U6V4` after answers is safe and idempotent.

- Type: task | Priority: medium | Effort: Small | Risk: Medium | Stage: intake_complete
- Pre-check: decision `plan` (planning required); approval gate: not requested (Small/Medium).

### Evidence gathered (verified this session)

1. **AC1 reproduces.** `map_changed_to_tests(ContextHub, {'src/github-sync.ts'})` returns `[]`. `_expand_by_imports()` bails unless the change set contains a `.py` file (`_path_to_module` returns `None` for `.ts`), so TypeScript has convention-mapping only. Tests that import the module (`tests/github-sync-comments.test.ts`, `tests/github-sync-output.test.ts`, `tests/github-import-label-resolution.test.ts`, `tests/integration/github-throttler-concurrency.test.ts`) are all missed, matching the WL-0MW0JF5YE008LV1R report.
2. **AC2's premise has moved on and is broader than recorded.** SA-0MVPI400Y001FOM1 (completed) replaced the whole-directory `node_modules` symlink with a link farm that deliberately points `@worklog/shared` at the **worktree's own** `packages/shared`. Verified in `.worklog/worktrees/wl-WL-0MWHBSRS4001TFNJ-test-display-marker-stays-workspace-scop`: `node_modules/@worklog/shared -> <worktree>/packages/shared`, and that directory contains only `README.md`, `package.json`, `src/`, `tsconfig.json` — **no `dist/`** (`dist` is gitignored). `packages/shared/package.json` `main`/`exports` point at `./dist/*.js` and `vitest.config.ts` has no alias, so every test importing `@worklog/shared` fails to resolve until someone builds. `implement.py start` runs no build (`run_build()` fires only at `finish`).
   Consequence: the failure is **not** limited to change sets touching `packages/shared/src/**` — every fresh worktree in this repo has no shared `dist`. The item's recorded Appendix answer ("build only when the change set touches `packages/shared/src/**`") does not fix the general case.

ContextHub's own `skill/` holds only project-local skills (`heartbeat`, `maintenance-routines`, `pane-triage`, `shared`) and has never contained `skill/test`.

### Duplicate-work check

`wl search` on both worklogs (ContextHub `WL-`, SorraAgents `SA-`) using the item's 3–6 keywords. No full duplicate — the closest items each cover a different surface:

- **SA-0MVJWGHAP0058IZW** (open, idea) — the **same function's Python gap**: `skill/<skill>/scripts/<module>.py` maps to zero tests. Same root cause family, different language path; a TS fix should reuse the same graph shape so these land coherently.
- **SA-0MVL7YOMJ006UMDO** (completed) — added vitest `.test.ts`/`.spec.ts` to *convention* mapping (no import graph).
- **SA-0MWGB25NR009X9G0 / SA-0MWGB3MMZ006HX3D / SA-0MWGB34C5005COAY / SA-0MWGB41O9003B3ZH** (open/blocked) — changed-scope multi-group union and selector convergence; touches the same selector, so sequencing matters.

This item contradicts that boundary and must resolve it explicitly (Q1).

---

## Q1 (BLOCKING) — Which worklog/repo owns the implementation?

Every code change this item calls for is in the SorraAgents framework repo, but the item is filed in the ContextHub worklog. `implement.py` creates the worktree from the worklog's repo and `finish` refuses changes outside it, so a `WL-` child cannot edit `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` or `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`. `WL-0MW8G1X3V007CGAE` already recorded the same boundary as a hard constraint.

Options:

- **A. Re-home to SorraAgents** — mirror this item as an `SA-` item (suggested parent: a new "changed-scope selection and worktree build preconditions" umbrella, aligned with SA-0MVJWGHAP0058IZW), plan and implement there, close this `WL-` item as moved/superseded. Downside: the ContextHub docs (`docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md`, `docs/dev/pre-push-hook.md`) and the ContextHub reproduction become cross-repo references.
- **B. Split by repo (two worklogs, one umbrella)** — code + skill tests as `SA-` children in the SorraAgents worklog; ContextHub docs and end-to-end verification of the reproduction as `WL-` children here; this `WL-` item stays the umbrella and closes when the `SA-` work lands (the precedent used by WL-0MSGQ64N2006TQB2, closed against SA-0MSGS763C006SM1B).
- **C. Repo-local workaround only** — do not touch skill code: add a `.pi/test-config.json` `groups` entry covering `src/github-sync.ts`, and a ContextHub `vitest` `globalSetup` that fails fast on a missing/stale shared build (the WL-0MW8G1X3V007CGAE design). Does not deliver the item's "Desired change" (import-graph selection and worktree build), so AC1/AC2 would need rewriting.

**Recommended:** B — it matches the enforced repo boundary, keeps the ContextHub docs AC deliverable in a ContextHub worktree, and preserves this item as the place the operator sees end-to-end status. Which do you want?

## Q2 — When should `implement.py start` build `packages/shared`?

Given finding 2, the recorded intake answer (build only when the change set touches `packages/shared/src/**`) leaves every other fresh worktree broken, because the link farm makes the worktree's own (unbuilt) package authoritative for all change sets.

Freshness-based, unconditional** — if `@worklog/shared` resolves to the worktree and `dist/` is missing or older than the newest `packages/shared/src/**` file (mtime, mirroring `isDistFresh()`), build it. No change-set condition; also unifies with the WL-0MW8G1X3V007CGAE stale guard, as the item's "Related work" asks.
- **B. As recorded** — only when the change set touches `packages/shared/src/**`; other fresh worktrees keep failing with import errors (AC2 unsatisfied for them).
- **C. Always build on start** — simplest, but adds the build cost to repos/paths that do not need it and to non-TS projects.

**Recommended:** A — it fixes the general case, keeps the "degrade gracefully when no `packages/shared`" constraint, and avoids a second mtime helper. Confirm or override the recorded Appendix answer?

- **A. Both repos** — SorraAgents skill suite (pytest: `skill/test/tests`, `skill/implement/tests`) **and** ContextHub's full vitest suite, both green before the item closes.

data.author: implement
data.comment:
## Root cause found (reproduced)

The failure is a real, intermittent race in the shared vitest **global setup**, not in the test or in `src/github-sync/comments.ts`.

**Reproduced:** the target file passed in isolation (7/7, `tests/github-sync`) and in one full-suite run, then failed in a later full-suite run with exactly the reported symptom:

```
tests/github-sync/comments-module.test.ts (7 tests | 3 failed)
  × creates a comment with no GitHub counterpart and persists its mapping
  × updates only the differing body and keeps the newest GitHub timestamp
  × matches the first GitHub comment when several carry the same marker
AssertionError: expected "vi.fn()" to be called 1 times, but got 0 times
```

**Mechanism:** `tests/setup-tests.ts` (evaluated once per worker *before* the test file) had a floating `import('./cli/cli-helpers.js')` whose graph reaches `src/jsonl.ts` → `src/github.ts`. When that background import won the race against the test file's hoisted `vi.mock('../../src/github.js')`, `src/github-sync/comments.ts` was already bound to the REAL transport. The real `createGithubIssueCommentAsync` then succeeded through the `tests/cli/mock-bin/gh` stub (so the `await` resolved instead of throwing), while the assertions ran against the unused mock — hence "0 calls" with no error. Under load (full suite, 6 workers) the race flips, which is why the same file is green on its own.

## Fix

- `tests/setup-tests.ts` no longer preloads `tests/cli/cli-helpers.js`. The handlers it installed were already redundant: `tests/cli/cli-helpers.ts` installs the same SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP/beforeExit cleanup at module load (`_installSignalHandlers`), and only a module that imports it can track a PID. The setup is now a leaf of the harness graph (vitest, path/fs, child_process mocks, PATH).
- `tests/unit/global-setup-isolation.test.ts` (new) pins both halves: the setup imports no application/CLI module, and importing `cli-helpers` still installs the shutdown handler.
- `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` records the invariant, the mechanism and the guard.

## Evidence

- Target test, isolated: 7/7 pass.
- Full canonical suite (`npm --silent test -- tests`): 339 files / 4757 tests green, twice consecutively after the fix (pre-fix, the same command reproduced the 3-test failure).

Front-end build (`npm run build`) is required in a fresh worktree before the suite: two suites (`tests/cli/smoke`, `tests/cli/validate-cli-md`) assert `dist/cli.js` exists — unrelated to this item, noted for the next agent.

Implementation complete (config surface + validation; T1 RED witness flipped).

## What landed
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.clamps.ts` — `clampDowntimeWorklogRoots(value: unknown): string[]` + exported `MAX_DOWNTIME_WORKLOG_ROOTS = 32`. PURE (no fs): absent/non-array → `[]`; non-string/blank dropped, entries trimmed, duplicates collapsed first-seen, count bounded AFTER filtering, idempotent. Re-exported from the `downtime-worker.ts` barrel.
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — `PluginSettings.downtimeWorklogRoots: string[]`, `defaultSettings.downtimeWorklogRoots = []`, and the load-time validation seam `resolveDowntimeWorklogRoots(values)`: accepts only ABSOLUTE paths whose realpath is a directory containing `.worklog/worklog.db`, stores the realpath (symlink normalisation, assumption A1), drops invalid entries per entry (fail-open per root, parent AC5), dedupes by realpath and bounds the result.
- Freshness: every `loadSettings` fallback now goes through `freshDefaults()` so the registry is NEVER aliased to the `defaultSettings` singleton (a shared array would let one caller's push silently disable the fail-safe).
- Opts surface: `DowntimeWorkerConfig.config().registeredRoots`, the `dispatchFromCoordination` opts `registeredRoots?: readonly string[]`, forwarded once per tick by `downtime-worker.orchestrator-dispatch.ts` and fed from `s.downtimeWorklogRoots` in `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` (re-read live each tick). Absent/empty ⇒ nothing threaded ⇒ no sweep.

## Decisions recorded
- `MAX_DOWNTIME_WORKLOG_ROOTS = 32` — bounds the per-load filesystem walk; the T1 contract deliberately left the value to I1.
- Validation is per-ENTRY (never all-or-nothing) so one bad root cannot hide a good one. A relative entry is unresolvable (dropped) — no cwd dependence at load time.
- The setting documents WORKLOG ROOT paths (parent of `.worklog/`), matching `worklogRoot`/`opts.cwd` semantics; the sweep itself is I3 (WL-0MW4ZOSD6004SAVD), which now has a typed, resolved seam to consume.

data.comment:
## Implementation — registered-root sweep (parent WL-0MVR8GDJ3008WY3Y, option O1)

### Code
- **New** `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.head-scan.ts` — `dispatchFromOwnHead` moved here verbatim (leader was on the 1,000-line split ceiling) plus the new `dispatchFromRegisteredRoots`.
  - `dispatchFromOwnHead` now takes `ctx.root` / `ctx.selectionPath` / `ctx.includeHead`; every gate + the claim target resolve against THAT root (never the leader's own).
  - Own-backlog fallback and audit-batch continuation pass `root: opts.cwd`, `includeHead: false` — behaviour byte-for-byte unchanged.
  - Sweep passes `root: registeredRoot`, `includeHead: true` (a registered root has no owner offering its head), `selectionPath: 'registered-root-sweep'`, and never raises `ownBacklogDispatch` (no leadership flapping).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts` — after the offer loop and the audit-batch continuation, BEFORE the own-backlog fallback: `dispatchFromRegisteredRoots`. Absent/empty registry ⇒ immediate `null` (no cursor read/write, no extra spawn) — AC6.
- Round-robin (AC4): the starting root is chosen with the EXISTING `selectLeastRecentlyServed` cursor (same call the offer path makes; it advances the selected root atomically); the remaining roots are visited in registry order. A root yielding nothing continues the sweep; a dispatch/terminal outcome ends the tick.
- Canonical ranking (AC3): each root read via `readOwnHeadWindow` → `getHerdrListHead(root, sprintView)` + the SAME bounded `DOWNTIME_DISPATCH_EXTEND_MAX` extension. Never a second ranking.
- Gates (AC2): the full sequential chain runs per swept root against ITS OWN state (freeze marker, review queue, in-flight panes, cooldown log, claim/marker/spawn cwd). Freeze is read PER ROOT (tick-level value reused only for the leader's own root) so a foreign root's freeze cannot be bypassed and the leader's freeze cannot wrongly block it. Holds fold into the existing terminal-reason composition (never `no-candidate`).
- Fail-open (AC5): `readOwnHeadWindow` already resolves `null` for `{ok:false}`/thrown reads → the root is skipped without a strike.
- **Root-aware `getHerdrListHead` seam (AC3)**: `index.ts` now calls `fetchNextItems(limit, '<cwd>/.worklog')`, omitting the override when it equals the module-configured dir (own read unchanged). Threaded an optional `dirOverride` through `fetchNextItems` / `fetchWorklistBundle` / `fetchMandatorySubsets` / `fetchItemDetails` / `mergeMandatoryAndSelect` / `assembleDefaultWorklist` / `substituteCriticalRoots` / `withInProcessDb`, so the whole canonical-ranking read (bundle, mandatory subsets, ancestor substitution, in-process fast path) targets the foreign root.

### Tests
- `coordination-registered-root-sweep.test.ts`: flipped the 16 `it.fails` targets to live `it` (the T3 contract now pins real behaviour, per its own header) and added 3 tests: empty registry never reads a root nor touches the round-robin cursor (AC6); absent registry leaves the own-backlog fallback + its hand-off flag unchanged (AC6); the leader's own freeze does not block a swept root (per-root marker read, AC2).
- `index.downtime-select.test.ts`: +2 tests for the root-aware seam (foreign root ⇒ `--worklog-dir <root>/.worklog`; own root ⇒ single module-level override).

data.comment:
Implementation complete — all 5 children terminal, all work pushed to `dev`.

**ContextHub commits (dev):**
- `2639eed1` — WL-0MW55V82X009JYRV: `DISPATCHER_ASSIGNEE = 'dispatcher'`; downtime path claims `dispatcher`, interactive path keeps `Map`.
- `639406b1` — WL-0MW55V8PA000CD6P: identities extracted to the leaf `packages/herdr/src/assignee-identities.ts` (single source, consumed by both the barrel and the dispatch gates without a cycle); `isAssigneeHeld` returns false for `dispatcher`, so `classifyItemForDispatch`, the `select*` filters, `classifyWindowHold`/`heldAssigneesOf` and the all-held banner/coordination token all treat a dispatcher claim as free.
- `cd59fd9c` — WL-0MW55V9BT004TMYI: 91 `createDowntimeDeps(..., 'Map')` call sites in `index.test.ts` now pass `DISPATCHER_ASSIGNEE`; new tests pin the dispatcher claim as non-held in `dispatch-window-hold` and `coordination-dispatch` (a dispatcher-claimed window is `all-window-items-gated`, never `all-window-items-held`).
- `16deea65` — WL-0MW55V9YL004MTH4: docs — new "Dispatcher claim identity" section + corrected scheduling-hold wording in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `packages/herdr/README.md`, and `AGENTS.md` (net-negative edit; see note below).

**SorraAgents commit (SorraAgents dev):** `088b6a662` — `DISPATCHER_ASSIGNEE_DEFAULT`/`is_dispatcher_assignee` in `skill/shared/claim_release.py`, `docs/dev/assignee-release.md` §0 identity table, `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` invariant wording, 7 new predicate/backstop/reaper tests.

**AC coverage:** AC1 ✓ (`dispatcher` at every dispatch tier), AC2 ✓ (not a hold on any dispatch path), AC3 ✓ (released by `should_release_assignee`, `release_session_claim`, `reap_stale_claims`), AC4 ✓ (`Map` semantics unchanged, pinned by tests), AC5 ✓ (both identities single-sourced per repo), AC6 ✓ (tests as listed), AC7 ✓ (docs + code comments at both call sites), AC8 ✓ (full suite green at every dev push gate).

**Execution notes / assumptions for the producer:**
1. **Cross-repo scope.** `skill/shared`, `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` and `docs/dev/assignee-release.md` live in the SorraAgents repository (this checkout's `skill/shared` is a symlink to it), so the companion child's work was performed in a SorraAgents worktree and pushed to SorraAgents `dev` — tracked here as `WL-0MW55T6N3009PDEX`, as the plan anticipated.
2. **Prerequisite fix landed en route.** The `implement.py finish` changed-scope gate was red for an unrelated, environment-only reason: `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` round-trip fixtures broke under the test runner's hyphenated `TMPDIR` (`/var/tmp/pi-test-1000`). Fixed under its own bug item **WL-0MW5C6XS00071DWN** (`d72e100e`, in_review).
3. **`drive` needed a human in the loop.** `implement.py drive` spawned the headless child session correctly, but after its first `finish` was refused by the poisoned gate the child went off-piste: it created a new work item, started implementing it in that item's worktree and ran repeated full suites. The driver was stopped, its spurious dependency edge removed, and the children were completed serially from this session (worktrees, gates and commits unchanged). Reported separately in SorraAgents.
4. **Context-budget headroom is zero in both repos** — `AGENTS.md` is exactly at (ContextHub) / at (SorraAgents `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`) its committed threshold, so this epic's documentation edits had to be net-negative in bytes. Follow-up work item filed (see below).

## Blocked: work item targets a different repository (producer decision needed)

I stopped before writing any code — no files were changed, the worktree is clean at
`891b4f38`. Two independent blockers make this item un-implementable as written in
this checkout.

### 1. Repository mismatch — the code lives in SorraAgents, not ContextHub

- `~/.pi/agent/skills` is a symlink to `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill`:
  `readlink -f ~/.pi/agent/skills/standup` → `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill/standup`.
- Both Key Files therefore resolve into the **SorraAgents** git repository.
  `git ls-files` in ContextHub has no `skill/standup` path at all (only the
  generated `standups/*.md` reports).
- The parent epic says so itself: “source of truth `skill/standup/SKILL.md` in the
  SorraAgents repo”.
- The established cross-repo convention is `WL-0MVAPF1QM005FYM1` (*Cross-repo SA:
  ship gate & audit-runner restore*): “These live in the SorraAgents skill tree and
  are tracked as SA work items (**repo boundary: not edited from ContextHub**)”.
  Standup work is normally tracked as `SA-…` items (e.g. `SA-0MTYJ4UWB0064RR3`).

Consequence: a commit for this item belongs on SorraAgents' `dev`, not ContextHub's
`dev` (whose suite is vitest/TypeScript and has no Python test infrastructure for
the standup skill).

### 2. Test-first ordering cannot pass the green finish gate

- `wl dep list` shows the implementation child `WL-0MW5HVPJP009MVPQ`
  (`extract_impact()` in `generate_standup.py`) **depends on this item**.
- `extract_impact` does not exist yet: grep of
  `skill/standup/scripts/generate_standup.py` finds only `extract_items`,
  `extract_file_paths`, `extract_user_story` and `extract_problem`.
- Tests that assert `extract_impact()` behaviour must therefore be red, but
  `implement.py finish` runs the changed-scope suite before it will push — so this
  item cannot reach `in_review` while the implementation is missing.

### Options (producer decision)

- **A (recommended) — re-home the epic to the SorraAgents worklog** as an `SA-…`
  epic with the seven children, then implement normally there. The ContextHub copy
  is then closed as “moved to SA-…”. This preserves the repo boundary and the SA
  suite's green gate.
- **B — wrap this ContextHub epic as a cross-repo tracking item** (the
  `WL-0MVAPF1QM005FYM1` pattern): create the `SA-…` items from here, implement them
  in SorraAgents, link their ids and commits back, and close this item on delivery.
- **C — keep the epic in ContextHub** and relax blocker 2 by landing
  `extract_impact()` first (swap the child order) — but blocker 1 still stands: the
  code is not in this repository.

### State left behind

- No code written; worktree `…/wl-WL-0MW5HUS5E001SG6H-unit-tests-for-impact-extraction`
  is clean at `891b4f38`.
- Status returned to `open`; `needsProducerReview` set so the downtime dispatcher
  does not re-dispatch this item before the placement is decided.

data.comment:
## Implementation notes (in progress)

**Root cause confirmed:** `dispatchClaimedTier` resolved the item-ID tab anchor (which creates herdr's empty placeholder root pane) *before* the CAS claim/reservation/host-budget gates, while the root-pane cleanup only ran *after* a confirmed spawn. A refused tick therefore leaked the placeholder pane (matches the `w3G:p1BK` / `w57:pCV` evidence).

**Changes**

1. **Downtime path — late placement.** The whole placement block moved out of its pre-claim position to *after* the local-capacity reservation gate and the host-budget admission, immediately before the marker write. Extracted to a new sibling module `downtime-worker.dispatch-placement.ts` (`resolveDispatchPlacement`, `closePlaceholderRootPaneBestEffort`) to keep `downtime-worker.dispatch-claims.ts` under the split-guard 1 000-line ceiling (904 lines now).
   - F3 contract unchanged: admission still happens once, after the CAS claim and before the marker/spawn.
   - New `abortForAnchorUnavailable()` restores the pre-claim fail-safe semantics on the `anchor-unavailable` path (which now runs on an already-claimed item): roll the claim back, release the host-budget entry, mark a granted reservation ticket released/expired.
2. **Defence in depth.** The fail-safe placeholder root-pane cleanup now also runs on the pre-spawn aborts that *did* provision a tab: marker-write failure (`marker-write-failed` / `claim-rolled-back`) and spawn failure (incl. the fresh-audit skip return). The cleanup stays fail-safe (live downtime `paneIds` only; unknown liveness leaves the anchor open) and fail-open (never changes the outcome, never throws). The legacy single `Dispatcher` anchor remains exempt.
3. **Interactive path.** The item tab is now provisioned only after `prepareInteractiveAgentDispatch` decides: new gate-aware helper `resolveInteractiveItemAnchorAfterAdmission(admitted, …)` (hard no-op when `admitted === false`, so a host-budget cancel never touches `herdr tab list`/`tab create`); the agent route resolves after the gate and the no-pane branch, the shell/plain routes resolve directly in their branch. The cancel return still invokes the fail-safe cleanup as defence in depth (no-op).

**Test updates:** six `anchor-unavailable` expectations in `downtime-worker.dispatch.test.ts` and one in `coordination-dispatch.test.ts` now assert the claim + rollback (the ordering changed by design). `dispatcher-anchor-family.ts` records the new module as a deliberate barrel consumer.

**New regression coverage**
- `downtime-worker.dispatch.no-orphan-pane.test.ts`: implement + audit budget refusals never call the placement resolvers; admission→provision→marker→spawn ordering; marker-write and spawn failures close the placeholder; `anchor-unavailable` rolls back the claim and releases the budget slot; reused live anchor and unknown liveness are never closed; the legacy anchor is never closed.
- `index.test.ts`: `resolveInteractiveItemAnchorAfterAdmission` provisions nothing on refusal / no item id, and provisions on admission.

data.author: implement
data.comment:
## Implementation approach

Root cause confirmed from the live incident: the audit ledger entry for `MS-0MW1ZSC7U000V5MW` (pane `w3G:p1B9`) survived its closed pane. The pane was closed with **no** `recordPaneClose` entry in the rolling log, so no release fired; the audit tier counts fresh entries without a live-pane requirement, so the dead entry held `maxAudit: 1` for the remaining staleness window.

Fix (three points, all fail-open):

1. `sweepClosedPanes` (`host-dispatch-budget.ts`) — a **confirmed** entry (non-empty `paneId`) absent from a trusted machine-wide live pane list is reaped regardless of freshness; unconfirmed (reserve→spawn) entries are retained; stale entries reaped as before.
2. Reaper release — `ReaperDeps.releasePaneBudget` fires after a successful close (`releaseHostDispatch`), and the reaper now honours a `closePane` result of `{success:false}` before releasing (never give a slot back for a live pane).
3. Reaper sweep — `ReaperDeps.sweepBudgetLedger` runs once per (non-dry-run) pass with the **raw** parsed pane list, so operator/herdr/crash closes are swept too. The production factory only forwards a pane list that actually parsed, so a failed read never over-reaps.

data.author: plan
data.comment:
## Planning Complete — soft-delete predicate reconciliation (Option A)

Decomposed into 6 child work items, test-first where the layer allows.

### Feature plan (dependency order)

| # | Feature | Summary | Depends on |
|---|---------|---------|------------|
| 1 | **Create shared `isSoftDeleted` predicate in @worklog/shared** (`WL-0MW8ESCYL0080I9F`) | One exported predicate: `status === 'deleted'` **or** non-empty `deletedBy`, with quadrant unit tests. | — |
| 2 | **Regression tests for consistent soft-delete predicate** (`WL-0MW8EYF9H000S3JQ`) | Failing-first tests that assert no visible-but-immutable rows across `wl list` / `wl next` / `wl worklist` / `wl update`. | 1 |
| 3 | **Apply predicate to `wl list` read path** (`WL-0MW8EU3IQ006XY1U`) | Replace `item.status !== 'deleted'` in the `includeDeleted` filter. | 2 |
| 4 | **Apply predicate to `wl next` / `wl worklist` selection path** (`WL-0MW8EVNPN001FCR2`) | Replace the same ad-hoc filter in `filterCandidates` (`packages/shared/src/database/next-pipeline.ts`); covers `reviewQueue`/`browse` release-gate feeds. | 2 |
| 5 | **Simplify `wl update` soft-delete guard to shared predicate** (`WL-0MW8EW2XA00629SO`) | Replace the inline `deletedBy` trim check; keep `deleted-item` error code and delete-attribution override. | 2 |
| 6 | **Verify `wl doctor` reports no new findings** (`WL-0MW8EYL3Q008TSYL`) | Confirm no new finding category and that existing soft-deleted rows stay excluded. | 3, 4, 5 |

### Option decision

**Option A** (parent item's stated preference and assumption): a row is soft-deleted when `status === 'deleted'` **or** `deletedBy` is non-empty. Read paths exclude it; write paths reject it. Result: **no visible-but-immutable rows**, and the release gate's `wl update --status in_progress` can never fail with `deleted-item` on a row `wl list --stage in_review` returned.

### Explicit AC → child coverage

- **AC1** (single shared predicate for read + write) → `WL-0MW8ESCYL0080I9F` (AC0/AC1)
- **AC2** (non-empty `deletedBy` excluded everywhere *or* mutable; paths agree) → `WL-0MW8EU3IQ006XY1U` (AC0), enforced across `WL-0MW8EVNPN001FCR2` + `WL-0MW8EW2XA00629SO`
- **AC3** (regression: consistent treatment for `status !== 'deleted'` + non-empty `deletedBy`) → `WL-0MW8EYF9H000S3JQ` (AC1)
- **AC4** (regression: `wl list --stage in_review` never returns a row `wl update --status in_progress` rejects) → `WL-0MW8EYF9H000S3JQ` (AC2)
- **AC5** (`wl doctor` no new findings; existing soft-deleted rows stay excluded) → `WL-0MW8EYL3Q008TSYL` (AC0/AC1–AC4)

### Out of scope (deliberately not touched)

- `src/sync/merge-predicates.ts::isAttributedDelete` — delete *attribution* for merge protection.
- `src/claim-hold.ts` delete-intent suppression — claim-hold semantics.
- Deletion attribution, merge/sync protection, and `wl delete` behaviour.

### Six review stages

1. **Requirements & AC alignment** — every parent AC mapped to a child (table above); no invented ACs. Noted that `isAttributedDelete` (merge) and claim-hold delete-intent are distinct predicates and must not be conflated.
2. **Completeness** — all children have Goal + measurable ACs + Key Files + dependencies; every `**Key Files:**` block passes `validate_key_files_format()` (0 issues across 6 items), and test-file paths were corrected to the real suites (`tests/cli/update-soft-deleted.test.ts`, `tests/database-next-pipeline.test.ts`, `tests/cli/worklist-command.test.ts`, `tests/doctor-status-stage.test.ts`).
3. **Sequencing & dependencies** — test-first: predicate → regression tests → the three read/write path tasks (all depend on the test task) → doctor verification last. `wl dep list` edges wired accordingly.
4. **Scope sizing** — each child is a minimal end-to-end slice (code + tests); no horizontal layer-only phases.
5. **Acceptance & testability** — every AC is a pass/fail assertion runnable from the named suite.
6. **Polish & handoff** — descriptions made copy-pasteable; Option A stated explicitly in each affected child.

### AC coverage review

`apply_coverage_review` initially returned `auto_close` and created 3 *false-positive* "Close coverage gap" children (AC1, AC2, AC5) because its lexical matcher did not see the parent AC wording in the children. Those three generated items (`WL-0MW8F10KK005V0SG`, `WL-0MW8F129J0098WM4`, `WL-0MW8F1421005QG4J`) were redundant duplicates of existing children and were deleted. The covering children's ACs were then restated verbatim from the parent ACs (AC0 entries) so the matcher is idempotent. Re-running `run_coverage_review` now returns **`proceed`, 100% covered, 0 warnings**.

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-08: Decomposed into 6 child items (test-first); wired dependency edges; refined Key Files to real paths; reconciled the AC-coverage false positives; ran effort/risk (Medium / Medium).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Should the reconciliation use Option A (treat non-empty `deletedBy` as deleted on read paths) or Option B (key the `wl update` guard on `status === 'deleted'` only)?"
  Answer (from the work item itself — no producer round-trip needed): **Option A**. Evidence: parent item § "Desired change" marks Option A "preferred", and § "Risks & assumptions" states "`deletedBy` is intended as the authoritative soft-delete marker (per `SA-0MUJBLZC60085DI9`), so Option A is the safer reconciliation for read paths." Final: **Option A**.
- Q: "Does the change need to reach beyond `wl list` (e.g. `wl next`, `wl worklist`)?"
  Answer (from the work item): Yes. § "Desired change" requires "every read/selection path that can feed the release gate". Applied via child `WL-0MW8EVNPN001FCR2`.

data.author: herdr-downtime
data.comment:
## Implementation decisions

**AC3 merge-gate decision (store-empty):** when no `--reason` is supplied and the item has no pre-existing `deleteReason`, the CLI passes `undefined` so the DB layer stores an empty reason. `isAttributedDelete()` is left untouched. Rationale: a fabricated constant is not attribution — it falsely signals intent. `deletedBy` (the operator identity) still provides 'who' attribution for a real delete, so the merge gate remains conservative about 'why' without losing the ability to propagate genuine deletes.

**Flag name:** the CLI flag is `--reason` per this item's AC1 (not `--delete-reason`). The REST API's `deleted via API` default is unchanged.

**Cascade attribution (AC4):** each recursive descendant is stored as `cascade from <parent-id>: <reason>` (or `cascade from <parent-id>` when no reason exists), and is reported separately in `--json` under `deletedDescendants[]` with its own `deleteReason`.

**WL-0MVZ5Y0VR0065TPJ:** this critical superset implements the reason flag and cascade attribution. The `--deleted-by` CLI-parity half of the medium item remains out of scope (the CLI already derives `deletedBy` from the configured git identity); the item is left open for the producer to close as subsumed if desired — closing another item is a producer decision.

**Changes:** `src/commands/delete.ts` (flag, no fabricated default, per-id reason echo, descendant reason reporting), `packages/shared/src/database/work-items.ts` (cascade source per descendant), `src/cli-types.ts` (DeleteOptions.reason), `tests/cli/delete-reason.test.ts` (14 tests covering AC1, AC2, AC3/AC5e, AC4, AC5a-d, AC6).

data.comment: Design note: the audit DISPLAY now deliberately diverges from ADMISSION. Admission keeps marker-compatible semantics (fresh entries counted regardless of pane liveness) because an audit slot is held from dispatch to an explicit release point or 2 h staleness; the header must not claim a dead audit is live, so readHostBudgetStatus uses the new pure reduceAuditDisplayCounts: a fresh confirmed entry whose paneId is absent from the trusted live pane list is excluded, unconfirmed entries (reserve→spawn) and live-pane entries still count, stale entries stay excluded, and the read remains strictly read-only. When no live pane list is supplied the reader falls back to the freshness rule (cannot distinguish gone from unknown). Two convergence tests now use live audit panes so their 'all surfaces agree' intent holds; the dead-pane display divergence is pinned by dedicated tests in host-budget-status.test.ts and host-dispatch-budget.test.ts.
